text:
Real estate advertising is no walk in the park. You’ve got the listings, the staging, the open houses — and then there’s the marketing. Even the slightest misstep can mean the difference between selling a property or letting it languish on the market. The truth is that the stakes are high in real estate advertising. You’re not just selling a home; you’re selling a dream, a lifestyle, and an investment all rolled into one.
But let’s face it — mistakes happen. And in a competitive field like real estate, even the pros sometimes stumble. From poorly written copy to low-quality photos, these errors can turn off potential buyers faster than you can say “price reduction.” So, what are the most common real estate advertising mistakes you should steer clear of?
Let’s dive into the top real estate advertising pitfalls and, more importantly, how to avoid them.
## Common Real Estate Advertising Mistakes and How to Fix Them
## 1. Overlooking the Potential of Video Prospecting
In the age of personalized marketing, skipping video prospecting in your real estate advertising is a mistake you can’t afford to make. Buyers crave connection, and there’s no better way to build trust and showcase a property’s charm than through a dynamic, engaging video.
Why It Matters AI videos breathe life into your listings. They allow buyers to visualize themselves in the space and make your outreach efforts feel more personal. Effectively curating your video prospecting scripts also sets you apart in a crowded market where static images and text dominate.
Video prospecting is no longer a “nice-to-have” — it’s a necessity in real estate advertising. AI sales tools like Potion allow realtors to create personalized videos effortlessly. Imagine addressing each potential buyer by name, showcasing the property’s best features, and delivering a unique experience — all in one video. Best part? You have the choice to generate these videos instead of recording them. Yes, simply input your script and seamlessly generate full-length custom AI videos, with your own face, voice and gestures.
By automating the process while retaining a human touch, AI real estate tools like Potion ensure that your AI video outreach feels genuine and impactful.
What Goes Wrong?
- Skipping Video Altogether: Relying solely on photos and descriptions can make your listings feel flat and impersonal.
- Generic Content: Using cookie-cutter real estate email templates that lack personalization fails to capture attention.
- Poor Execution: Grainy footage, bad lighting, or shaky camera work can turn off potential buyers.
How to Fix It
- Invest in Quality Equipment or Professionals: Crisp, high-definition videos with good lighting make a world of difference.
- Add a Personal Touch: Include a short introduction where you address buyers directly and highlight the property’s key features.
- Show, Don’t Tell: Use video storytelling to showcase the flow of the home, its unique features, and the surrounding neighborhood.
Example of Effective AI Video Prospecting Imagine receiving a personalized AI video message: “Hi [Prospect’s-Name], I know you’re looking for a home with a large backyard for your kids. Check out this one — there’s even space for a swing set and a garden! I’d love to schedule a tour to show you around.”
This type of tailored message grabs attention and fosters a deeper connection with the buyer. Searching for inspiration? Here are a few video prospecting examples you could use for your next campaign.
Pro Tip: Use video prospecting tools like Potion to automate personalized video marketing for prospects. It’s a game-changer for scaling your AI video outreach while keeping it personal.
## 2. Skimping on Quality Visuals
Ever heard the phrase, “A picture is worth a thousand words”? In real estate, a picture could be worth thousands of dollars! Yet, one of the most common realtor advertising mistakes is skimping on quality visuals.
Why It Matters When buyers scroll through listings online, photos are often the first thing they notice. Grainy, poorly lit, or unflattering images can instantly deter interest. Think about it — would you be drawn to a house that looks dark and cramped in its photos? Probably not.
What Goes Wrong?
- Using Smartphone Photos: While phone cameras have come a long way, they often lack the sharpness and depth professional cameras provide.
- Ignoring Staging: A cluttered or unkempt room in a photo screams neglect.
- Skipping Editing: Even great photos need a little tweaking for lighting and color balance.
How to Fix It
- Invest in a Professional Photographer: Trust the experts to highlight a property’s best features.
- Stage Before Shooting: Declutter, clean, and arrange furniture to create an inviting atmosphere.
- Edit Like a Pro: Use editing software to enhance photos, but don’t overdo it — buyers want authenticity.
Pro Tip: Use drone photography to showcase large properties, unique layouts, or impressive landscapes. It’s a small investment that can yield big returns!
## 3. Writing Generic or Vague Property Descriptions
Another big property advertisement mistake? Bland, cookie-cutter copy that leaves buyers scratching their heads.
Why It Matters Your property description isn’t just filler text — it’s your chance to captivate buyers and set the stage for a showing. A vague or uninspired description can make even the most beautiful home seem unremarkable.
What Goes Wrong?
- Overused Phrases: If every home is described as “cozy” or “spacious,” the words lose meaning.
- Lack of Detail: Phrases like “beautiful kitchen” or “great backyard” don’t paint a vivid picture.
- Typos or Grammatical Errors: Sloppy writing makes you seem unprofessional.
How to Fix It
- Highlight Unique Features: Does the home have a chef’s kitchen? A sun-drenched reading nook? Call it out!
- Be Specific: Instead of “large backyard,” say “a 500-square-foot backyard perfect for entertaining.”
- Proofread Twice: Ensure your copy is polished and error-free.
- Complement With Video: The written word is powerful, but pairing it with AI personalized videos takes engagement to the next level. With AI email marketing tools like Potion, you can supplement compelling property descriptions with dynamic, tailored videos that bring the listing to life.
Example: Instead of “Spacious 3-bedroom home in a great neighborhood,” try: “This 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom home in Maplewood boasts a newly renovated kitchen, a sunlit living room with vaulted ceilings, and a backyard oasis complete with a pergola and koi pond.”
## 4. Neglecting Targeted Advertising
It’s not enough to throw an ad online and hope for the best. One of the most overlooked real estate advertising mistakes is failing to tailor your marketing to your audience.
Why It Matters In the digital age, buyers expect personalized experiences. Casting a wide net might get your ad in front of more people, but you're wasting time and money if they’re not the right people.
What Goes Wrong?
- Ignoring Demographics: Marketing a luxury home to first-time buyers? That’s a mismatch.
- Skipping Social Media Ads: Relying solely on MLS listings means you’re missing out on platforms like Facebook and Instagram.
- Failing to Track Performance: Without data, you don’t know what’s working and what’s not.
How to Fix It
- Define Your Audience: Are you targeting young professionals, growing families, or retirees? Tailor your messaging accordingly.
- Leverage Social Media: Use platforms like Instagram for visual-heavy campaigns and Facebook for targeted ads.
- Monitor Metrics: Tools like Google Analytics can help you refine your strategy based on performance.
Pro Tip: Experiment with geo-targeted ads to reach buyers in specific locations who might be looking to relocate to your area.
## 5. Ignoring Mobile Optimization
In today’s world, where people are glued to their smartphones, neglecting mobile optimization is one of the most critical real estate advertising mistakes you can make.
Why It Matters A majority of homebuyers browse listings on their phones. If your ad doesn’t look great — or worse, doesn’t function properly — on a mobile device, you’re essentially slamming the door on potential leads.
What Goes Wrong?
- Clunky Website Design: A slow, hard-to-navigate website will have users hitting the back button in seconds.
- Unreadable Content: Tiny fonts or poorly formatted text on mobile screens can drive users away.
- Broken Links or Features: If the “Contact Us” button doesn’t work or images fail to load, you’re losing trust — and business.
How to Fix It
- Go Responsive: Use responsive web design to ensure your site and ads adapt seamlessly to all screen sizes.
- Test, Test, Test: Check your ads, website, and landing pages on multiple devices to catch any issues.
- Prioritize Speed: Compress images and eliminate unnecessary code to improve load times.
Pro Tip: SEOMator’s Mobile-Friendly Test tool is a lifesaver for assessing your site’s mobile readiness.
## 6. Overpricing the Property in Ads
Let’s be real — price is a make-or-break factor for most buyers. Listing a property at an unrealistically high price is one of the biggest realtor advertising mistakes that can scare off potential buyers before they even take a look.
Why It Matters Overpricing decreases interest and can lead to longer days on the market. The longer a property sits unsold, the more buyers assume something’s wrong with it, which can force price cuts later on.
What Goes Wrong?
- Ignoring Market Trends: Failing to research comparable properties can lead to inflated pricing.
- Seller Pressure: Some sellers insist on setting the price too high, which can backfire.
- Lack of Transparency: Ads without clear pricing often leave buyers frustrated and disinterested.
How to Fix It
- Do a Competitive Analysis: Research similar properties in the area to set a competitive price.
- Educate Sellers: Explain the risks of overpricing and the benefits of starting at a fair market value.
- Be Upfront: Clearly display the price in your ads to build trust and attract serious inquiries.
Example: Instead of advertising a property as “Priced to Sell” without specifics, list it as: “Beautiful 4-bedroom home in Pine Ridge — just $450,000, the best value in the neighborhood!”
## 7. Neglecting to Use Video Marketing
If you’re skipping video marketing, you’re leaving money on the table. This is one of the most overlooked property advertisement mistakes in today’s highly visual, content-driven market.
Why It Matters Videos grab attention, showcase properties in a dynamic way, and give buyers a better sense of the home’s layout and ambiance. In fact, listings with videos get 403% more inquiries than those without!
What Goes Wrong?
- Relying Solely on Photos: Static images can’t capture the flow of a property like a walkthrough video can.
- Ignoring Storytelling: A video that’s just a slideshow of photos won’t engage buyers as effectively as a guided tour.
- Poor Quality: Grainy or shaky videos can do more harm than good.
How to Fix It
- Invest in Professional Videography: A polished, well-lit walkthrough video speaks volumes.
- Incorporate Drone Footage: Use drones to showcase large properties, unique landscapes, or desirable surroundings.
- Add Narration or Captions: Highlight key features as viewers virtually “tour” the property.
- Add a Personal Touch: By leveraging Potion’s personal AI avatars, you can produce polished, engaging videos that elevate your marketing efforts without ever stepping in front of the camera. Simmply add your script and Potion’s AI will generate full-length videos in showcasing your face, gestures & voice.
Pro Tip: Use platforms like YouTube or Instagram to share your videos and expand your real estate business.
## 8. Overloading Ads with Technical Jargon
Ever come across a property ad that felt more like reading a legal document than an invitation to tour your dream home? That’s what happens when you overuse technical jargon, one of the sneakiest real estate advertising mistakes.
Why It Matters Homebuyers want to feel connected to the property, not struggle to decode terms like “egress windows” or “double-hung sash.” Overly technical language can alienate potential buyers who may not be familiar with real estate lingo.
What Goes Wrong?
- Unrelatable Language: Ads packed with terms like “encumbrances” or “cap rate” fail to resonate with most buyers.
- Lost Emotional Appeal: Technical descriptions often lack the warmth buyers are looking for.
- Miscommunication: Buyers might misunderstand terms, leading to confusion or false expectations.
How to Fix It
- Speak Their Language: Focus on benefits rather than technicalities. For example, instead of saying “energy-efficient double-glazed windows,” say “windows that keep your home cozy in winter and cool in summer.”
- Balance Jargon with Simplicity: If technical terms are necessary, explain them briefly.
- Use Storytelling: Paint a picture of what it’s like to live in the home rather than focusing solely on specs.
Pro Tip: Test your ad copy by asking a friend outside the real estate industry if it’s clear and engaging. If it sounds confusing to them, rewrite it!
## 9. Overlooking Local Market Trends
Ignoring local market dynamics is one of the most damaging realtor advertising mistakes — and it’s more common than you’d think.
Why It Matters Real estate is all about location, location, location. Ads that fail to reflect local market trends risk attracting the wrong audience — or worse, none at all.
What Goes Wrong?
- Mismatched Messaging: Advertising a home as a “fixer-upper” in a luxury-driven market can backfire.
- Ignoring Seasonality: Running summer-focused ads in the middle of winter feels tone-deaf.
- Failure to Highlight Local Perks: Skipping mentions of nearby schools, parks, or attractions undervalues the property.
How to Fix It
- Research the Market: Study local trends to understand what buyers are looking for in your area.
- Tailor the Message: Emphasize features that resonate with local buyers — like energy-efficient homes in colder regions or outdoor amenities in sunny locales.
- Highlight Neighborhood Benefits: Call out the walkability, dining options, or access to public transit.
Example: Instead of “Great family home,” say, “Located just steps from Lincoln Park and top-rated schools, this home offers the perfect setting for growing families.”
## 10. Failing to Include a Clear Call-to-Action (CTA)
A beautiful ad with no clear next step is like a GPS without directions — it leaves potential buyers lost and frustrated. One of the simplest yet most overlooked property advertisement mistakes is failing to include a compelling call-to-action.
Why It Matters Your ad is the starting point of a buyer’s journey. Without a clear CTA, you’re relying on buyers to figure out their next move, which rarely works in your favor.
What Goes Wrong?
- Unclear Instructions: Ads that end with vague phrases like “Call for more details” lack urgency.
- No Contact Information: Forgetting to include an email, phone number, or website makes it hard for buyers to reach you.
- Missed Opportunities: Without a CTA, you’re leaving potential leads hanging.
How to Fix It
- Be Specific: Tell buyers exactly what to do next, such as “Schedule a tour today!” or “Click to view more photos.”
- Create Urgency: Add phrases like “Limited showings available” or “Offer expires soon.”
- Make Contact Easy: Include clickable links, buttons, and multiple contact options.
Pro Tip: Use action-oriented words like “Discover,” “Explore,” or “Book” to make your CTA more engaging.
## 11. Using Outdated Marketing Channels
Sticking to the same old advertising methods might feel safe, but it’s a surefire way to fall behind. One of the biggest real estate advertising mistakes is relying solely on outdated marketing channels while ignoring newer, more effective ones.
Why It Matters The way people search for homes has changed dramatically. You're missing out on a massive audience if you’re still putting all your effort into print ads and flyers while neglecting digital platforms.
What Goes Wrong?
- Limited Reach: Print ads and traditional media can’t compete with the exposure of digital platforms.
- Missed Engagement Opportunities: Modern buyers expect interactive content like social media posts, virtual tours, and live Q&A sessions.
- Wasted Budget: Traditional advertising often costs more while delivering fewer measurable results.
How to Fix It
- Embrace Social Media: Platforms like Instagram and TikTok are goldmines for visually-driven industries like real estate.
- Invest in Paid Ads: Google Ads and Facebook Ads allow precise targeting to reach the right audience.
- Try Emerging Trends: Experiment with tools like augmented reality (AR) to let buyers virtually “walk through” a property.
Pro Tip: Combine traditional and digital efforts by including QR codes in print materials that link to interactive online content.
## 12. Mismanaging Ad Budgets
It’s easy to burn through your budget if you’re not strategic, making this one of the most costly realtor advertising mistakes. Whether you’re overspending on ineffective channels or spreading your budget too thin, mismanagement can derail even the best real estate marketing plan.
Why It Matters A poorly managed budget wastes money and limits your ability to invest in high-performing strategies. It’s not about how much you spend — it’s about spending wisely.
What Goes Wrong?
- No Tracking: Without tracking ROI, you won’t know which ads are driving results.
- Overinvesting in One Channel: Putting all your money into a single platform is risky and limits reach.
- Underestimating Costs: Many agents fail to account for additional expenses like editing, ad boosts, or retargeting campaigns.
How to Fix It
- Set Clear Goals: Define what you want to achieve — more leads, faster sales, or higher-quality inquiries — and allocate your budget accordingly.
- Monitor Performance: Use analytics tools to track which ads are delivering the best results.
- Diversify Spending: Spread your budget across multiple platforms and adjust based on what works best.
Pro Tip: Always include a small buffer in your budget for unexpected costs or testing new strategies.
## 13. Forgetting to Update or Refresh Ads
Running the same ad for months on end can lead to what marketers call “ad fatigue.” Forgetting to update your advertising materials is one of the sneakiest property advertisement mistakes because it gradually reduces effectiveness without you even noticing.
Why It Matters Potential buyers get bored seeing the same ad repeatedly, and over time, it becomes easy to ignore. Fresh, updated ads keep your audience engaged and intrigued.
What Goes Wrong?
- Stale Content: Reusing the same copy, images, or videos for too long makes your listing feel outdated.
- Ignoring Market Changes: Ads that don’t reflect current trends or seasons can seem irrelevant.
- Overexposure: Frequent viewers may feel they’ve “seen it all,” even if they haven’t explored the property fully.
How to Fix It
- Rotate Content: Use multiple versions of your ads to keep things fresh and engaging.
- Adapt to Seasons: Update imagery and copy to reflect the time of year. For instance, highlight cozy fireplaces in winter or spacious outdoor areas in summer.
- Test New Ideas: Run A/B tests with different headlines, visuals, and CTAs to see what resonates most.
Pro Tip: Add a countdown timer to ads for real estate open houses or limited-time offers to create urgency and encourage quicker action.
## 14. Overloading Ads with Too Much Information
You’ve got a lot to say about your property — that’s understandable! But stuffing your ad with every single detail is one of the most common real estate advertising mistakes. Buyers are looking for quick, digestible information, not a full-blown essay.
Why It Matters Overloading your ad can overwhelm potential buyers and bury the key selling points. Instead of feeling informed, they might feel confused or uninterested.
What Goes Wrong?
- Text Walls: Long paragraphs with no breaks are hard to read.
- Unfocused Messaging: Trying to highlight too many features makes the ad feel cluttered and disorganized.
- Irrelevant Details: Including minor details like paint brands or curtain rod types dilutes the impact of important features.
How to Fix It
- Focus on Highlights: Showcase 3–5 standout features that make the property unique.
- Use Bullet Points: Break up text into easy-to-read sections.
- Keep It Simple: Save in-depth information for showings or additional materials.
Pro Tip: Use a hierarchy in your ad: grab attention with a compelling headline, follow up with key features, and close with a call-to-action.
## 15. Ignoring the Power of Testimonials and Reviews
When it comes to building trust, nothing beats social proof. Ignoring testimonials or reviews in your real estate ads is one of the biggest realtor advertising mistakes in today’s trust-driven market.
Why It Matters Buying a home is a huge decision, and buyers need reassurance that they’re working with a reliable realtor. Testimonials from happy clients can build confidence and make your ads more relatable.
What Goes Wrong?
- No Testimonials: Failing to include any social proof makes your ad less credible.
- Generic Reviews: Vague statements like “Great experience!” don’t add much value.
- Unverified Claims: Sharing reviews that seem overly polished or fake can backfire.
How to Fix It
- Feature Real Client Stories: Use testimonials that highlight specific benefits or successful outcomes.
- Incorporate Video Reviews: A short video from a happy client can be more engaging than text.
- Showcase on Multiple Channels: Add testimonials to your website, social media posts, and print materials.
Pro Tip: If you don’t have enough reviews, ask past clients for feedback and permission to feature their experiences in your advertising.
## 16. Failing to Leverage Local Partnerships
Real estate isn’t just about homes — it’s about the communities they’re in. One overlooked property advertisement mistake is failing to collaborate with local businesses or influencers to enhance your marketing efforts.
Why It Matters Partnering with local businesses or influencers can expand your reach and create a sense of community around your listing. Buyers are often just as interested in the neighborhood as the property itself.
What Goes Wrong?
- No Local Ties: Ads that don’t mention local businesses or attractions feel disconnected.
- Missing Out on Cross-Promotion: Ignoring partnership opportunities means fewer eyes on your listing.
- Overlooking Influencers: Skipping local influencers who know the area well can cost you valuable exposure.
How to Fix It
- Highlight Local Perks: Mention nearby coffee shops, parks, gyms, or popular hangout spots in your ads.
- Collaborate on Events: Partner with local businesses for open houses or community events to attract foot traffic.
- Work with Influencers: Engage neighborhood influencers to showcase your property to their followers.
Example: “Located steps away from Oakwood Café and Greenfield Park, this home offers not just a place to live but a community to thrive in.”
Pro Tip: Include shoutouts to local hotspots in your social media posts to create buzz and connect with the audience.
## Quick-Recap: 16 Real Estate Advertising Mistakes to Avoid
Real estate advertising is an art and science, but even seasoned professionals can fall into these common traps:
- Don’t skip video prospecting: It’s one of the most engaging ways to showcase properties and connect with buyers. Tailor your videos to the buyer’s needs for maximum impact. High-quality visuals and clear audio ensure your videos stand out. Here are a few examples of video prospecting for real estate agents.
- Skimping on Quality Visuals: Poor photos or videos turn buyers away — invest in professional virtual staging and photography.
- Writing Generic Descriptions: Bland or vague copy fails to highlight unique property features.
- Neglecting Targeted Advertising: Without audience-specific messaging, you’re wasting time and money.
- Ignoring Mobile Optimization: A clunky mobile experience loses leads — go responsive and test on all devices.
- Overpricing Properties: Inflated prices deter buyers and drag out sales.
- Skipping Video Marketing: Videos engage buyers and offer dynamic property showcases — don’t skip this powerful tool.
- Using Too Much Jargon: Overly technical language alienates buyers — keep it simple and relatable.
- Ignoring Local Market Trends: Tailor your messaging to highlight what’s relevant in your area.
- Failing to Include Clear CTAs: Without a compelling call-to-action, potential buyers won’t know the next step.
- Relying on Outdated Channels: Embrace digital tools like social media and paid ads to stay competitive.
- Mismanaging Budgets: Track ROI and spend strategically to maximize your advertising impact.
- Forgetting to Update Ads: Fresh, seasonal content keeps your listings relevant and engaging.
- Overloading Ads with Information: Keep your copy concise and focused on the key selling points.
- Ignoring Testimonials: Social proof builds trust and reassures buyers you’re the right realtor for the job.
- Failing to Leverage Local Partnerships: Collaborate with businesses and influencers to showcase community appeal.
By addressing these pitfalls, you’ll create ads that captivate buyers, build trust, and close deals faster. Avoiding these mistakes isn’t just about improving your marketing; it’s about positioning yourself as a trusted, professional realtor in a competitive market.
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: How does personalized video marketing for real estate enhance advertisement performance?
Videos provide a dynamic, immersive experience that photos alone can’t deliver. Personalized video emails with walkthroughs, drone footage, and guided tours give buyers a better sense of the property’s layout and ambiance. Listings with videos receive significantly more inquiries, making video marketing a must-have tool.
## Q: Why is video prospecting so essential in real estate prospecting?
Personalized video outreach with video makes your property listings more engaging. Unlike static images, videos allow buyers to visualize the property’s layout, features, and ambiance, helping them form an emotional connection. Adding a personal touch, like addressing the buyer’s specific needs in the video, further builds trust and sets you apart from competitors.
## Q: Does virtual staging mislead buyers?
Virtual staging isn’t misleading as long as it’s disclosed in the listing. Clearly label photos as “virtually staged” and ensure they reflect realistic possibilities for the space. Transparency builds trust and avoids disappointment during showings.
## Q: How can I improve my ad copy to attract more buyers?
Use engaging, descriptive language that focuses on the property’s unique features and benefits. Avoid generic terms like “nice house” and instead highlight specifics, such as “a sun-drenched living room with floor-to-ceiling windows.” Ensure your copy is concise, typo-free, and includes a clear call-to-action to guide buyers.
## Q: What should I include in a virtual tour to make it effective?
A virtual tour should offer a comprehensive view of the property, covering all key areas like the kitchen, living spaces, bedrooms, and outdoor spaces. Use smooth transitions, wide-angle shots, and natural lighting to enhance the experience. Add voiceover narration or pop-up notes to highlight unique features.
## Q: How do I avoid “ad fatigue” with repeated listings?
Rotate your content regularly by updating images, changing ad copy, and experimenting with different formats like videos or slideshows. Highlight seasonal features, such as a cozy fireplace in winter or a lush garden in spring. Testing new headlines or CTAs can also help keep your ads fresh and engaging.
## Q: How can I use testimonials strategically in advertising?
Place client testimonials in high-visibility areas like landing pages, social media posts, or email campaigns. Use specific, relatable stories that highlight how you helped clients achieve their goals. Video testimonials are especially impactful, as they feel more authentic and engaging than text alone.
## Q: How do I measure the success of my real estate advertising campaigns?
Key performance indicators (KPIs) like click-through rates (CTR), cost per lead (CPL), and conversion rates can help measure your success. Use analytics tools to track these metrics and identify which ads perform well. Regularly review and optimize your strategy based on this data.
## Conclusion
Real estate advertising is as much about avoiding pitfalls as it is about showcasing properties effectively. However, with the right strategies, these missteps can be opportunities for growth and success. You can elevate your advertising efforts to build trust, capture attention, and connect with the right audience — faster and more effectively.
B2B sales prospecting tools like Potion empower realtors to create hyper-personalized, scalable video messaging campaigns that feel genuine and leave a lasting impression. From video sales letters to testimonial sharing, Potion streamlines your efforts while maximizing engagement. Thus, making it an invaluable tool in the real estate marketing strategy.
Mistakes are inevitable, but how you respond to them defines your success. Avoiding these blunders isn’t just about better ads; it’s about positioning yourself as a reliable, forward-thinking realtor who understands the art of marketing homes. So, take these insights, refine your approach, and turn your advertising into a powerful tool that attracts buyers and closes deals.
The real estate market is ever-evolving, and staying ahead means staying informed. Ready to revolutionize your marketing strategy? The next big sale is just a well-crafted ad away!

## Top Effective Real Estate Advertising Methods for Every Agent
## 1. Try Video Prospecting For Faster Closes
If a picture is worth a thousand words, imagine the power of personalized AI videos! AI video prospecting has become a game-changing strategy in real estate advertising. It allows agents to build personal connections with potential clients and showcase properties in a way that static images or text simply can’t.
Why Video Prospecting is a Real Estate Game-Changer
- Highly Personal: Sending custom AI videos making your leads feel valued and heard, building trust from the get-go.
- Boosts Engagement: Video sales letters grab attention faster than plain emails or texts, increasing response rates.
- Showcases Properties Better: Highlighting unique features through a personalized video email walk-through. Thus, creating an immersive experience.
How to Make Video Prospecting Work for Real Estate
- Personalized Property Showcases Instead of sending generic emails, record personalized video tours for each lead. Mention their preferences — like a family-friendly neighborhood or a spacious kitchen — to show you’ve been listening.
- Follow-Up Messages Got a lead who didn’t respond to your email or call? Send a quick, upbeat video messaging like: “Hey [Name], just wanted to follow up! I found a property I think you’ll love. Check it out, and let me know your thoughts!” Pro Tip: Keep it under 60 seconds for maximum impact.
- Virtual Open House Invites Invite prospects to your open house with a short, professional video explaining what makes the property special. Include snippets of the home, like the lush backyard or luxurious master suite, to build excitement. Additionally, here are a few real estate open house tips that you could follow.
- Answer FAQs via Video Answer common buyer or seller questions — like “How does the closing process work?” — through quick explainer videos. This adds a personal touch while demonstrating your expertise.

You can send videos directly via email, embed them in LinkedIn outreach, or use them in messaging apps. Potion even offers tools for seamless integration into your outreach efforts.
Pro Tips for Video Prospecting
- Keep It Short: Aim for 1–2 minutes. Long videos can lose the viewer’s attention.
- Be Authentic: Don’t over-rehearse. A genuine, conversational tone works best.
- Use Engaging Visuals: Add your branding, captions, or even a call-to-action at the end of the video.
- Follow Up: After sending a video, follow up with a quick message to ensure it was received.

Each video showcased the property tailored to the buyer’s preferences — like family-friendly homes or modern apartments. The campaign led to 15 direct inquiries and 3 successful sales within two weeks!

Your next big deal might just be one click away! Additionally, here are a few more real estate prospecting ideas that you could use.
## 2. The Power of Social Media
Social media isn’t just a trend — it’s where your audience lives, breathes, and scrolls. Platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok have revolutionized advertising for real estate. Thus, giving agents a golden opportunity to showcase properties like never before.
Why Social Media Works for Realtors
- Massive Reach: Over 5.17 billion people use social media. Your next buyer is likely one of them!
- Visual Appeal: Real estate thrives on visuals, and platforms like Instagram let you showcase your listings in stunning
- ways.
- Cost-Effective: A boosted post on Facebook or Instagram can generate thousands of impressions for a fraction of traditional ad costs.
Pro Tips for Social Media Advertising
- Leverage Video Content: Create engaging video tours of properties. Use Reels or TikTok to highlight unique features like “the coziest reading nook” or “a rooftop view to die for.”
- Use Paid Ads Wisely: Run targeted ads based on location, income, and buying behavior. Meta’s Ad Manager is a treasure trove for pinpointing your ideal audience.
- Engage Your Audience: Post polls, Q&A sessions, or property quizzes to spark interaction. People love to feel involved.
- Tap Into Stories: Use Instagram or Facebook Stories to post quick, behind-the-scenes snippets, like virtual staging a home or prepping for an open house.
Example: A small real estate agency in Austin increased inquiries by 60% simply by creating Instagram Reels showcasing properties with quirky storytelling. A snippet like “Welcome to your future dream home!” paired with upbeat music grabbed eyeballs — and hearts. Here’s a sample for your reference:
## 3. Dominate with Google Ads
When potential buyers search for properties, where do they turn? Google! That’s why Google Ads should be a cornerstone of your real estate advertising strategy.
Why Google Ads Are Gold for Realtors
- High Intent Audience: People searching “homes for sale near me” or “best property deals in [city]” are actively looking to buy.
- Local Targeting: Google Ads let you zero in on specific zip codes, ensuring your ads reach the right people.
- Measurable Results: With detailed analytics, you’ll know exactly how well your ad is performing.
Best Practices for Google Ads
- Use Specific Keywords: Keywords like “commercial real estate advertising” or “property advertising in [city]” work better than generic terms.
- Craft a Compelling Call-to-Action (CTA): “Book a Free Consultation” or “Schedule a Virtual Tour Today!” grabs attention and encourages clicks.
- Optimize Landing Pages: Ensure your landing page matches the ad. If the ad is about luxury condos, don’t redirect users to a generic homepage.
- Experiment with Ad Extensions: Use site links, call buttons, or location extensions to make your ad stand out.
Example: A realtor in Miami used Google Ads targeting “oceanfront condos in Miami Beach” and saw a 45% increase in click-through rates within a month. The secret? A catchy CTA — “Experience Luxury Living by the Sea” — and a beautifully designed landing page.
## 4. Local SEO
Real estate is all about location, location, location. So why not dominate your local market with a solid SEO strategy? Local SEO ensures your business pops up when buyers search for properties in your area.
Why Local SEO Matters
- Increased Visibility: 46% of Google searches have local intent, meaning people are looking for businesses near them.
- Trust Factor: Appearing in local search results builds credibility and trust.
- Cost-Effective: Unlike paid ads, organic traffic from SEO is free — no recurring costs!
Steps to Nail Local SEO
- Claim Your Google My Business Profile: Fill out every detail, from your address to your business hours, and don’t forget to upload high-quality images.
- Encourage Reviews: Ask satisfied clients to leave glowing reviews on Google. Positive reviews can skyrocket your rankings.
- Use Location-Based Keywords: Incorporate phrases like “best realtor in [city]” or “property advertising near me” into your website copy and blog posts.
- Publish Local Content: Write blogs like “Top Neighborhoods to Buy a Home in [City]” or “5 Must-Know Real Estate Trends in [Year].”
Example: A real estate agent in Palm springs created a blog series titled “Palm Spring’s Hottest Neighborhoods” and optimized it with local keywords. Within three months, they noticed a 60% increase in organic website traffic and a spike in local inquiries.
## 5. Let Buyers Step Inside Virtually
Gone are the days when buyers had to visit multiple properties to decide. With Virtual Reality (VR) and 3D tours, you can let potential clients “walk through” homes without leaving their couch. Talk about a game-changer!
Why VR and 3D Tours Are Revolutionary
- Convenience: Buyers can explore properties anytime, anywhere.
- Enhanced Engagement: A 3D tour offers an immersive experience, keeping potential clients hooked.
- Broader Audience Reach: Out-of-town buyers or international investors can view properties as if they were physically there.
How to Implement VR and 3D Tours
- Partner with Professionals: Use services like Matterport or hire a professional who specializes in real estate VR to create high-quality tours.
- Highlight Unique Features: Make sure your 3D tour focuses on selling points like a spacious kitchen, luxury bathrooms, or a scenic backyard.
- Embed Tours Everywhere: Share these tours on your website, social media, and even in your email campaigns for maximum exposure.
- Use VR for Open Houses: Host virtual open houses to connect with buyers who can’t attend in person.
Example: A real estate agent in New York used 3D tours to showcase a luxury penthouse during the pandemic. The property sold within a week for the full asking price, even though the buyer never visited it in person.
## 6. Tap Into Influencer Marketing
Think influencers are just for fashion or tech brands? Think again! Influencer marketing is one of the best advertising strategies for real estate agents, especially when targeting younger buyers or specific niches.
Why Influencers Work for Realtors
- Built-In Audience: Influencers already have a loyal following that trusts their recommendations.
- Niche Targeting: Collaborate with influencers who align with your target market, like lifestyle bloggers or local content creators.
- Authenticity: A well-crafted influencer endorsement can feel more genuine than a traditional ad.
Pro Tips for Influencer Marketing
- Choose the Right Influencer: Look for local influencers or those with interests in real estate, interior design, or architecture.
- Create Engaging Content: Have the influencer create property tours, post Instagram stories, or share testimonials about working with you.
- Offer Value: Provide exclusive previews or early access to properties for the influencer to share with their audience.
- Track Performance: Use unique promo codes or trackable links to measure how much traffic or leads the influencer generates.
Example: A realtor in Los Angeles partnered with a local lifestyle blogger to promote an open house for a modern condo. The influencer’s Instagram story brought in over 200 attendees, and the condo was sold within two weeks!
## 7. Become the Go-To Content Expert
When buyers or sellers research online, guess what they’re looking for? Information. By offering valuable content, you can position yourself as a trusted expert in the real estate world.
Why Content Marketing Works
- Builds Trust: Sharing helpful advice and insights establishes you as a reliable source.
- Drives Traffic: Optimized blog posts and videos can bring in organic traffic.
- Encourages Lead Generation: Quality content keeps potential clients coming back to your site, increasing the chances of a conversion.
Ideas for Winning Content
- Educational Blog Posts: Write articles like “Top 10 Mistakes First-Time Homebuyers Make” or “Understanding Property Taxes 101.”
- Video Content: Create short, snappy videos explaining the buying process or showcasing local neighborhoods.
- Email Newsletters: Share market updates, newly listed properties, or home improvement tips with your subscribers.
- Downloadable Guides: Offer free resources like “The Ultimate Home-Selling Checklist” in exchange for email sign-ups.
Example: A property advertising agency in Seattle launched a blog series on “Hidden Gems of Seattle’s Real Estate Marketing.” The content was shared widely on social media, bringing in hundreds of new leads every month.
## 8. Embrace Geotargeted Advertising
Location matters in real estate — big time! Geotargeted advertising ensures your ads reach people in specific areas where they’re most likely to buy or rent. It’s like casting a laser-focused net rather than a wide, generic one.
Why Geotargeting Works in Real Estate
- Localized Relevance: Ads are shown to people in areas where you’re actively selling or renting properties.
- Cost-Efficiency: Instead of wasting your budget on irrelevant audiences, geotargeting ensures your money is well-spent.
- Higher Engagement: Buyers and renters are more likely to respond when the ads feel personally relevant.
Pro Tips for Geotargeted Real Estate Ads
- Use Social Media Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, and even Snapchat allow for geotargeted campaigns based on zip codes or cities.
- Leverage Google Ads: Set your ads to appear when users search for “homes near me” or similar terms in your target area.
- Include Local Keywords: Phrases like “luxury homes in [City]” or “affordable rentals in [Neighborhood]” can boost your click-through rates.
- Utilize Geofencing: Trigger ads for users who enter a specific geographic boundary — like a bustling downtown or a neighborhood near your listings.
Example: A realtor in Atlanta used geofencing to target ads around high-traffic apartment complexes and saw a 30% uptick in rental inquiries within weeks. By combining local imagery and keywords, the ads resonated perfectly with the audience.
## 9. Hosting Exclusive Property Events
Open houses are great, but exclusive property events? Now that’s next-level advertising for real estate. These invite-only affairs create a sense of exclusivity, attract serious buyers, and make properties feel more premium.
Why Exclusive Events Are Effective
- Drives High-Intent Traffic: Only genuinely interested buyers or investors are likely to attend.
- Builds Excitement: A well-organized event can create buzz and increase property visibility.
- Enhances the Property’s Appeal: Exclusive events position the property as high-end and desirable.
Steps to Host a Memorable Property Event
- Curate the Guest List: Focus on serious buyers, investors, and influencers in the real estate space.
- Add Unique Elements: Consider live music, gourmet catering, or virtual reality walkthroughs for a wow factor.
- Promote the Event: Use social media, email campaigns, and even direct mail to invite potential buyers.
- Offer Incentives: Provide perks like closing discounts or giveaways for attendees.
Example: A commercial real estate agent in Dallas hosted a wine-and-cheese evening at a newly listed office space. The event attracted top local businesses, resulting in two rental contracts by the end of the week.
## 10. Use Retargeting Ads To Your Benefit
Ever browsed a property online and noticed it following you across the internet? That’s retargeting in action, and it’s one of the most effective real estate advertising strategies to convert curious browsers into serious buyers.
Why Retargeting Ads Are Powerful
- Reminds Prospects: Keeps your property listings in front of people who’ve already shown interest.
- Increases Conversion Rates: Visitors who are retargeted are 70% more likely to take action.
- Customizable Messaging: Tailor ads based on the user’s behavior, like visiting a specific property page.
Best Practices for Retargeting
- Segment Your Audience: Target users based on their actions, such as viewing listings or filling out a form.
- Use Dynamic Ads: Showcase properties that the user previously viewed to reignite their interest.
- Cap the Frequency: Avoid bombarding users — keep the ad frequency reasonable to prevent ad fatigue.
- Include a Strong CTA: Use CTAs like “Book Your Tour Today!” or “Last Chance to Secure This Home!”
Example: A realtor in Chicago used Facebook retargeting ads to nudge users who had browsed a luxury townhouse listing. Within a month, the campaign resulted in three high-value offers.
## 11. Email Drip Campaigns To Nurture Leads
Email might sound old-school, but it’s a powerhouse when used strategically — especially for real estate. Drip campaigns are automated email sequences designed to guide leads through the buyer’s journey, keeping your brand top-of-mind without being pushy.
Why Email Drip Campaigns Are a Must-Have
- Cost-Effective: Unlike other channels, following real estate email marketing best practices delivers a high ROI with minimal investment.
- Personalization: Tailor emails based on user behavior, making each message feel like it was written just for them.
- Keeps Leads Warm: Instead of letting potential clients lose interest, regular emails keep them engaged.
Steps to a Winning Drip Campaign
- Segment Your Audience: Categorize leads into groups like first-time buyers, luxury buyers, or investors to tailor content effectively.
- Craft Engaging Subject Lines: Catch their attention with headlines like “Your Dream Home Awaits” or “Exclusive Listings in Your Area.” Here are a few of the best B2B cold email subject lines that you could use.
- Offer Value: Share helpful tips, market insights, or updates on new listings instead of just pushing sales.
- Include a Strong CTA: Every email should guide readers toward an action — schedule a tour, contact an agent, or visit your website.
- Regular Check-ins: Set regular email cadence for your campaigns to adapt with trends on time.
Example: A realtor in San Francisco implemented a drip campaign targeting tech professionals relocating to the city. With personalized emails showcasing nearby properties and lifestyle tips, the campaign generated five closed deals in three months!
## 12. Creative Print Advertising
While digital advertising steals the spotlight, print ads still hold their charm — especially in real estate. From eye-catching brochures to local magazines and postcards, print media can create a tangible connection with potential buyers.
Why Print Advertising Still Works
- Tangibility: A well-designed print ad sticks in a buyer’s memory longer than a fleeting digital banner.
- Local Reach: Placing ads in community newsletters or newspapers can connect you directly with local buyers.
- Boosts Credibility: High-quality print materials make your business appear polished and professional.
Ideas for Creative Print Ads
- Luxury Property Magazines: Showcase high-end properties in glossy publications targeting affluent audiences.
- Neighborhood-Focused Brochures: Highlight listings, local attractions, and amenities to appeal to specific communities.
- Direct Mail Postcards: Send beautifully designed postcards with property details or invites to open houses.
- Event Flyers: Use print ads to promote exclusive property events or real estate workshops.
Example: A small real estate firm in Boston sent out creative postcards shaped like houses to 500 local residents. The result? 30 inquiries and two property sales — all from one affordable print campaign!
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: What is the basic rule of advertising in real estate?
The basic rule of advertising in real estate is to know your audience. Tailor your message, visuals, and platforms to the specific needs and preferences of your target market. Whether it’s first-time buyers, luxury home seekers, or commercial investors, focus on showcasing the property’s unique value while building trust and credibility. Authenticity and clear calls-to-action are also key to converting interest into action. Additionally, here’s how to create a real estate marketing plan step by step.
## Q: What is the best way to get started with video prospecting in real estate?
Start small! Use video messaging tools like Potion to create personalized video marketing campaigns. Begin by sending video introductions to potential clients, showcasing a property’s key features, or responding to inquiries with quick, authentic video messages. Over time, you can experiment with virtual open house invitations and FAQ-style explainer videos to expand your AI video outreach. Here are a few examples of real estate video prospecting that you could use.
## Q: What types of content perform best on social media for real estate?
Content like video tours, before-and-after staging posts, client testimonials, and interactive polls work well. Showcasing local attractions, sharing market insights, or posting tips for buyers and sellers also boosts engagement. Platforms like Instagram and TikTok thrive on visual appeal, so high-quality images and short, engaging videos are essential.
## Q: What are some examples of effective call-to-actions (CTAs) in real estate advertising?
Examples include:
- “Book Your Free Home Valuation Today”
- “Explore Virtual Tours Now”
- “Schedule a Private Showing”
- “Discover Your Dream Home in [City]”
- “Contact Us for Exclusive Listings”
A strong CTA motivates users to take the next step, making it an essential component of any campaign.
## Q: What’s the best way to follow up after sending a video prospecting message?
After sending a video, follow up with a short, friendly text or email. For example: “Hi [Name], just wanted to make sure you saw the video I sent earlier. Let me know if you’d like more details or want to schedule a tour!”
This keeps the conversation open and shows that you’re attentive.
## Q: How can agents integrate multiple advertising strategies for better results?
Combine complementary strategies for a multi-channel approach. For example:
- Use Google Ads and social media for immediate visibility.
- Optimize local SEO and content marketing for long-term organic growth.
- Enhance outreach with personalized video prospecting and retargeting ads.
Integration ensures you reach potential clients at various stages of their journey.
## Q: What’s the role of video storytelling in real estate advertising?
Video storytelling creates an emotional connection with potential buyers. Instead of just listing features, describe how a family could create memories in the spacious kitchen or how the serene backyard offers a perfect escape. Stories make properties more relatable and memorable.
## Conclusion
Real estate advertising isn’t just about showcasing properties. It’s about creating meaningful connections and building trust in a crowded market. By incorporating innovative strategies like personalized videos for real estate agents, harnessing the power of AI videos, and leveraging AI email marketing tools like Potion, you can engage with clients on a deeper, more personalized level.
Pair these modern techniques with proven methods like local SEO, exclusive events, and creative print advertising. And you’ll have a comprehensive approach to attracting the right buyers and sellers. The beauty of these strategies lies in their versatility — whether you’re targeting first-time buyers, luxury clients, or commercial investors, there’s a tactic to fit every niche.
Remember, success in real estate is all about standing out. With a mix of creativity, technology, and a clear understanding of your audience, your advertising can transform your business, one connection at a time. So, dive in, experiment boldly, and watch your efforts turn into sold signs!

text:
An open house isn’t just about unlocking the front door and waiting for buyers to stroll in. It’s a strategic play in the real estate game — and you’ve got to play it well! A great open house is your chance to showcase a property in its best light, create buzz, and help buyers envision themselves calling it “home sweet home.” So, how do you make your open house stand out from the rest?
In this guide, we’ll explore powerful real estate open house tips that every agent (or homeowner) can use to make a lasting impression. These tips go beyond the basics and dive into real strategies to drive attendance, engage buyers, and close deals.
Let’s jump in!
## Turn Lookers Into Buyers: Real Estate Open House Tips & Best Practices to Impress Buyers
## Tip #1: Make the First Impression Count
You’ve heard it before: “You never get a second chance to make a first impression.” Well, this couldn’t be more true in real estate! The moment buyers pull up to the property, they’re forming opinions. Your job? Wow them right from the start.
Focus on Curb Appeal The exterior of the home sets the tone. A well-kept front yard and inviting entrance immediately signal that the property is worth their time.
- Mow the lawn and trim overgrown hedges. No one likes a jungle!
- Add fresh flowers or potted plants. A pop of color works wonders.
- Clean the driveway, porch, and windows. Think sparkling clean.
- Place a welcome mat. Small details can make a home feel inviting.
Pro Tip: If it’s a warm day, offer a refreshing lemonade stand outside. It’s a friendly way to make attendees feel welcomed — and they’ll remember it!
Stage the Entryway Once buyers walk through the door, keep the momentum going with a tidy, well-staged entryway.
- Declutter and depersonalize. Remove personal photos, shoes, and unnecessary items.
- Add a statement piece. A console table with a vase of fresh flowers or a stylish mirror can add a touch of charm.
- Keep it bright. Natural light is your best friend, so open curtains and blinds.
Example: Imagine stepping into a cozy home where the scent of freshly baked cookies wafts through the air. Add soft background music, and you’ve got the recipe for a perfect welcome.
## Tip #2: Promote Your Open House Like a Pro
You can stage the home to perfection, but if no one shows up, what’s the point? Successful promotion is critical to a high-traffic open house.
Go Big on Social Media Social media platforms are your secret weapon for spreading the word. Don’t just post about the open house — create buzz around it.
- Facebook Events: Set up an event page and invite your network.
- Instagram Stories: Use photos, videos, and countdown timers to remind followers of the date.
- Short Videos: Give a sneak peek of the property. Highlight features like the spacious backyard or newly renovated kitchen.
- Geo-Targeted Ads: Promote the open house to potential buyers in specific locations.
- Create Personalized Video Invitations: Send one-on-one video messages to potential buyers in your database. Mention specific features they might appreciate. Use video prospecting tools like Potion to save time on this by creating AI personalized videos at scale. Record a single video, and Potion’s AI will seamlessly customize it with each recipient’s name and details — saving you hours of work while maximizing outreach. Here’s a tutorial covering how to do this.
Pro Tip: Use hashtags like #OpenHouse, #[YourCity]RealEstate, or #DreamHome to boost visibility.
Leverage Local Networks Word of mouth can be just as powerful as digital promotion. Tap into local networks to spread the news.
- Neighborhood Groups: Post on Nextdoor or community Facebook pages.
- Partner with Local Businesses: Ask coffee shops or gyms to display flyers.
- Email Lists: Reach out to your database of buyers and fellow agents.
- Use Video in Email Campaigns: Embed videos in your email invites. Video thumbnails can boost click-through rates and engagement significantly.
Example: Use B2B sales prospecting tools like Potion to send a personalized video email that says, “Hi [Name], this charming 3-bedroom home won’t last long! Join us for an open house this Saturday to explore the spacious kitchen, cozy living room, and stunning backyard. I can’t wait for you to see it!”
## Tip #3: Create an Experience, Not Just a Tour
A successful open house should feel like an event — not just another personalized video tour. You want buyers to stay, explore, and picture themselves living there.
Offer Something Memorable Go beyond the usual and give visitors a reason to linger.
- Serve Refreshments: Snacks and drinks make people feel comfortable. Think coffee, cookies, or even a catered spread for high-end properties.
- Host Giveaways: Offer small prizes, like a gift card raffle, for attendees who leave their contact details.
- Provide Informative Brochures: Highlight key features, upgrades, and neighborhood perks in a handout they can take home.
Pro Tip: Create a digital brochure with a QR code for tech-savvy buyers. They can scan it and access property details on their phone.
Engage with Attendees A friendly and knowledgeable host can make all the difference. Don’t just stand in the corner — actively engage with visitors.
- Ask Open-Ended Questions: “What do you think of the backyard? Could you see yourself entertaining here?”
- Share Stories: Tell them about the upgrades, the neighborhood, or the home’s unique history.
- Provide Expert Insight: Be ready to answer questions about schools, amenities, or the buying process.
- Pre-Engage Visitors with AI Videos: Start building relationships even before your open house begins. Use AI sales tools like Potion to send a personalized video welcoming potential attendees and sharing what they can expect at the event. Highlight standout features, address FAQs, and create excitement before they arrive, all without ever stepping in front of the camera. Simply create custom videos with Potion’s personal AI video avatars.
Example Script For Pre-Event Video: “Hi there! I’m excited to welcome you to our open house at 789 Elm Street this Saturday. The newly renovated kitchen and large backyard are just a few of the highlights I think you’ll love. I look forward to meeting you!”
Pro Tip: AI Videos can help you prequalify leads by generating interest and excitement. Thus, making your open house more effective.
Example: If someone mentions they love the kitchen, respond with, “It’s great, isn’t it? The owners installed those quartz countertops just last year — they’re incredibly durable and stylish.”
## Tip #4: Highlight the Home’s Best Features with a Story
Every home has a story. It’s your job to tell it in a way that resonates with buyers and connects them emotionally to the space. People don’t just buy houses — they buy what life could look like in that house.
Spotlight the “Wow Factor” Identify the standout features of the home and give them the attention they deserve. Whether it’s a newly renovated kitchen, a stunning fireplace, or a dreamy backyard, let buyers experience these spaces in an unforgettable way.
- For Kitchens: Set the scene with a cozy vibe — think fresh flowers on the counter, a bowl of lemons for a pop of color, and the smell of fresh coffee.
- For Outdoor Spaces: Arrange patio furniture with soft cushions and twinkling string lights to highlight a usable, entertaining space.
- For Living Areas: Add warm touches like throw pillows, artful rugs, and soft music playing in the background.
Tell the Story of the Space When showing key features, connect them to lifestyle benefits. Ask yourself, what kind of memories could be made here?
- “Picture yourself hosting Sunday brunch in this sunlit dining room — it’s perfect for entertaining family and friends.”
- “Can you imagine summer nights spent in this backyard with friends around the firepit?”
Pro Tip: If the home has a unique history (like an original 1920s hardwood floor), share it! Buyers love details that make a home feel special.
## Tip #5: Use Technology to Make the Open House Stand Out
In today’s tech-driven world, buyers expect more than just a walk-through. Integrating technology into your open house can make it more engaging, accessible, and memorable — especially for younger, digital-savvy buyers.
Provide Virtual Open House Options Not every buyer can attend in person, but that doesn’t mean they should miss out! Virtual tours can expand your reach and attract out-of-town buyers or busy professionals.
- Live Virtual Tours: Use platforms like Zoom or Facebook Live to give remote buyers a real-time walkthrough. Highlight the key spaces and take live questions.
- 360° Virtual Walkthroughs: Create a pre-recorded, interactive virtual tour buyers can explore at their convenience.
Set Up Digital Tools for Visitors Incorporate interactive tech to enhance the experience for attendees.
- QR Codes: Place scannable QR codes around the house that link to room details, renovation histories, or neighborhood amenities.
- Digital Sign-Ins: Replace the old paper-and-pen guest book with an iPad or phone sign-in. Not only does this modernize the experience, but it also ensures you collect accurate contact information.
- Interactive Maps: Showcase nearby schools, parks, or local favorites like cafes and gyms on a digital map to highlight the lifestyle benefits.
- Enhance Follow-Up with Personalized AI Videos: After your open house, keep attendees engaged with tailored follow-up videos. Use AI tools for real estate agents like Potion to send personalized thank-you videos, answer questions, or re-engage visitors who couldn’t attend. Potion’s AI allows you to create custom AI videos in bulk. All you need is a script, and it generates full-length videos with your own face, voice & gestures. Thus, making your follow-ups feel personal while saving you time. Here are few examples of video prospecting for real estate.
Pro Tip: Offer a digital brochure that buyers can take with them. Ensure that you load them with high-quality images, videos, and neighborhood perks. It’s convenient and leaves a lasting impression!
## Tip #6: Schedule the Open House at the Perfect Time
When it comes to real estate, timing is everything — and your open house is no exception. If you want maximum attendance, you need to schedule it when buyers are most likely to show up.
Pick the Right Day and Time While weekends are traditionally prime time for open houses, not all weekends are created equal! Here’s how to optimize your timing:
- Saturday Mornings (10 AM–12 PM): Early risers and weekend planners will often carve out time to attend.
- Sunday Afternoons (1 PM–4 PM): This is the sweet spot for most open houses, as people are typically free and relaxed after brunch.
- Weekday Evenings (5 PM–7 PM): Host a “Twilight Open House” for professionals who can’t attend during the day. The evening light can add a magical touch to the property.
Avoid Competing with Local Events Check your local calendar to ensure your open house doesn’t clash with major events like festivals, sports games, or holidays that could steal your audience’s attention.
Create Urgency with Limited Availability Promote the open house as a “one-day-only” opportunity to view the property.
- Use phrases like, “Don’t miss your chance to see this stunning home in person — one day only!”
- Combine this with targeted marketing on social media, email campaigns, and neighborhood signs to build buzz.
Pro Tip: If the property has beautiful evening lighting, consider hosting a sunset open house. Offer drinks like sparkling water or wine, and let the soft golden hour light do its magic!
## Tip #7: Make It Easy for Buyers to Visualize Their Future
When buyers step into a property, they should feel like they can move in tomorrow. Creating a blank canvas while still making the home feel warm and inviting is a fine balance — but it’s worth it!
Declutter Like a Pro Clutter is the enemy of visualization. Buyers should focus on the space itself, not on distractions.
- Pack Away Personal Items: Remove family photos, kids’ artwork, and fridge magnets. You want the home to feel neutral.
- Clear Surfaces: Kitchen counters, bathroom vanities, and living room tables should be clean and minimal.
- Organize Closets: Buyers will open closets. A well-organized, clutter-free closet signals ample storage.
Add Neutral Touches While depersonalization is key, you still want to make the space feel inviting.
- Use neutral-colored throws, rugs, and pillows to create a clean, modern look.
- Add fresh greenery or a simple vase of flowers to brighten rooms naturally.
- Use soft scents, like lavender or citrus, to create a calming atmosphere.
Pro Tip: Rent a storage unit to temporarily house personal items and excess furniture. More open space = a larger-feeling home!
## Tip #8: Pay Attention to the Little Details That Buyers Notice
It’s often the little things that make or break a buyer’s impression of a home. Small issues can create doubt, while thoughtful touches leave a positive mark.
Fix What’s Broken (Even Minor Issues) You’d be surprised how quickly small imperfections can add up in a buyer’s mind. Before the open house:
- Replace burnt-out lightbulbs and fix flickering lights.
- Tighten wobbly doorknobs, cabinet handles, or railings.
- Repair leaky faucets and ensure all toilets flush smoothly.
- Touch up chipped paint and scuffed walls.
Clean, Clean, Clean Buyers expect the property to look pristine — no excuses!
- Windows: Sparkling windows let in more natural light and make rooms feel bigger.
- Floors: Deep clean carpets, polish hardwood, and vacuum thoroughly.
- Appliances: Buyers often peek inside the fridge or oven — make sure they shine.
- Bathrooms: Scrub the grout, replace worn-out caulking, and hang fresh towels.
Pro Tip: Hire a professional cleaning service if you’re short on time. It’s a small investment with a huge payoff!
## Tip #9: Offer a Neighborhood Tour Along with the Home
Selling a house isn’t just about the property — it’s about the lifestyle. Many buyers care as much about the neighborhood as they do the home itself. Show them why this location is a dream come true.
Highlight Key Neighborhood Perks Before the open house, gather details about local amenities that matter to buyers:
- Schools and Parks: Perfect for families with kids. Mention nearby schools, playgrounds, and sports fields.
- Dining and Shopping: Point out trendy cafes, restaurants, and shopping centers.
- Commute and Transportation: Highlight how close the home is to public transit, major highways, or business hubs.
Example: “This home is just a 5-minute walk to the local farmers’ market and a 10-minute drive to downtown — ideal for both weekend fun and work commutes.”
Create a Local Info Station Set up a small corner in the home with brochures or a digital screen showcasing neighborhood highlights. Include:
- Maps of the area
- Photos of local parks, cafes, or landmarks
- Testimonials from current residents about why they love the neighborhood
Pro Tip: Offer personalized tours of the neighborhood for serious buyers. Drive them around and show off its hidden gems — this extra step leaves a lasting impression!
## Tip #10: Use Light to Your Advantage
Lighting can make or break the feel of a home. The right light transforms a space, making it feel larger, warmer, and more inviting — something every buyer will notice.
Maximize Natural Light Nothing beats sunlight streaming through the windows. It makes rooms look bigger, brighter, and more appealing. Here’s how to make the most of it:
- Open all blinds, curtains, and shutters before the open house begins.
- Trim bushes or trees outside windows to ensure they don’t block the light.
- Clean windows inside and out for a crystal-clear, sunlight-filled view.
Example: If the home has a gorgeous window in the living room, place a cozy seating arrangement nearby to draw attention to it.
Layer Artificial Lighting For rooms with limited natural light — like basements or hallways — layering artificial light can work wonders.
- Use overhead lighting to brighten the space evenly.
- Add floor lamps or table lamps to create pockets of warmth.
- Install under-cabinet lights in the kitchen to highlight workspaces.
Pro Tip: Stick with soft white LED bulbs (around 2700K–3000K). They provide a cozy glow without being too harsh or yellow.
## Tip #11: Add Strategic Signage to Guide Visitors
An open house is more than just a walk-through — it’s a curated experience. Thoughtful, well-placed signage can guide buyers through the home seamlessly, highlight key features, and answer common questions before they even need to ask.
Directional Signs for Flow Guide visitors naturally through the property so they don’t miss any highlights. Use small, tasteful signs like:
- “→ Don’t Miss the Backyard!” to point buyers toward outdoor spaces.
- “Check Out the Spa-Like Master Bathroom!” to direct attention to luxurious upgrades.
- “Upstairs → Bedrooms & Bonus Room” to maintain flow.
Feature Tags for Key Selling Points Buyers won’t always notice the finer details, so call them out! Place small signs or cards near standout features:
- “New Quartz Countertops Installed 2023” on kitchen counters.
- “Energy-Efficient HVAC System” near thermostats or air vents.
- “Smart Home Features: Ask for a Demo!” if the property has tech upgrades.
Neighborhood Info at the Exit Before buyers leave, remind them why the location is a win. Place a sign with highlights like:
- “Top-Rated Schools Nearby!”
- “5 Minutes to Downtown Dining & Shops.”
Pro Tip: Use professional-looking signage. Avoid handwritten notes — they can feel rushed and unpolished.
## Tip #12: Be Prepared to Answer Every Question
Buyers come to open houses with a list of questions in their minds. The more informed and confident you are, the more trust you’ll build — and trust is the secret to turning interest into offers.
Know the Property Inside and Out Buyers may ask for details about the home’s history, upgrades, or functionality. Be ready with answers!
- Renovation Timeline: “The kitchen and bathrooms were updated in 2022 with modern finishes.”
- Utility Costs: “The average monthly electricity bill is $120, thanks to the energy-efficient windows.”
- Property Age and Maintenance: “The roof was replaced in 2021, and the HVAC system is brand new.”
Anticipate Buyer Concerns Think ahead about anything buyers might worry about and address it proactively.
- If the backyard is small, mention its low-maintenance appeal: “Perfect for busy families who don’t want endless yard work!”
- If the home is older, highlight updates: “This 1950s gem has a brand-new electrical system and plumbing.”
Be the Neighborhood Expert Buyers care about more than just the house — they want to know about the lifestyle they’re buying into. Be ready to discuss:
- Local schools, gyms, and grocery stores
- Commute times and public transit options
- Upcoming developments or neighborhood improvements
Pro Tip: Keep a printed FAQ sheet at the open house. It’s a great reference for buyers, and they’ll appreciate the extra effort.
## Tip #13: Add a Personal Touch to Stand Out
An open house can sometimes feel a little impersonal, especially when buyers are hopping from property to property. Adding thoughtful, personalized touches helps you stand out and ensures buyers remember the experience — and the home.
Handwritten Notes for Buyers Create small, handwritten cards or notes highlighting charming details throughout the home. Place them in strategic spots for buyers to discover. For example:
- On the Kitchen Counter: “Imagine hosting your family dinners here. These brand-new appliances make cooking a breeze!”
- By the Fireplace: “Picture cozy winter evenings curled up by the fire with your favorite book or movie.”
- In the Master Bedroom: “Wake up to this peaceful view every morning — pure bliss!”
It’s a simple, low-cost gesture that feels personal and thoughtful.
Customize the Experience for the Target Buyer Think about the ideal buyer for the home and tailor the experience accordingly.
- Families: Leave coloring books or small treats for kids to keep them busy while parents explore.
- Young Professionals: Play upbeat, modern music and highlight nearby restaurants, gyms, or co-working spaces.
- High Ticket Sales Hack: Offer a small “welcome gift” like gourmet chocolates or scented candles for luxury buyers.
Pro Tip: Include a personalized thank-you note for attendees to take home, along with property brochures. It’s a small touch that goes a long way.
## Tip #14: Bring the Outdoors In
The connection between indoor and outdoor spaces can make a home feel bigger, brighter, and more functional. If you want buyers to fall in love with the property, make sure they can see — and feel — how the outdoors complements the indoors.
Stage the Outdoor Areas A poorly presented backyard or balcony is a missed opportunity. Stage outdoor spaces as extensions of the living areas to show their potential.
- Add patio furniture with cozy cushions and an outdoor rug.
- Place a small bistro table on balconies to create a charming breakfast nook.
- String fairy lights or set up lanterns for evening open houses — instant ambiance!
Example: For a home with a small backyard, set up a fire pit and a few chairs. Buyers will instantly imagine evenings spent under the stars.
Showcase the Views If the property has great views — whether it’s city lights, greenery, or a serene lake — show them off!
- Pull back all curtains and blinds in rooms with scenic views.
- Place small benches or chairs near windows so buyers can “sit and take it in.”
- During sunset hours, schedule the open house to make the view even more magical.
Pro Tip: If weather permits, leave the patio door open slightly to create a seamless flow between indoors and outdoors. Fresh air and natural sounds (like birds chirping) enhance the experience.
## Tip #15: Set Up a Feedback System That Works
Feedback is gold in real estate — it helps you improve future open houses and gauge buyer interest. However, getting meaningful feedback requires more than just a “Did you like the house?”
Create Easy-to-Fill Feedback Forms Prepare short, focused feedback cards or digital forms that visitors can complete in under a minute. Ask specific, open-ended questions like:
- “What was your favorite feature of the home?”
- “Is there anything that didn’t meet your expectations?”
- “How would you rate the property on a scale of 1–10?”
Include a section for attendees to leave their contact info (optional) for follow-up. If you’re using tech, set up a quick QR code that links to a feedback form on their phones.
Engage for Real-Time Feedback Don’t wait until the end of the open house — talk to buyers as they walk through the property. You can casually ask questions like:
- “How does this space work for you and your family’s needs?”
- “What are your thoughts on the kitchen upgrades? Would you want any other changes?”
- “What’s one thing you look for most in a home?”
These insights help you tailor your follow-up communication.
Pro Tip: Offer an incentive for feedback, like entering attendees into a small giveaway (think coffee shop gift cards or home decor vouchers). It encourages honesty and increases participation.
## Tip #16: Incorporate a Theme or “Lifestyle Hook”
An open house should feel less like a property tour and more like a curated experience. A themed approach brings personality to the event, appeals to buyer emotions, and helps them connect with the property on a deeper level.
Choose a Theme That Fits the Home Think about the property, the target audience, and the neighborhood vibe. Then create a theme that complements it.
- For Modern Homes: A “Tech-Forward Living” theme with smart home demos, sleek decor, and digital brochures.
- For Family-Friendly Homes: A “Family Fun Day” with cookies in the kitchen, a kids’ corner, and brochures highlighting nearby schools and parks.
- For Luxury Properties: An “Evening of Elegance” twilight open house with soft jazz, hors d’oeuvres, and sparkling drinks.
Example: Imagine hosting a “Backyard BBQ Open House” for a property with a spacious yard and deck. Offer burgers, lemonade, and lawn games like cornhole to show buyers how the space can shine for summer gatherings.
Pro Tip: Subtle decor — like coordinated flowers, refreshments, and background music — helps reinforce the theme without being over the top.
## Tip #17: Partner with Local Businesses for Cross-Promotion
An open house isn’t just about showcasing a home — it’s about selling a lifestyle. Partnering with local businesses creates buzz, adds value for buyers, and strengthens your reputation within the community.
Offer Samples or Discounts from Local Businesses Work with nearby businesses to provide open house attendees with something special. For example:
- A coffee shop could offer free coffee or pastries for attendees.
- A local florist could supply fresh bouquets for staging and offer discount coupons to buyers.
- A home decor store could display stylish pieces in the home and offer exclusive promotions.
This partnership benefits everyone — you get added value for your open house, businesses get exposure, and buyers leave with a positive experience.
Showcase Neighborhood Perks Include flyers or digital brochures featuring local hotspots that buyers will love, such as:
- Top-rated restaurants or coffee shops
- Popular gyms or yoga studios
- Local boutiques or farmers’ markets
Example: Hand out a small “Neighborhood Guide” that highlights nearby businesses and offers discounts. It makes the buyer feel like they’re already part of the community.
Pro Tip: Take it a step further by inviting local businesses to attend the open house. A bakery could set up a treat table, or a gym could display info about classes and promotions.
## Tip #18: Create a Follow-Up Plan That Converts
Your work doesn’t end when buyers leave the open house. A strong follow-up strategy in a real estate marketing plan ensures you stay top-of-mind. Thus, keeps the conversation going, and nudges interested buyers closer to making an offer.
Personalize Your Follow-Ups Buyers don’t want generic emails — they want to feel like their interest matters. Tailor your follow-up communication based on their feedback and questions during the open house.
- For Curious Buyers: Send a follow-up email with answers to any questions they asked, along with additional property details or photos.
- For Serious Buyers: Offer to schedule a private, second tour at their convenience.
- For Buyers On the Fence: Highlight the home’s strongest selling points or recent interest: “We’ve had multiple inquiries since the open house — let’s set up a time for you to take another look!”
- Address Questions: If you noticed specific concerns during the open house, respond directly with custom AI videos.
- Re-Engage Missed Opportunities: Send a recap video to prospects who couldn’t attend, inviting them to schedule a private showing.
- Use Potion to Send Custom Video Follow-Ups: Turn your follow-up strategy into a seamless, standout experience with Potion. Instead of generic emails, send AI personalized videos that re-engage buyers and address their needs. Whether it’s thanking them for attending, showcasing additional property details, or addressing specific questions, Potion helps you deliver tailored video messaging at scale.
