text:
Email marketing can be a goldmine — or a disaster! The difference often boils down to the little things that go unnoticed. If you’re putting in the effort but not seeing the returns, chances are you’re making one or more of these common email marketing mistakes. The good news? Most of these issues are easy to fix if you know what to look for.
In this article, we’ll walk through the most common blunders marketers make with email campaigns, why they matter, and how you can sidestep these pitfalls. If you’ve ever wondered why open rates are low or why subscribers keep dropping off, read on. We’ve got your back!
## Common Email Marketing Mistakes That Are Costing You Conversions (And How to Fix Them)
## Mistake #1: Ignoring Email Segmentation
Ever received an email that felt totally irrelevant to you? Maybe you signed up for a newsletter, and suddenly you’re getting product offers that don’t align with your interests? This happens when companies don’t segment their email lists properly.
Why This Is a Problem? Ignoring segmentation means treating all subscribers the same, regardless of their interests, behavior, or demographics. This approach leads to poor engagement and higher unsubscribe rates. When people feel like they’re just another name on a mailing list, they won’t hesitate to hit “unsubscribe.”
How to Fix It
- Try personalized video email tools: For advanced segmentation that includes hyper-personalized video emails, try using Potion. Potion allows you to create custom AI videos for different audience segments, making each email feel tailored and relevant. Whether you’re addressing customer onboarding, returning users, or cart abandonment solutions, Potion helps you engage more effectively by delivering unique, personalized video messaging for business.
- Start segmenting your audience: Divide your email list based on meaningful categories such as purchase history, location, gender, or behavioral actions (e.g., abandoned carts or product clicks).
- Use dynamic content: Incorporate sections within emails that change based on the recipient’s interests or behavior.
- Analyze customer data regularly: Stay updated on how customers interact with your emails, and tweak your segments accordingly.
Pro Tip: If you’re just getting started, try simple segmentation first — like sending separate emails to new vs. returning customers. You’ll see immediate results without overwhelming yourself.
## Mistake #2: Neglecting Subject Lines
Your subject line is the front door to your email — if it’s not inviting, no one will step inside. Yet, many marketers treat subject lines as an afterthought, resulting in low open rates.
Why This Is a Problem? If your subject line is too long, too vague, or too salesy, your email might land straight in the trash (or worse, the spam folder). Subject lines are the first thing recipients see, and they set the tone for the entire email experience.
How to Fix It
- Keep it short and sweet: Aim for subject lines with 6–10 words or fewer than 50 characters.
- Create urgency and curiosity: Use time-sensitive words or open-ended statements (e.g., “Don’t miss this offer!” or “Guess what’s inside?”).
- Test different variations: Use A/B testing to experiment with different subject lines and find what resonates best.
- Avoid spammy words: Words like “FREE,” “Buy Now,” or “Limited Time Offer” can trigger spam filters.
Pro Tip: Personalizing the subject line with the recipient’s name or recent activity (e.g., “John, your favorite shoes are back in stock!”) can significantly improve open rates. Here are a few good subject lines for cold emails that you can refer to.
## Mistake #3: Overloading Emails with Images and No Text
Sure, visuals are important, but going overboard with images and neglecting text can backfire. Many marketers fall into the trap of stuffing emails with graphics, GIFs, and photos, assuming they’ll catch more attention. Unfortunately, this can lead to accessibility issues and delivery problems.
Why This Is a Problem? Emails that are too image-heavy load slowly, especially on mobile devices. If the recipient is using an email client that blocks images by default, your message may not even be seen. Additionally, without proper alt text or fallback content, some subscribers might have no idea what your email is about!
How to Fix It
- Balance visuals with text: A good rule of thumb is a 60/40 text-to-image ratio. Use images to enhance, not replace, your message.
- Optimize images for fast loading: Compress your images and test how they load across different email platforms and devices.
- Add descriptive alt text: Provide meaningful alternative text for images so recipients know what’s there, even if the image doesn’t load.
- Use a plain-text version: Always offer a plain-text version of your email to accommodate recipients with slow connections or accessibility needs.
Pro Tip: Try using interactive elements like clickable buttons instead of relying only on visuals. This keeps the email engaging without compromising load speed.
## Mistake #4: Sending Emails Without a Clear Call-to-Action (CTA)
Ever opened an email and thought, “What do they want me to do?” That’s the result of a vague or missing call-to-action (CTA). Many marketers make the mistake of focusing too much on content and forgetting to guide the reader toward the next step.
Why This Is a Problem? If your email doesn’t contain a clear, actionable next step, readers will feel lost. Without a proper CTA, even the most engaging email won’t drive conversions. Whether it’s making a purchase, signing up for an event, or reading a blog post, your audience needs a nudge in the right direction.
How to Fix It
- Try Video CTA: Want to drive engagement with compelling CTAs? Use Potion to embed dynamic AI personalized videos into your emails. These videos can prompt viewers with a clear call-to-action, like scheduling a meeting or visiting a landing page, right from the video interface — making it easy for subscribers to take the next step.
- Use one primary CTA: Stick to a single, prominent CTA to avoid confusing the reader. Multiple CTAs dilute the focus and reduce effectiveness.
- Make it action-oriented: Use verbs that encourage action, like “Shop Now,” “Learn More,” or “Join the Webinar.”
- Place CTAs strategically: Ensure the CTA button or link is visible above the fold and repeated at least once later in the email.
- Use contrasting colors: Make your CTA stand out by using colors that grab attention without clashing with your brand’s design.
Pro Tip: Test your CTAs by changing the wording slightly. For example, switching from “Subscribe” to “Get Updates” can make a noticeable difference in click-through rates.
## Mistake #5: Failing to Optimize Emails for Mobile Devices
In today’s world, most people check their emails on their phones — so failing to optimize for mobile is a rookie mistake. If your email looks awkward on mobile or forces recipients to zoom in, you can bet they’ll exit it faster than you can say, “Email unsubscribe.”
Why This Is a Problem? Emails that aren’t optimized for mobile can appear broken, with images out of place and text too small to read. This not only frustrates readers but also negatively impacts click-through rates and conversions. A clunky mobile experience can make your brand seem unprofessional.
How to Fix It
- Use a responsive email design: Choose email templates that automatically adjust to different screen sizes.
- Stick to single-column layouts: Multi-column layouts can look messy on small screens. A single-column design ensures everything stays in place.
- Optimize fonts and buttons: Use at least 14px for body text and ensure buttons are large enough for easy tapping.
- Preview your email on mobile: Test how the email looks on various devices and email clients before hitting send.
Pro Tip: Emails with concise subject lines perform better on mobile since long subject lines get cut off. Keep your subject line under 30 characters for mobile-friendly readability.
## Mistake #6: Ignoring the Power of Email Analytics
If you’re not tracking the performance of your email campaigns, you’re flying blind. Too many marketers hit “send” and hope for the best, neglecting valuable insights that analytics can provide.
Why This Is a Problem? Without tracking data like open rates, click-through rates, and unsubscribe rates, you have no way of knowing what’s working — or what’s not. Ignoring analytics means you’re missing out on opportunities to optimize and improve future campaigns.
How to Fix It
- Track key metrics: Keep an eye on metrics like open rates, bounce rates, and conversion rates to measure performance.
- Use A/B testing: Test different subject lines, email designs, and send times to see what resonates best with your audience.
- Monitor engagement over time: Identify trends in engagement to determine which content and formats your audience prefers.
- Act on the data: If a campaign performs poorly, dig into the analytics to find out why — and adjust your strategy accordingly.
Pro Tip: Pay attention to unsubscribe rates. A sudden spike may indicate that your email content or frequency isn’t aligned with subscriber expectations. Take corrective action before it becomes a trend.
## Mistake #7: Bombarding Subscribers with Too Many Emails
Nobody likes an inbox flooded with emails from the same sender. Over-emailing your audience is one of the fastest ways to exhaust their patience and land yourself in the spam folder. You might think frequent emails keep your brand top of mind, but in reality, it can feel pushy and annoying.
Why This Is a Problem? When subscribers feel overwhelmed by too many emails, they are more likely to unsubscribe or mark your messages as spam. Email fatigue is real, and it can harm your reputation, leading to lower engagement and open rates over time.
How to Fix It
- Use smart follow-ups: Instead of sending multiple generic “text-only” emails, use AI sales tools like Potion to deliver personalized video follow-up emails at key moments. With Potion, you can automate personalized video sequences, reducing email volume while increasing relevance. This ensures your messages come across as thoughtful rather than overwhelming.
- Set a reasonable email frequency: Stick to an email cadence that adds value without overwhelming your audience — 1–2 emails per week is a safe starting point.
- Give subscribers control: Allow them to choose how often they want to hear from you via preference settings.
- Use automated workflows wisely: Ensure your automation sequences are spaced out and do not bombard the recipient with multiple emails on the same day.
- Monitor unsubscribe trends: Keep an eye on unsubscribe and spam complaint rates to gauge if you need to tone down the frequency.
Pro Tip: For seasonal or high-volume campaigns, give your audience a heads-up about receiving more emails. A little transparency goes a long way in keeping them engaged.
## Mistake #8: Sending Emails at the Wrong Time
Timing is everything! Sending emails at the wrong time — like on a Friday night or early Monday morning — can drastically reduce your chances of engagement. If your emails arrive when your audience isn’t in the right mindset to engage, they’ll likely go unopened or get buried under newer emails.
Why This Is a Problem? Sending emails without considering the recipient’s habits can result in poor open and click-through rates. People are more likely to engage with emails during certain hours or days, so missing that sweet spot means your message could go unnoticed.
How to Fix It
- Analyze the data: Use historical data to determine when your subscribers are most active.
- Segment by time zones: Schedule emails to align with the local time of your recipients for higher engagement.
- Experiment with A/B testing: Test different send times to identify when your audience is most responsive.
- Consider industry trends: In general, mid-morning on Tuesdays or Thursdays tends to perform well for many businesses, but your mileage may vary.
Pro Tip: If you’re targeting an international audience, use email automation tools that allow time zone-based delivery to ensure each recipient receives the email at the right moment.
## Mistake #9: Overlooking Email Personalization
No one likes to feel like they’re receiving a generic, mass-sent email. Yet, many marketers skip personalization, missing an easy opportunity to create stronger connections with their audience. Sending emails that feel cold and impersonal can damage trust and engagement.
Why This Is a Problem? A lack of personalization makes recipients feel like just another number on your list. When people feel unvalued, they’re more likely to ignore your emails — or worse, hit that “unsubscribe” button. Personalized emails, however, show that you understand and care about their needs.
How to Fix It
- Shift to video: Integrate Potion’s AI video personalization into your email strategy for next-level results. With Potion, you can generate AI videos that address each recipient by name and refer to specific interactions or preferences. Imagine sending an email that not only greets a subscriber by name but also showcases the exact product they were browsing — automatically!
- Use dynamic fields: Insert the recipient’s name, location, or other personalized details within the email body and subject lines.
- Leverage behavioral data: Personalize recommendations based on a user’s browsing or purchase history.
- Create targeted campaigns: Send different emails to customers based on where they are in the sales funnel.
- Celebrate milestones: Acknowledge customer anniversaries, birthdays, or loyalty program achievements with tailored messages.
Pro Tip: Personalization doesn’t have to stop at names — reference a recent product the recipient viewed or include helpful content based on their preferences. Small touches make a big impact!
## Mistake #10: Failing to Clean and Maintain Your Email List
How often do you clear out inactive subscribers or invalid email addresses from your mailing list? If the answer is “rarely” or “never,” you’re committing a common yet damaging mistake. Neglecting regular list maintenance can result in wasted efforts, poor engagement, and deliverability issues.
Why This Is a Problem? A bloated email list full of outdated or invalid contacts hurts your sender reputation. Internet service providers (ISPs) track how people engage with your emails — if too many bounce or go unopened, your future emails may land in spam. Worse, low engagement rates can skew your campaign analytics, giving you misleading insights.
How to Fix It
- Use email validation tools: Regularly clean your list to remove invalid or inactive addresses.
- Implement re-engagement campaigns: Send targeted emails to inactive subscribers to encourage them to engage again — or opt out if they’re no longer interested.
- Segment active vs. inactive users: Focus more effort on engaged subscribers for better results.
- Automate list hygiene: Set up rules to automatically remove or flag contacts who haven’t engaged within a set period, such as six months.
Pro Tip: Make it a habit to clean your list every 3–6 months. It’s better to have a smaller, active list than a massive one filled with ghost subscribers.
## Mistake #11: Using Too Many Links in a Single Email
We get it — there’s a lot you want your subscribers to see. But bombarding your emails with multiple links is more likely to confuse readers and discourage them from clicking any at all. Plus, it can make your email look suspicious to spam filters!
Why This Is a Problem? Too many links dilute the focus of your message and overwhelm readers with choices. Additionally, emails packed with links are often flagged as spam by ISPs. The more your email looks like a promotional gimmick rather than a helpful message, the worse your engagement rates will be.
How to Fix It
- Limit your email to one or two CTAs: Each email should have a clear purpose, with no more than two CTAs guiding the recipient.
- Use buttons strategically: Instead of stuffing your message with links, use clearly labeled buttons to encourage clicks.
- Check your links carefully: Ensure all links are relevant and working properly — broken links create a poor user experience.
- Test for spam triggers: Before sending, test your email with spam-check tools to ensure it passes through filters.
Pro Tip: If you need to share multiple resources, use a link to a landing page with curated content rather than cramming everything into one email. Less is more!
## Mistake #12: Forgetting to Include an Unsubscribe Option
It might seem counterintuitive, but giving people the option to leave your email list easily is essential. Forgetting to include an unsubscribe link — or worse, hiding it — can frustrate recipients and damage your brand reputation.
Why This Is a Problem? Not only is it illegal under laws like CAN-SPAM (in the US) and GDPR (in Europe), but making it hard to unsubscribe makes people resent your brand. Instead of engaging, they’ll likely mark your emails as spam. High spam complaint rates harm your sender reputation and can even get you blacklisted by ISPs.
How to Fix It
- Include a clear unsubscribe link: Place the link at the bottom of your email and make it easy to spot.
- Allow for preference management: Offer subscribers the chance to adjust their preferences (e.g., reduce email frequency) instead of unsubscribing entirely.
- Respect unsubscribes immediately: Ensure anyone who opts out is removed from your list promptly to comply with email regulations.
- Monitor unsubscribe trends: If you notice a sudden spike, dig into the cause — your frequency, content, or targeting may need adjustments.
Pro Tip: Consider including a cheeky, lighthearted message alongside your unsubscribe link (e.g., “We’ll miss you! But you can always come back.”) to leave a positive impression.
## Mistake #13: Not Testing Emails Before Sending
Sending an email without testing it first is like playing darts blindfolded — you’re hoping it lands where it should, but there’s a good chance it won’t. Many marketers skip testing their emails, only to discover too late that the design is broken, the links are incorrect, or the formatting looks messy on certain devices.
Why This Is a Problem? Emails display differently across various devices and email clients (like Gmail, Outlook, or Apple Mail). If you don’t test them beforehand, your carefully crafted message might appear disjointed, with images out of alignment or buttons that don’t work. Poorly formatted emails can frustrate recipients and lead to lost engagement.
How to Fix It
- Preview emails on multiple platforms: Test how your email looks on mobile, desktop, and tablets, as well as in major email clients.
- Send test emails to your team: Get feedback from colleagues to ensure everything looks perfect before the campaign goes live.
- Check for broken links and typos: Even minor errors can make your brand appear unprofessional.
- Use spam-testing tools: These tools simulate how your email will be treated by spam filters and offer suggestions to improve deliverability.
Pro Tip: Create a checklist of things to review (like alt text, broken links, and formatting) before hitting “send.” This will save you from future headaches!
## Mistake #14: Overusing Automation Without Personal Touch
While automation is a marketer’s best friend, relying too heavily on it without adding personal touches can make your emails feel robotic. Your audience can easily tell when they’re part of a generic automation sequence, and it often results in lower engagement and higher unsubscribes.
Why This Is a Problem? Email automation is great for efficiency, but overusing it without tailoring messages to specific customer behaviors and needs makes your communication feel impersonal. It can alienate subscribers, making them feel like just another number on your list instead of valued individuals.
How to Fix It
- Add personalization wherever possible: Use dynamic fields to insert personal details, like names and past purchases, into your emails.
- Incorporate behavior-triggered emails: Instead of relying on time-based automation alone, send emails based on specific actions (e.g., a follow-up after a purchase or browsing activity).
- Use friendly and natural language: Even automated emails should feel like they’re coming from a person, not a bot.
- Regularly review and tweak email sequences: Keep your content fresh and ensure it aligns with changing customer expectations.
Pro Tip: Occasionally send a manual email that feels like a personal check-in. This adds a human touch and strengthens the relationship with your audience.
## Mistake #15: Failing to Provide Value in Every Email
If your emails are all about selling and not about offering value, your subscribers will quickly lose interest. Many marketers make the mistake of focusing solely on promotions and offers, forgetting that valuable content is what keeps audiences engaged in the long run.
Why This Is a Problem? Email marketing isn’t just about transactions — it’s about building relationships. If your emails are always about “buy this” or “act now,” your audience will grow tired of the sales-heavy approach. Over time, they’ll stop engaging, and your unsubscribe rate will increase.
How to Fix It
- Provide a mix of content: Balance promotional messages with educational, entertaining, or informative content.
- Use Video: Deliver more value by integrating personalized AI videos using Potion. Instead of sending static emails, offer video demos, personalized product walkthroughs, or welcome videos. Subscribers are more likely to engage with valuable, personalized video content, keeping them hooked and reducing unsubscribe rates.
- Offer exclusive value: Send sneak peeks, free resources, or early access to new products to make your subscribers feel special.
- Curate useful tips or advice: For example, if you sell fitness gear, share workout tips or nutrition advice in your emails.
- Use storytelling to connect: People love stories — whether it’s a customer success story or a behind-the-scenes peek at your brand.
Pro Tip: Think of the 80/20 rule — 80% of your emails should offer value, while only 20% should focus on promotions. This keeps your audience hooked and prevents email fatigue.
## Mistake #16: Ignoring Email Accessibility
Accessibility often flies under the radar in email marketing, but neglecting it limits your audience and sends a message that not everyone is welcome. Marketers who skip accessibility guidelines inadvertently make it hard for people with disabilities to interact with their emails, causing frustration and lost opportunities for engagement.
Why This Is a Problem? Emails that aren’t accessible can alienate a significant portion of your audience. If visually impaired users can’t read your email or navigate it easily, they’re less likely to engage. Accessibility also impacts email deliverability, as some providers give preference to well-optimized content.
How to Fix It
- Use descriptive alt text: Add alt text to all images so recipients using screen readers know what each image represents.
- Optimize for screen readers: Ensure the HTML structure of your emails is simple and easy to navigate. Avoid placing text inside images.
- Use high contrast colors: Make sure your email is easy to read, even for people with visual impairments.
- Provide a plain-text version: Offering a plain-text alternative ensures all recipients can access your content, even on devices with limited capabilities.
Pro Tip: Test your emails with accessibility tools or screen readers to ensure they provide a smooth user experience for all recipients.
## Mistake #17: Skipping Welcome Emails for New Subscribers
First impressions count, and failing to send a welcome email is a missed opportunity to set the tone for your relationship with new subscribers. Some marketers add people to their list and wait for the next scheduled campaign, losing the chance to make that crucial initial connection.
Why This Is a Problem? When someone subscribes, they’re most engaged at that moment. If you don’t acknowledge them right away, they might forget they even signed up! Welcome emails have some of the highest open and click-through rates, so skipping them means you’re leaving money — and trust — on the table.
How to Fix It
- Set up automated welcome emails: Send a friendly welcome message as soon as someone subscribes.
- Introduce your brand: Let new subscribers know what to expect from your emails (e.g., type of content and frequency).
- Provide a valuable offer: Consider including a discount code or free resource to kick off the relationship on a positive note.
- Encourage engagement early: Ask a simple question, invite them to follow you on social media, or share helpful links in the first email.
Pro Tip: A welcome email series (2–3 emails spread over a few days) works even better. Start with a greeting, follow up with a story, and end with a special offer to keep them hooked.
## Mistake #18: Relying Too Much on Images and Neglecting Email Copy
While visual content plays a role in making your emails look appealing, focusing too much on images at the expense of good copy is a common mistake. Some marketers design flashy emails with minimal or weak text, assuming visuals alone will drive engagement.
Why This Is a Problem? Images can enhance your message, but they don’t replace clear, persuasive text. Many email clients block images by default, so if your email relies entirely on visuals, recipients might miss the message. Strong, engaging copy is essential for driving conversions, especially when images fail to load.
How to Fix It
- Write compelling, concise copy: Use engaging language to convey your message clearly, even if images don’t load.
- Balance visuals and text: Ensure that your email makes sense with or without the images. Aim for a 60/40 text-to-image ratio.
- Incorporate clear headlines and subheadings: These guide readers through the email and improve readability.
- Use actionable language: Make your copy irresistible with CTAs that compel readers to click and engage.
Pro Tip: Think of images as supporting actors and the copy as the lead — both should complement each other, but it’s the words that do the heavy lifting in your emails.
## Mistake #19: Ignoring Email Deliverability Issues
You might have the most beautifully designed email, but if it never makes it to your recipient’s inbox, it’s all for nothing. Many marketers don’t pay attention to email deliverability, assuming that if they hit “send,” the message will land safely. Unfortunately, poor practices can lead to emails getting flagged by spam filters or blocked entirely.
Why This Is a Problem? Deliverability issues can kill your email campaign before it even begins. If your sender reputation takes a hit, future emails will have a harder time reaching the inbox. Factors like using purchased lists, inconsistent sending patterns, and triggering spam filters can seriously harm deliverability.
How to Fix It
- Authenticate your domain: Use SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication to prove to ISPs that your emails are legitimate.
- Warm up your domain: If you’re new to email marketing, gradually increase your sending volume to build a good reputation.
- Avoid spam trigger words: Words like “Buy now” or “Act fast” can get your emails flagged as spam.
- Monitor your sender reputation: Use tools like Google Postmaster to keep tabs on your domain’s health.
Pro Tip: Always use a double opt-in process for building your email list. This ensures that your subscribers genuinely want to hear from you, improving your deliverability rate over time. Here’s how you can improve your email deliverability.
## Mistake #20: Not Refreshing Email Campaigns Regularly
Reusing the same campaigns and templates over and over can lead to email fatigue. Some marketers get comfortable with what worked in the past and forget to innovate, resulting in campaigns that start to feel stale. Your audience will notice — and disengage — if your emails don’t evolve with their changing interests.
Why This Is a Problem? Subscribers can quickly lose interest if your emails become predictable. Over time, your engagement rates will drop, and your audience will tune out. Failing to refresh your strategy also means you’re missing out on opportunities to experiment with new trends, formats, and messaging that could resonate better.
How to Fix It
- Update templates and visuals regularly: Give your emails a fresh look every few months to keep things exciting.
- Experiment with new formats: Try interactive elements like polls, quizzes, or animated GIFs to surprise your audience.
- Rotate subject lines: Even subtle changes in subject lines can make a difference in open rates.
- Gather subscriber feedback: Ask your audience what they’d like to see more (or less) of and adjust your campaigns accordingly.
Pro Tip: Create seasonal campaigns that align with holidays, events, or industry trends. This keeps your emails relevant and timely, which increases engagement.
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: How many links should I include in an email?
It’s best to limit your email to one or two CTAs. Too many links can confuse readers and trigger spam filters. If you have multiple resources to share, consider linking to a curated landing page instead of overloading the email.
## Q: What’s the best way to re-engage inactive subscribers?
Run re-engagement campaigns by sending targeted messages to inactive subscribers. Offer exclusive content, use personalized video emails or incentives to encourage interaction. If they still don’t engage, consider removing them from your list to keep your audience fresh and active.
## Q: What tools can I use to test my emails before sending?
Use AI email marketing tools like Litmus or Email on Acid to preview your emails across devices and email clients. Spam-check tools can simulate how your email will be treated by ISPs, helping you catch deliverability issues early. Send test emails to your team to catch formatting or link errors before launch.
## Q: How can I avoid email fatigue among subscribers?
To avoid email fatigue:
- Segment your audience and send relevant content.
- Adjust sending frequency based on engagement data.
- Mix promotional emails with valuable content like tips, stories, or resources.
- Provide preference settings so subscribers control how often they receive emails.
Transparency is key — notify your audience if you plan to increase email frequency during certain periods, like sales or holidays.
## Q: What’s the ideal subject line length?
Subject lines should ideally be 6–10 words or under 50 characters to ensure they display properly across devices and grab attention. For mobile devices, aim for 30 characters or less to prevent the subject from getting cut off.
## Q: How can I effectively personalize emails beyond just using the subscriber’s name?
Personalization goes way beyond addressing someone by their first name. Here are some ways to make your emails more relevant and engaging:
- Behavioral triggers: Send follow-up emails based on specific actions (e.g., abandoned carts, browsing activity).
- Dynamic product recommendations: Suggest products or content based on the subscriber’s past purchases or website visits.
- Location-based personalization: Promote events, offers, or shipping discounts relevant to the recipient’s region.
- Anniversary or milestone emails: Celebrate a subscriber’s birthday, customer anniversary, or membership milestones with a special offer.
- Content preferences: Offer segmented newsletters based on the recipient’s chosen topics of interest.
Pro Tip: Personalized emails that acknowledge recent activity or preferences show subscribers that you understand and care about their unique needs. This goes a long way in building brand loyalty.
## Conclusion
Mastering email marketing isn’t rocket science — it’s about paying attention to the details and avoiding common mistakes that can quietly sabotage your campaigns. Whether it’s fine-tuning your subject lines, segmenting your audience, or ensuring every email offers value, small changes can make a big difference.
The key takeaway? Email marketing works best when it’s personal, strategic, and intentional. Avoiding these common email marketing mistakes can transform your campaigns from mediocre to exceptional.
Remember, email marketing is a relationship-building tool, not just a promotional channel. Respect your audience’s preferences, keep experimenting with new ideas, and use analytics to fine-tune your efforts.
If you’re looking for an edge in email marketing, Potion can help you stand out. With personalized video marketing that capture attention, drive engagement, and build relationships, Potion takes email marketing to the next level. Use it to avoid common pitfalls, improve marketing personalization, and make every email interaction meaningful and memorable.
With consistent attention to best practices, your emails will stop getting lost in inboxes and start generating high ticket sales, engagement, loyalty, and conversions you aim for.
Now it’s your turn! Use these insights to audit your current email strategy, fix the cracks, and create campaigns that stand out in crowded inboxes. Success is within reach — all it takes is a little adjustment and attention to what truly matters. Happy emailing! 🚀

text:
In today’s digital age, email marketing remains a powerful tool for businesses to connect with their audience and drive conversions. However, with the increasing competition and evolving consumer expectations, staying ahead of the curve is crucial.
Email marketing may seem like old news, but it’s still one of the most effective tools for engaging customers. With all the digital noise, crafting emails that stand out is no small feat. If you’ve ever wondered how to improve email campaigns, you’re not alone!
The key isn’t just sending more emails but sending smarter emails.
Ready to dive into some game-changing strategies? Let’s explore ways to improve your email marketing and make every campaign count.
## Ways on How to Improve Email Marketing Campaigns for Unbeatable Results
## 1. Personalize Your Emails
Personalization isn’t just a buzzword — it’s a powerful strategy that can transform how your audience views your emails. Gone are the days of generic, one-size-fits-all email blasts. Customers expect more, and when you deliver personalized content, you create a stronger connection.
How does it work? Personalized emails use data to tailor content to each subscriber’s preferences. You can use names, past purchase behavior, location, or even browsing history to craft emails that speak directly to them.
Examples of Personalization
- Subject Lines: Simply adding someone’s name in the subject line increases the chances of them opening the email. Instead of “Exclusive Offer Inside,” try “John, Don’t Miss Your Exclusive Offer!”
- Product Recommendations: Based on a subscriber’s previous interactions with your site, suggest products they may like. For example, “We noticed you were browsing sneakers. Check out these trending styles!”
- Location-Based Content: If you know where your customer lives, you can send them deals relevant to their region or notify them about events happening nearby.
Take personalization a step further by incorporating personalized video messages in your emails. Video adds a personal touch that text alone can’t achieve, building a deeper emotional connection with your audience. Video personalization tools like Potion allow you to create video with AI that dynamically adjust based on recipient data — think personalized greetings or tailored product recommendations within videos. This approach makes your emails feel like a one-on-one conversation, driving engagement and loyalty.
Pro Tip: Use dynamic content! Dynamic content lets you create one email with different variations depending on the recipient. For instance, if you’re promoting an online sale, customers in colder climates might see winter gear while others see summer products.
Why Personalization Matters?
It’s simple: people like to feel special! By addressing their needs and preferences, you build trust and loyalty, which translates to higher engagement rates.
## 2. Segment Your Email List
Another sure-fire way to improve your email marketing is to segment your email list. When you segment your subscribers into specific groups, you can send tailored messages that are more relevant and engaging.
What is Email Segmentation? Segmentation is the practice of dividing your email list into smaller, more defined categories based on demographics, behaviors, or preferences. This approach allows you to send more targeted emails, boosting open rates and conversions.
Ways to Segment Your List
- Demographic Data: Age, gender, or location are great starting points. For instance, if you’re a clothing retailer, you might want to send different emails to men and women.
- Purchase History: Send emails based on what customers have already bought. Did they buy a laptop? Offer accessories like a case or extra chargers.
- Engagement Level: Not everyone on your list is equally active. For those who haven’t opened your emails in a while, send a re-engagement campaign. For your loyal readers, offer exclusive discounts.
Pro Tip: Test your segments; don’t assume one method of segmentation works for all businesses. Test different segments to see which ones lead to the highest open and click-through rates. Over time, you’ll learn which group responds best to what type of message.
Why Segmentation Works? When people get emails that are relevant to them, they’re more likely to open and engage with the content. In fact, studies have shown that segmented campaigns can increase revenue by up to 760%. It’s a powerful way to connect with your audience!
## 3. Craft Compelling Subject Lines
Your subject line is the first impression of your email — make it count! It doesn’t matter how amazing your content is if no one opens the email in the first place. A killer subject line can dramatically improve your open rates and overall campaign success.
What Makes a Good Subject Line? It needs to be intriguing but clear. A good subject line should spark curiosity, create urgency, or offer value, all while keeping it short and sweet. Aim for around 40–50 characters to make sure it’s fully visible on mobile devices. For inspiration, here are a few examples of good subject lines for cold emails.
Tips for Writing Better Subject Lines
- Be Direct: Don’t beat around the bush — tell them what they’re getting. “50% Off Your Favorite Products — Today Only!”
- Create Urgency: Fear of missing out (FOMO) is real! Use it to your advantage by adding urgency. “Last Chance to Get Free Shipping!”
- Ask a Question: Engage curiosity by asking questions. “Looking for the Perfect Gift?”
- Use Emojis (Sparingly): Emojis can make your subject line stand out in a crowded inbox, but don’t overdo it. Use them to add personality: “🎉 Big Sale Inside! Don’t Miss Out!”
Pro Tip: Don’t just rely on guesswork — A/B test different subject lines to see which performs better. By experimenting with variations, you can discover what resonates most with your audience.
Why It’s Crucial A well-crafted subject line makes the difference between an email that’s opened and one that’s deleted without a second thought. Think of it as the hook that reels in your audience!
## 4. Optimize for Mobile
Let’s face it: people are glued to their phones. Whether they’re checking emails during their commute or while waiting in line for coffee, mobile devices are how most people read their emails these days. If your emails aren’t optimized for mobile, you could be missing out on a huge chunk of your audience.
Why Mobile Optimization Matters? More than half of all email opens happen on mobile devices. That means if your emails look wonky on a small screen — tiny text, images that don’t load, or links that are impossible to click — people won’t stick around. They’ll hit that delete button faster than you can say “unsubscribe.”
Tips for Mobile Optimization
- Use a Responsive Design: Make sure your email design adapts to any screen size. Most modern email marketing platforms offer responsive templates, so take advantage of them.
- Shorten Subject Lines: On mobile, space is limited. Keep your subject lines punchy and to the point. Aim for around 30–40 characters for mobile-friendly subject lines.
- Use Large Fonts and Buttons: Small text can be hard to read on mobile, and tiny buttons? Forget about it. Use a minimum of 14-point font for body text and make buttons large enough for people to click with their thumbs.
- Reduce Image Size: Large images can slow down load times on mobile devices. Compress images to speed things up, and make sure they look good even if they don’t load.
Pro Tip: Just because an email looks great on your phone doesn’t mean it will on others. Test your emails on a variety of devices and email clients to ensure they work well across the board.
Why It Works? Optimizing your emails for mobile improves user experience, increases open rates, and makes it easier for people to take action, whether that’s clicking a link or making a purchase.
## 5. Add a Clear Call to Action (CTA)
You’ve captured your audience’s attention with a great subject line, personalized content, and stunning design — now what? Every email needs a clear, compelling call to action (CTA). Without it, your readers are left wondering what to do next. And guess what? They’ll probably do nothing.
What Makes a Good CTA? A good CTA is short, direct, and action-oriented. It tells your readers exactly what to do next, whether that’s clicking a link, downloading a resource, or making a purchase. And don’t be afraid to be bold! Using action verbs like “Shop Now,” “Get Started,” or “Claim Your Discount” can encourage more clicks.
Tips for Crafting Effective CTAs
- Make It Stand Out: Your CTA should be the most visually prominent element in your email. Use contrasting colors, bold text, or large buttons to draw attention to it.
- Create a Sense of Urgency: Adding urgency to your CTA can boost conversion rates. Phrases like “Limited Time Offer” or “Don’t Miss Out” can motivate readers to act fast.
- Be Specific: Vague CTAs won’t cut it. Instead of saying “Click Here,” go for something specific like “Download Your Free Guide” or “Start Your Free Trial.”
- Limit the Number of CTAs: Don’t overwhelm your readers with too many choices. Ideally, stick to one or two CTAs per email to keep the focus clear.
Pro Tip: While one CTA is great, placing it in multiple locations can increase the chances of someone clicking through. Try adding one near the top and another towards the bottom of your email for maximum exposure.
Why It Works? A clear, well-placed CTA eliminates confusion and guides readers toward taking the next step. When done right, it can significantly boost your click-through and conversion rates.
## 6. Use Behavioral Triggers
Want to send emails that arrive at just the right moment? Behavioral triggers are a powerful way to engage your audience when they’re most likely to take action. Instead of sending emails on a set schedule, behavioral-triggered emails are automatically sent based on specific actions your subscribers take — or don’t take.
What Are Behavioral Triggers? Behavioral triggers are actions or events that prompt an automated email to be sent. For example, when someone signs up for your newsletter, they might immediately receive a welcome email. Or if a customer abandons their shopping cart, you can send a follow-up email reminding them to complete their purchase.
Triggered emails become even more effective when enhanced with video. For example, instead of a standard shopping cart abandonment solution, you could send a personalized video message encouraging the recipient to complete their purchase. Potion makes it simple to create and automate such personalized video messages. Thus, ensuring you connect with customers when they’re most engaged. Whether it’s a welcome video or a post-purchase thank-you, Potion’s AI-driven platform helps you craft timely, relevant content with minimal effort.
Examples of Triggered Emails
- Welcome Emails: Greet new subscribers the moment they sign up with a warm welcome message.
- Abandoned Cart Emails: Remind customers about the items they left behind in their shopping cart and encourage them to complete their purchase.
- Post-Purchase Emails: Send follow-up emails after a customer makes a purchase to thank them, request feedback, or suggest complementary products.
- Re-Engagement Emails: If a subscriber hasn’t interacted with your emails in a while, send them a re-engagement email to reignite their interest.
Pro Tip: You don’t have to send triggered emails immediately. For example, if a customer hasn’t completed their purchase after 24 hours, you can send a “last chance” reminder. Using time delays strategically can improve the effectiveness of your emails.
Why It Works? Behavioral triggers allow you to reach your audience when they’re most engaged, increasing the likelihood that they’ll open your email and take action. It’s like having perfect timing — every time!
## 7. Test and Refine Your Emails (A/B Testing)
Email marketing isn’t a set-it-and-forget-it game — what worked last month might not work today. That’s where A/B testing (also called split testing) comes into play. A/B testing allows you to experiment with different elements of your email, so you can figure out what works best for your audience and improve over time.
What is A/B Testing? A/B testing is when you send two versions of an email to small segments of your audience to see which one performs better. You can test anything from subject lines to email layout, images, or CTA buttons. Once you find a winner, send that version to the rest of your list.
What Can You A/B Test?
- Subject Lines & Preview Texts: Test different approaches — try one that’s direct and another that’s playful or mysterious. See which style resonates more with your readers.
- Email Copy: Does a longer, more detailed email perform better than a short, snappy one? You won’t know until you test it!
- Images vs. No Images: Some audiences respond well to visually-driven emails, while others prefer text-heavy content. Find out what works best for yours.
- Send Times: Does your audience engage more when you send emails in the morning or the evening? Testing different times can help you land in that sweet spot.
Pro Tip: For accurate results, stick to testing one variable at a time. If you change both the subject line and the layout, you won’t know which change led to better performance. Keep it simple and track your results over time.
Why It Works? A/B testing helps you fine-tune your emails based on real data rather than guesswork. Over time, you’ll learn exactly what drives your audience to engage, resulting in better open rates, click-throughs, and conversions.
## 8. Focus on Deliverability
You can craft the best email in the world, but if it doesn’t land in your subscriber’s inbox, it’s all for nothing. That’s why improving email deliverability is crucial to the success of your campaigns. Deliverability is the ability of your emails to reach your recipients’ inboxes without getting caught in spam filters or blocked entirely.
What Affects Email Deliverability? A lot goes into ensuring your emails land where they’re supposed to. Here are some factors that influence deliverability:
- Sender Reputation: Internet service providers (ISPs) track the reputation of your sending domain and IP address. If your emails get marked as spam too often, your reputation suffers, making it harder to reach inboxes.
- Content: Certain words, phrases, or symbols (like “FREE!!!!”) can trigger spam filters, sending your emails straight to the junk folder.
- Engagement Rates: ISPs also look at how recipients engage with your emails. If people are consistently ignoring, deleting, or marking your emails as spam, that hurts your deliverability.
Tips for Improving Deliverability
- Authenticate Your Domain: Set up proper email authentication protocols, like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, to prove your emails are legitimate and reduce the chance of getting flagged as spam.
- Clean Your Email List Regularly: Having inactive or invalid email addresses on your list can hurt your reputation. Regularly remove hard bounces and disengaged users.
- Avoid Spammy Phrases: Be mindful of the words you use in your subject lines and body text. Avoid using all caps, excessive punctuation, or overly promotional language that might trigger spam filters.
- Ask Subscribers to Whitelist You: Encourage your subscribers to add your email address to their address book or safe sender list. This helps ensure your emails land in their inbox rather than the spam folder.
Pro Tip: Use tools to track key deliverability metrics like bounce rates, spam complaints, and open rates. If you notice a sudden drop in performance, dig into the data to find out why.
Why It Works? By focusing on deliverability, you ensure your emails reach their intended destination, increasing the chances of engagement and reducing the risk of being marked as spam.
## 9. Create Engaging, Value-Packed Content
People sign up for your email list because they expect something valuable in return. And if you’re not delivering on that promise, they’ll either unsubscribe or, even worse, just ignore your emails. That’s why focusing on creating engaging, value-packed content is key to improving your email marketing.
What Does Value-Packed Content Look Like? Value-packed content is content that offers your subscribers something useful, entertaining, or educational. It’s not about pushing your products 24/7 — it’s about building a relationship with your audience by giving them content that matters to them.
Types of Engaging Content
- Educational Resources: Share tips, how-to guides, or insights that help your readers solve a problem. For instance, if you run a fitness brand, send out weekly workout plans or nutrition tips.
- Exclusive Offers: Reward your subscribers with special deals or early access to new products. Make them feel like they’re part of an exclusive club.
- Interactive Content: Add quizzes, polls, or surveys to your emails to engage your audience. People love interactive content because it gives them a chance to participate.
- Behind-the-Scenes Looks: Share behind-the-scenes content from your business. Whether it’s how you create your products or a sneak peek of upcoming projects, this helps build a deeper connection with your audience.
Pro Tip: People are busy and won’t read long paragraphs of text. Use headings, bullet points, and short, punchy sentences to make your emails easy to read and digest. Remember: the more value you can deliver in a short amount of time, the better!
Why It Works? When you provide consistent value through your emails, your subscribers will not only open your messages but also look forward to them. This builds trust and increases engagement over time, leading to higher conversion rates.
## 10. Leverage Automation for Consistent Engagement
Staying top-of-mind with your audience can be challenging, especially when managing multiple campaigns at once. That’s where email automation comes into play. Automation allows you to set up emails triggered by specific actions, ensuring your audience receives the right message at the right time without manually hitting send.
What is Email Automation? Email automation involves pre-scheduling a series of emails to be sent based on user behavior, preferences, or other triggers. This could include welcome emails, birthday discounts, or follow-ups after a purchase. Think of it as your marketing assistant, working behind the scenes to nurture your leads and keep customers engaged.
Examples of Automated Email Campaigns
- Welcome Series: When someone signs up for your newsletter or creates an account, send a series of welcome emails to introduce your brand, highlight key products or services, and establish trust from the get-go.
- Re-engagement Campaigns: If subscribers haven’t opened your emails in a while, an automated re-engagement campaign can help win them back. You can ask if they still want to receive your emails or offer a special incentive to draw them back in.
- Drip Campaigns: Drip campaigns send a series of emails over time based on a user’s actions or stage in the sales funnel. For instance, if someone downloads a white paper, they could receive follow-up emails offering related resources or product demos.
Pro Tip: Don’t let opportunities slip through the cracks. Use automation to send upsell or cross-sell emails based on a customer’s previous purchases. If someone just bought a new laptop, why not send them a follow-up email offering a discounted case or accessories?
With tools like Potion, automation isn’t limited to text-based emails. You can set up automated video campaigns to engage your audience at key moments. From customer onboarding videos sent to new clients to re-engagement videos for dormant subscribers, Potion allows you to create AI-generated, personalized video content that runs on autopilot. This ensures consistent engagement while freeing you up to focus on other strategic tasks.
Why It Works? Automation helps you stay connected with your audience in a consistent and scalable way, ensuring no one slips through the cracks. It also frees up time for you to focus on strategy rather than execution, while boosting engagement and conversions.
## 11. Craft Killer Preheaders
While the subject line gets most of the attention, the preheader text is equally important in getting your emails noticed and opened. The preheader is the short summary text that appears next to or below your subject line in the inbox. It’s your second chance to grab attention and entice your audience to open the email.
Why Preheaders Matter? Think of the preheader as a sneak peek into the content of your email. If your subject line catches someone’s eye, the preheader can seal the deal by giving them a reason to click. On mobile devices, preheaders are especially important since they are often visible right beneath the subject line.
Tips for Writing Effective Preheaders
- Complement the Subject Line: Your preheader should work hand-in-hand with your subject line to create curiosity. For example, if your subject line says, “Flash Sale! 24 Hours Only,” your preheader could say, “Don’t miss 50% off sitewide today only.”
- Keep It Short and Sweet: Like subject lines, preheaders need to be brief. Aim for around 40–60 characters to ensure they display correctly on both desktop and mobile devices.
- Use Emojis Sparingly: Adding a well-placed emoji can help your preheader stand out in crowded inboxes, but don’t go overboard. Too many can make your email seem unprofessional or gimmicky.
- Create Urgency: Just like with subject lines, adding a sense of urgency or exclusivity to your preheader can increase open rates. For instance, “Only a few hours left to claim your discount!”
Pro Tip: Instead of duplicating your subject line in the preheader, use it as an opportunity to expand on the message or tease the content inside. Think of the preheader as the cherry on top of your email — just enough to pique curiosity but not so much that it gives everything away.
Why It Works? A well-crafted preheader can make the difference between your email being opened or ignored. When used effectively, it can boost your open rates and get more eyes on your content, increasing the chances of conversions.
## 12. Create a Consistent Email Schedule
Timing is everything in email marketing. If you’re inconsistent with when you send your emails — either bombarding your subscribers one week and going silent the next — you risk losing their attention or, worse, prompting them to unsubscribe. A consistent email schedule helps set expectations with your audience and keeps your brand top of mind without overwhelming them.
How to Create a Consistent Email Schedule?
- Find Your Optimal Send Time: Different audiences engage with emails at different times. Use data to find when your audience is most likely to open and engage with your emails. For instance, some audiences may be more responsive to emails sent in the morning, while others prefer afternoon or evening sends.
- Stick to a Regular Frequency: Whether you’re sending emails weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly, consistency is key. Once you establish a cadence, stick to it. Subscribers appreciate knowing when they can expect to hear from you, and it builds trust over time.
- Balance Frequency and Value: Don’t send emails just for the sake of it. Each email should provide value, whether it’s an exclusive offer, a useful tip, or important news. If you’re sending too many emails without meaningful content, you’ll likely see a drop in engagement or an uptick in unsubscribes.
- Use an Editorial Calendar: To keep track of your email schedule, consider creating an editorial calendar. This will help you plan your content in advance and ensure you’re sending out emails regularly without scrambling at the last minute.
Pro Tip: Research has shown that certain days and times tend to result in higher open and click-through rates. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are often the best days to send emails, with late morning (around 10–11 AM) being the sweet spot for engagement. However, every audience is different, so don’t forget to test what works best for yours!
Why It Works? Consistency builds trust. When your subscribers know they can rely on you to provide value at regular intervals, they’re more likely to stay engaged and open your emails. A well-planned schedule also ensures you’re staying relevant and top-of-mind without annoying your audience with too many emails.
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: How often should I send emails to my subscribers?
There’s no one-size-fits-all answer — it depends on your audience and the value of your content. A general recommendation is to start with 1–2 emails per week. The key is to be consistent and provide value with each email, ensuring you don’t overwhelm your audience. Additionally, ensure that you follow the necessary professional email etiquette rules.
## Q: What’s the difference between email segmentation and personalization?
Segmentation divides your email list into smaller groups based on shared characteristics (like demographics or purchase history). Marketing personalization, on the other hand, tailors individual messages within those segments using specific details such as the recipient’s name or behavior. The two strategies work together to create targeted and relevant emails.
## Q: How can personalized videos improve customer engagement?
By catering directly to the viewer’s interests, personalized video marketing fosters a sense of connection and relevance. This increases open rates, click-through rates, and watch times. Thus, resulting in deeper engagement and better overall campaign performance.
## Q: How can I avoid my video emails landing in the spam folder?
To improve video email deliverability, authenticate your domain using SPF, DKIM, and DMARC protocols, avoid spammy words (like “FREE” or excessive punctuation), and clean your email list regularly. Also, encourage recipients to whitelist your email address for better inbox placement. To learn more, follow the tips shared in this guide on how to keep video emails out of spam.
## Q: What is email segmentation based on engagement?
Segmentation based on engagement divides your audience into groups based on how they interact with your emails. For example:
- Highly engaged: Frequent openers and clickers
- Moderately engaged: Occasional interactions
- Disengaged: No interactions for a long time
This segmentation helps you tailor campaigns — rewarding loyal subscribers, re-engaging dormant ones, and identifying segments for list cleaning.
## Q: How can I improve my email campaign’s click-through rate (CTR)?
Improving CTR involves a combination of strategies:
- Use clear and compelling CTAs
- Place links strategically throughout your email
- Personalize the content to make it relevant
- Optimize email layout for easy navigation
- Experiment with A/B testing to find what resonates most with your audience
## Q: What tools can I use for personalized video marketing?
Personalized video marketing software like Potion specializes in creating and distributing personalized AI videos. It offers features such as dynamic text, automated AI video generation, and integrations with CRM systems for smooth, targeted AI video outreach.
## Q: Is it possible to create personalized videos at scale?
Yes! With automation tools, personalized video marketing can scale efficiently. Video messaging software like Potion allows you to create templates where only specific details — like names or video backgrounds — change dynamically. This way, you can produce hundreds or thousands of videos quickly.
## Q: How can I prevent unsubscribes from increasing?
To minimize unsubscribes and improve email marketing engagement, you should:
- Ensure every email offers value to your readers.
- Don’t bombard subscribers with too many emails — find a balanced frequency.
- Provide content that aligns with subscribers’ interests and preferences.
- Offer an email preferences center, allowing subscribers to choose the types of emails they receive or how often.
Remember, a gradual decline in unsubscribes is a good indicator of improved email relevance and engagement.
## Conclusion
Improving your email marketing doesn’t have to be a guessing game. With these surefire ways to improve email marketing, you now have a toolkit of strategies to drive engagement. Each tip plays a key role, from personalization and segmentation to optimizing for mobile and leveraging automation.
But don’t stop there! As digital trends evolve, personalized video emails are becoming a game-changer in further boosting engagement. Adding personalized video content to your emails can create a unique experience that grabs attention and builds meaningful connections.

If you’re ready to level up your email marketing, explore the power of video messaging in business. Integrating dynamic, AI personalized video messages can transform how your audience interacts with your brand. AI email marketing tools like Potion make it easy to create custom AI videos that connect with your subscribers on a whole new level.
Apply the strategies shared in this guide, experiment with personalized video email tools, and watch your engagement soar. With consistency, creativity, and AI video generator tools like Potion, you’ll be well on your way to achieving outstanding results!
