text:
You’ve spent hours crafting the perfect video email, and you’re excited to send it out to your audience. But it doesn’t get through? Frustrating, right? The sad truth is, email spam filters are stricter than ever, and video emails are often prime candidates for getting flagged. If you’re wondering how to keep video emails out of spam — you’re not alone. Deliverability is a real challenge in today’s digital world. But with the right strategies, your video emails can make it into the inbox and not disappear into the spam abyss.
Video emails do offer a more engaging way to connect with your audience. But here’s the thing: what good is a brilliant video email if it never sees the light of day and gets buried in the spam folder? Whether you’re a marketer, a sales professional, or someone just trying to reach out, it’s vital to understand how to fix video email deliverability.
In this article, we’ll share what is video email deliverability, how to fix it, and practical tips on how to keep your video emails out of spam. Ready to boost your email game? Let’s dive in!
Spoiler alert: it’s easier than you might think!
## What is Video Email Deliverability?
Video email deliverability refers to the ability of your video-containing emails to successfully reach your recipient’s inbox rather than being filtered into their spam or junk folders. In simpler terms, it’s the percentage of your emails (that include videos or video links) that actually land in the inbox where they can be seen and engaged with by the recipient.
## Important
Deliverability is crucial because even the most compelling video won’t do much good if it never makes it to your audience. If your video emails are flagged as spam, not only do you lose out on potential engagement and conversions, but repeated issues can also damage your sender reputation — leading to more of your emails being filtered out by spam filters.
## Why Do Video Emails End Up in Spam?
Before we dive into the tips, let’s address the elephant in the room: why do video emails sometimes go straight to the spam folder? It usually boils down to email filters. Email providers like Gmail and Outlook use sophisticated algorithms to determine whether an email is junk or worth opening. Unfortunately, video emails, with their links and multimedia content, can trigger these filters.
Further, here’s the complete list of common culprits:
- Too many links — Video emails often have links to external platforms (like YouTube or Vimeo), which can set off spam triggers.
- Large file sizes — Videos tend to increase the email size, and big attachments can make emails look suspicious to spam filters.
- Spammy subject lines — Words like “Free,” “Act now,” or excessive exclamation marks (!) can land your email in spam.
- Low sender reputation — If your email domain has a poor reputation, ISPs may route your email directly to spam.
- No proper permission — Sending unsolicited video emails to people who haven’t opted in is a major no-no.
- Poor List Management: If you’re sending emails to unengaged recipients, spam filters will notice the lack of interaction.
Now that we know what lands emails in spam, let’s focus on crafting video emails with a fighting chance of reaching the inbox. Generally, it is a good practice to test your video emails with spam filter checkers before sending them out. It’s a simple way to catch potential red flags.
Remember, it’s not just about the video — it’s about the email as a whole.
Pro Tip: Use a video thumbnail! Instead of embedding the video directly in the email (which could trigger spam filters), use a clickable thumbnail image that links to a landing page with the video. This keeps the email lighter and less likely to be flagged. This is where AI email marketing tools like Potion come into play. With it, you can have custom video GIFs as thumbnails, boosting engagement and deliverability while ensuring a smooth experience for your recipients.
## How to Keep Video Emails Out of Spam
Now that we’ve covered the common reasons, let’s explore how to keep video emails out of spam. Follow these actionable steps, and you’ll be well on your way to boosting your video email deliverability.
## 1. Choose the Right Email Service Provider (ESP)
Let’s start with the basics. The email service provider (ESP) you use can significantly impact whether your video emails land in spam or hit the inbox. But how?
Why Your ESP Matters Think of your ESP like a trusted middleman between you and your audience. Some ESPs have better reputations with ISPs (Internet Service Providers) than others. A reputable ESP is known for following good email practices, so when your email is sent through them, ISPs are more likely to trust it. This trust plays a major role in determining whether your email gets flagged as spam or makes it to the inbox.
Pro Tip: Always check if your ESP has good deliverability rates, especially for video-heavy emails. Look for features like video embedding tools, spam score analyzers, and deliverability reports to ensure you’re making the right choice.
Examples of Popular ESPs Not all ESPs are created equal, so it’s important to do your homework. Some of the best ESPs for video emails are:
- Mailchimp
- Constant Contact
- GetResponse
- ActiveCampaign
These platforms offer tools specifically designed for optimizing video emails, so your content reaches the right place.
## 2. Optimize Your Subject Line and Preview Text
Let’s be real — most people decide whether or not to open an email based on the subject line. If it looks spammy, you’re done for! That’s why nailing your subject line is crucial. It’s the first thing your recipients see, and it can make or break your email’s chances of being opened. But it doesn’t stop there! The preview text (the small snippet that shows after the subject line) also plays a big role in your deliverability.
How to Craft a Killer Subject Line Here’s the deal: avoid anything that sounds too “salesy.” Words like “free,” “buy now,” or “limited time” can trigger spam filters. Instead, focus on being clear and concise. You want your subject line to give a hint of what’s inside but also spark curiosity.
Here’s a quick checklist for writing effective subject lines:
- Keep it under 50 characters
- Avoid ALL CAPS or excessive punctuation (!!!)
- Don’t use spammy words like “discount” or “urgent”
- Personalize it when possible (e.g., “Hey [Name], here’s your personalized video!”)
- Include video-related keywords like “Watch this” or “Exclusive Video”
Example Subject Lines:
- “Check out this AI personalized video for you!”
- “A quick walkthrough of a video prospecting software just for you”
- “Don’t miss this free AI video explainer generator online!”
Why Preview Text Matters? The preview text is your second chance to hook the reader. It gives them a glimpse of what’s inside your email. Make sure it complements your subject line without repeating it verbatim. Use it to tease what your video is about, so they feel compelled to click and watch.
Pro Tip: Try A/B testing different subject lines and preview texts to see what works best for your audience. Many ESPs offer this feature, allowing you to experiment with variations and find the winning formula for higher open rates.
## 3. Avoid Overloading Your Email with Video Files
When it comes to video emails, the temptation is to include large video files directly in the email. Don’t do it! Embedding heavy video files not only increases the risk of landing in spam but also slows down loading times, making your email less engaging.
The Right Way to Include Videos in Emails Instead of embedding the entire video, include a thumbnail or GIF preview of the video with a link to view it. You can direct recipients to a landing page or your website where the video is hosted. With Potion, you can create hyper-personalized video thumbnails that seamlessly link to your video landing page. Thus, giving recipients an interactive experience while keeping your email lightweight and spam-safe.
Why It Works Spam filters often flag emails that have large attachments, and video files are no exception. By using a thumbnail and a hyperlink to your video, you avoid this pitfall while still giving your audience easy access to the content. Plus, this strategy improves your tracking capabilities, as you can monitor click-through rates to see how many people actually watched the video.
Pro Tip: Use a call-to-action (CTA) that encourages recipients to click on the thumbnail. Something like “Click to watch this quick video!” or “Watch the full video now” works wonders.
Example Email Structure:
- Subject Line: “Your personalized video is ready!”
- Body: “Hi [Name], We’ve created a quick, personalized video just for you. Click the thumbnail below to watch it!” [Thumbnail Image] “Looking forward to hearing your thoughts!” [Company Name]
This structure keeps your email simple, yet effective, while giving readers easy access to the video without overwhelming their inbox.
## 4. Authenticate Your Emails (SPF, DKIM, and DMARC)
When it comes to keeping your video emails out of spam, email authentication is a biggie. Think of it like proving your identity when you send a package. Without proper authentication, email servers can’t be sure that your email is really coming from you, and that’s when things go south — straight to the spam folder!
What Are SPF, DKIM, and DMARC? These are not just technical mumbo-jumbo; they’re crucial security protocols that tell email providers, “Hey, this email is legit!” Let’s break it down:
- SPF (Sender Policy Framework): This confirms that your email is sent from an authorized server.
- DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail): This adds a digital signature to your emails, verifying that they haven’t been tampered with during delivery.
- DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance): This helps you manage what happens to emails that fail SPF and DKIM checks — whether they should be rejected or go to spam.
Why This Matters? If your emails aren’t authenticated, inbox providers like Gmail, Yahoo, or Outlook may flag your email as suspicious. Even worse, your emails might not even get delivered at all! So, if you’re serious about avoiding spam folders, make sure your email server is properly authenticated with these protocols.
Pro Tip: If you’re not familiar with setting up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, your ESP usually has guides or support teams that can help you implement them. Trust me, this technical tweak can significantly improve your deliverability!
## 5. Keep Your Email List Clean and Engaged
You might think sending your video emails to as many people as possible is the way to go, but it’s actually the opposite. Sending emails to inactive, disengaged, or non-existent email addresses can hurt your sender reputation, which in turn, increases the chances of your emails landing in spam.
Why a Clean List Is Gold? Here’s the deal: email providers keep track of how often your emails get opened, clicked, or — even worse — bounced. If they see low engagement or high bounce rates, they’ll start labeling your emails as junk. So, it’s better to have a smaller, engaged list than a large, inactive one.
How to Clean Your List
- Remove Hard Bounces: If an email address is invalid and bounces back, take it off your list. No point in keeping it.
- Prune Inactive Subscribers: If someone hasn’t opened your emails in 6 months, it’s time to consider removing them. You can always run a re-engagement campaign before you cut them off, but don’t hesitate to clear out dead weight.
- Use Double Opt-In: This ensures that people who sign up for your emails actually want to receive them. It reduces the chances of getting spam complaints from uninterested recipients.
Pro Tip: You can also segment your list based on engagement. Target your most active subscribers with special video emails to keep them engaged, and try re-engagement strategies for those who haven’t opened your emails in a while. This keeps your list healthy and improves your deliverability!
## 6. Pay Attention to Your Email’s Text-to-Image Ratio
Let’s be honest: we all love beautifully designed emails filled with images, GIFs, and videos. But here’s the catch — too many images and too little text is a red flag for spam filters. And yes, this applies to video emails too!
The Ideal Text-to-Image Ratio Most email providers recommend a 60:40 ratio — 60% text, 40% images. Why? Because spam filters need enough text to “read” and understand the context of your email. If your email is overloaded with visuals and light on text, it might get flagged as spam, even if your intentions are pure.
How to Strike the Perfect Balance?
- Include a Text-Based CTA: Instead of relying solely on an image-based call-to-action (CTA), add a clear, concise, text-based CTA. For example, “Click here to watch the video” or “Watch now.”
- Alt-Text for Images: Always include descriptive alt-text for your images and video thumbnails. This not only helps improve deliverability but also enhances the experience for recipients with image-blocking enabled.
- Don’t Overload with Images: Limit your use of images to no more than 3–4 per email. Remember, it’s about balance, not filling the email with graphics.
Pro Tip: When embedding videos or GIFs, balance them out with sufficient, relevant text. Use video-related keywords and describe the content of the video, so even if the images don’t load, your message still makes sense and is engaging.
## 7. Monitor Your Sending Frequency (Don’t Overwhelm Your Audience)
We get it — you’re excited about your content, especially those shiny new video emails! But before you hit that “send” button every other day, stop and think. Are you sending too many emails? Bombarding your audience with frequent emails can lead to fatigue, which not only causes them to stop opening your emails but can also trigger spam complaints.
Why Sending Too Often Hurts Your Deliverability? Here’s the thing: inbox providers like Gmail and Yahoo are super-sensitive to user behavior. If too many people start marking your emails as spam — or even worse, ignoring them entirely — it signals to these providers that your emails aren’t worth delivering to the inbox. As a result, your future emails are more likely to end up in the spam folder, no matter how awesome your content is.
How to Find the Sweet Spot?
- Track Engagement: Pay attention to how your audience is interacting with your emails. If open rates start to dip or unsubscribe rates climb, it’s a sign you may need to dial back on the frequency.
- Respect the Unsubscribe: If someone wants off your list, let them go gracefully. Don’t try to overwhelm them with follow-up emails asking them to stay. Forcing people to stay on your list increases the chances of spam complaints, and trust me, you don’t want that.
- Consider a Preference Center: Allow your subscribers to choose how often they want to hear from you. Giving them control over the frequency can lead to better engagement and fewer complaints.
Pro Tip: If you send weekly video emails, but your engagement starts to drop, try switching to bi-weekly or monthly campaigns. The key is to test and find the right balance that keeps your audience interested without overwhelming them.
## 8. Warm Up Your IP Address
This tip is a little technical, but it’s absolutely critical if you’re just starting with email marketing or switching to a new email platform. Sending a large volume of emails from a “cold” IP address can look suspicious to email providers, which means your carefully crafted video emails are more likely to end up in spam.
What Does It Mean to Warm Up an IP Address? When you send a high volume of emails from a new or unused IP address all at once, email providers may see it as spammy behavior. Warming up your IP involves gradually increasing the number of emails you send over time, allowing email providers to build trust in your sending practices.
How to Properly Warm Up Your IP?
- Start Small: Begin by sending your video emails to your most engaged subscribers first. These are the people who are more likely to open, click, and interact with your content.
- Gradually Increase Volume: Slowly ramp up your email volume over a few weeks. For instance, start by sending to 1,000 subscribers, then 5,000, and so on. This steady increase helps build a positive sender reputation with email providers.
- Monitor Engagement: Keep a close eye on your open rates, click-through rates, and any spam complaints. If engagement is strong, you can continue increasing your volume. If not, it’s time to reassess your strategy.
Pro Tip: If you’re using a shared IP (meaning other companies are sending emails from the same IP), you’re sharing the reputation of that IP with them. If their practices are questionable, it could hurt your deliverability. If possible, opt for a dedicated IP so you have complete control over your sender reputation.
## 9. Pay Attention to Your Email’s HTML Code (Keep It Clean)
If you’re including video in your emails, chances are you’re working with some HTML code. And while it’s great to have a visually appealing email, messy or poorly written HTML can be a big red flag for spam filters. In fact, many spam filters are designed to catch emails with sloppy or overly complex code.
Why Clean Code Matters? Think of your email’s HTML code like the foundation of a house. If it’s well-structured and organized, everything runs smoothly. But if it’s full of broken links, unnecessary tags, or large chunks of code, it becomes unstable — and inbox providers are less likely to trust it.
Spam filters are programmed to detect common issues in HTML code that spammers often use, like hidden text, excessive use of images, or poorly constructed tables. If your video email contains any of these, it might not even make it to your recipient’s inbox!
Best Practices for Clean HTML
- Stick to Simple Layouts: The simpler your email design, the easier it is to keep your HTML clean. Avoid complex tables, unnecessary divs, or nested elements.
- Avoid Embedded Media: Instead of embedding videos directly in your email, use a thumbnail with a hyperlink (like we discussed earlier). This not only reduces the size of your email but also keeps your HTML code cleaner.
- Test Your HTML: Many ESPs provide tools to check your email’s HTML code for errors. Take advantage of these tools to identify and fix any potential issues before sending.
Pro Tip: If you’re not a coding expert, no worries! Most email marketing platforms offer pre-designed templates with clean HTML built-in. Use these templates as a base, and customize them to suit your brand without the risk of introducing messy code.
## 10. Segment Your Audience for Targeted Video Emails
We’ve all heard the saying, “One size doesn’t fit all.” This couldn’t be truer when it comes to email marketing. Sending the same generic email to your entire list might seem convenient, but it’s actually a one-way ticket to the spam folder for a lot of recipients. Why? Because not all content is relevant to every subscriber, and sending irrelevant emails is a fast track to disengagement — and even spam complaints.
Why Segmentation Boosts Deliverability? When you segment your audience based on their behavior, preferences, or demographics, you’re more likely to send video emails that resonate with them. This means higher open rates, more clicks, and fewer chances of your emails being marked as spam. Plus, email providers notice this engagement and reward you with better deliverability.
Ways to Segment Your List
- Behavioral Segmentation: Split your audience based on how they interact with your previous emails. For example, you can send different video content to those who clicked on your last email vs. those who didn’t.
- Geographic Segmentation: Send region-specific video emails if your audience is spread across different locations. This can make your content feel more personal and relevant.
- Demographic Segmentation: Tailor your video emails based on age, gender, or job role. For instance, you wouldn’t send the same content to a C-level executive as you would to an intern.
Pro Tip: Use your ESP’s segmentation features to create specific lists for different types of recipients. Then, craft video emails that speak directly to each group’s needs or interests. The more personalized your emails are, the less likely they’ll end up in the dreaded spam folder.
## 11. Test Your Emails Before Sending (Spam Tests and Previewing)
Imagine sending out an amazing video email, only to find out later that it landed in spam because of a small, avoidable error. Ouch! This is where testing comes into play. Before you send out that email blast, running spam tests and previewing your email across different platforms and devices is a must to ensure your video email doesn’t accidentally trigger spam filters.
Why Testing Matters? Spam filters are smarter than ever, and they analyze dozens of factors before deciding where to place your email. Something as simple as an incorrectly formatted subject line, a broken link, or even an overuse of certain keywords can trigger those filters. By testing your emails ahead of time, you can catch and fix potential issues that could send your email straight to the junk folder.
Types of Tests to Run
- Spam Test: Many ESPs offer built-in spam testing tools. These tools analyze your email and provide a spam score, alerting you to any red flags like poor subject line choices, suspicious links, or improper email authentication.
- Preview Test: Use preview features to see how your video email will look on different devices and email clients (like Gmail, Yahoo, or Outlook). This helps you ensure that your video thumbnails, CTAs, and layout all display correctly, regardless of the device or platform.
- Load Time Test: Check how quickly your video email loads. If it takes too long, some users might close the email before it even finishes loading — hurting your engagement rates and deliverability.
Pro Tip: Run your video email through a service like Litmus or Email on Acid to get detailed previews and spam scores before hitting send. This extra step ensures that your email looks polished and avoids any common spam triggers.
## 12. Use Consistent and Recognizable Sender Information
Trust is everything in email marketing. If your recipients don’t recognize who the email is from, chances are they won’t open it — or worse, they’ll mark it as spam. This is why having a consistent and recognizable sender name and email address is so important.
How Sender Information Affects Deliverability? Email providers look at your “From” name and email address to determine whether or not your email is trustworthy. If you’re constantly switching between different sender names or email addresses, it can raise suspicion, leading to your email being flagged as spam. But if your sender info is consistent, it builds trust with both email providers and your audience, improving your chances of landing in the inbox.
Best Practices for Sender Information
- Use a Consistent “From” Name: Stick to the same sender name for all your video email campaigns. Whether it’s your personal name, your company name, or a combination of both, consistency is key.
- Choose a Reputable Email Address: Avoid using generic or untrustworthy-looking email addresses like no-reply@company.com or marketing@company.com. Instead, opt for a personalized address like yourname@company.com or team@company.com.
- Make Sure It’s Recognizable: Your subscribers should instantly recognize who the email is from. If they don’t, they’re more likely to mark it as spam. So, whether you’re using your personal name, your company’s name, or a combination of both (e.g., John at [Company]), make sure it’s familiar.
Pro Tip: For a professional touch, use a branded domain for your email address (like @yourcompany.com) rather than a free service like Gmail or Yahoo. This helps build trust and credibility with your audience and improves your email’s deliverability.
In a nutshell, video email deliverability is all about making sure your video-based emails land in your recipients’ inboxes. To improve it, focus on keeping a clean email list, using authentication methods, optimizing your content, and maintaining a good sender reputation. The goal? Ensuring that your carefully crafted video content is seen by your audience and not lost in the spam wasteland.
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: What should I do if my video email deliverability suddenly drops?
If you notice a sudden drop in deliverability, start by checking your spam score, subject lines, and sender reputation. Make sure your email is authenticated with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, and that your sending IP is warm. It’s also a good idea to check your email list for bounces or disengaged subscribers, as this can hurt your reputation over time. Lastly, review any recent changes in your email content or frequency, as these could be impacting your deliverability.
## Q: Do video emails go to spam more often than regular emails?
Video emails can sometimes trigger spam filters more easily than text-based emails, especially if they’re not optimized correctly. Factors like large video attachments, spammy subject lines, and unverified sender information can lead to video emails being flagged as spam. However, using techniques like embedding video thumbnails instead of full videos and ensuring your email complies with spam filter protocols can reduce the risk.
## Q: Does personalization in video emails improve deliverability?
Absolutely! Personalized video emails perform better in terms of deliverability because they are more relevant and engaging to the recipient. Video messaging platforms like Potion excel in creating personalized video content. Potion lets you create custom video messaging for each recipient, increasing engagement and ensuring your emails are less likely to be marked as spam.

Personalization also improves open rates, which signals to email providers that your emails are valuable, leading to better inbox placement.
## Q: Are personalized video emails more likely to avoid the spam folder?
Doing personalized video email marketing is generally less likely to be marked as spam because it resonates more with the recipient. By addressing the recipient by name, catering to their interests, or referencing past interactions, you increase engagement. Higher engagement rates — like opens and clicks — boost your sender reputation, which is one of the key factors email providers use to determine whether an email goes to the inbox or spam.
## Q: Are video emails good for deliverability overall?
Yes, video emails can be great for deliverability if they’re handled correctly. The key is balancing engagement with email best practices. Video content is highly engaging and can lead to increased open rates, click-throughs, and overall recipient interaction — all of which are positive signals to email service providers (ESPs) that your emails are valuable. Personalized video emails tend to have higher engagement rates because they make the recipient feel seen and valued. text:
Getting customers on board with your product or service isn’t just about delivering instructions — it’s about creating a seamless, engaging, and supportive experience from the get-go. With more businesses going digital, videos have become one of the most effective tools for onboarding customers. Why? Well, people prefer videos! They’re more engaging, memorable, and often easier to follow than written instructions.
When done right, customer onboarding videos make a massive difference in how customers perceive your brand, how quickly they get up to speed with your product, and how likely they are to stick around long-term. But not all videos are created equal — each serves a different purpose.
In this article, we’ll explore some key customer onboarding video types that will engage your users and keep them returning for more. We’ll also share customer onboarding video examples. Alongside with pro tips and essential elements for each client onboarding video type to ensure you create something truly effective.
## 12 Types of Customer Onboarding Videos That Boost Engagement and Retention (With Examples)
## 1. Welcome Videos: Setting the Stage Right
A welcome video is like the digital handshake between you and your new customer. It’s your first impression, and we all know how important first impressions are! A welcome video serves as an introduction to your company, its values, and a sneak peek into what the customer can expect. It’s not too in-depth about product features just yet; think of it as a warm greeting that says, “We’re excited you’re here!”
Why It Works
- Builds a personal connection: A welcome video humanizes your brand. When customers see a friendly face, hear a genuine voice, and get a sense of your company culture, they’re more likely to feel connected.
- Sets expectations: It gives customers a heads-up on what’s to come, preparing them for the rest of the onboarding journey.
- Creates excitement: Starting with energy and enthusiasm excites customers about using your product or service.
Key Elements of an Effective Welcome Video
- Warm, friendly tone: Make it conversational. Address your audience directly, like you’re talking to a new friend.
- Clear CTA: Your welcome video should end with a clear action item. Whether it’s encouraging users to explore their dashboard, set up their profile, or proceed to the next onboarding step.
- Brief and to the point: Keep it short — between 1 to 2 minutes. You want to spark curiosity without overwhelming new users.
Example: Check out Dropbox’s welcome video that introduces new users to the platform, showing the fun and simplicity of getting started.
Pro Tip: Personalize it! Using AI video generator tools like Potion, you can customize the welcome video to match the customer’s name or industry. Thus, making the customer onboarding video feel even more tailored.
## 2. Product Tour Videos: Show, Don’t Tell
Product tour videos demonstrate your product's functionality. Instead of reading a long guide, your customers can visually walk through key features and learn how to use the product at their own pace. It’s like giving them a mini demo, but through video. Think of this as a guided tour through your product’s major features, empowering users to navigate your platform independently.
Why It Works
- Visual learners benefit: Let’s face it — most people find it easier to learn by watching than by reading. Product tours are ideal for those who prefer to “see it in action.”
- Reduces support requests: When customers know exactly how to use your product, they’re less likely to reach out for help, reducing pressure on your customer support team.
- Improves product adoption: A well-executed product tour ensures users don’t miss any key features and helps them start using your product more effectively.
Key Elements of an Effective Product Tour Video
- Step-by-step navigation: Take users through each part of the product logically, so they understand how everything connects.
- Highlight key features: Focus on the features that matter most to your users. Don’t bog them down with advanced tools just yet; start with the basics.
- Include tips and shortcuts: If your product has time-saving features or nifty shortcuts, point them out in the video.
Example: Take a look at this Slack product tour that guides new users through their workspace, highlighting key features like channels and messages.
Pro Tip: Consider interactive elements. Some platforms allow users to pause the video and try out the features themselves, making the learning process more engaging and hands-on.
## 3. Feature-Specific Videos: Dive Deeper
While product tour videos cover a lot of ground, sometimes certain features need their own spotlight. That’s where feature-specific videos come in. These videos drill down into one particular feature, explaining it in detail, showing how it works, and why it’s useful. If your product has advanced functionalities, a detailed feature-specific video can really help users get the most out of it.
Why It Works
- Reduces overwhelm: Instead of bombarding users with too much information in one go, feature-specific videos break it down into digestible chunks.
- Enhances user experience: Customers feel more confident when they fully understand how to use specific tools or features, leading to better overall product engagement.
- Increases product satisfaction: When customers learn to utilize advanced features, they’re more likely to stick with your product long-term and find value in it.
Key Elements of an Effective Feature-Specific Video
- Deep dive into functionality: Focus on one feature, and walk users through its purpose, settings, and best practices.
- Real-world use cases: Show customers exactly how they can apply the feature in their day-to-day workflow.
- Actionable tips: Give users tips on how to maximize the value of that feature for their particular needs.
Now, let’s look at a customer onboarding video example for this.
Example: Take a look at Asana’s feature-specific video on setting up hierarchy. It breaks down how to create a project hierarchy and offers pro tips for project management.
Pro Tip: Create a series! If you’ve got several standout features, consider creating a feature-specific video series. That way, users can binge-watch your tutorials, just like they would their favorite show!
## 4. FAQ Videos: Answer Common Questions Before They’re Asked
An FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) video addresses the most common questions customers tend to ask when they first start using your product or service. Instead of making them dig through a help center or email your support team, you’re proactively answering their questions in a way that’s quick, easy, and visually engaging. Think of it as your on-demand support rep, available 24/7.
Why It Works
- Proactive support: By answering frequently asked questions upfront, you reduce the number of support tickets and give your users immediate solutions.
- Improves customer experience: Customers don’t have to wait for answers, leading to a smoother, frustration-free experience.
- Boosts engagement: It’s much easier to watch a short video than to sift through a long list of FAQs. Plus, videos can explain things in more detail, making the info stick.
Key Elements of an Effective FAQ Video
- Concise answers: Get to the point quickly. Aim for brevity while being as clear as possible.
- Visual demonstrations: If applicable, show how to solve the problem directly in the video (e.g., screen recordings or walkthroughs).
- Categorize questions: Consider grouping related questions together, so users can easily find what they need.
Example: Check out this video, in which a consulting company answers common questions it receives from prospects. This helps its clients understand common challenges faced in its industry.
Pro Tip: Make it easy to navigate. Create timestamps in your video description, so users can jump straight to the questions that matter most.
## 5. Interactive Client Onboarding Videos: Give Users Hands-On Experience
Interactive client onboarding videos are next-level training tools that allow users to engage with the content directly. Instead of passively watching, users are prompted to act, like clicking on specific elements, answering questions, or even completing tasks within the video. It’s a “learn by doing” approach, where customers actively participate in onboarding.
Why It Works
- Active engagement: Users are more likely to retain information when they’re involved in the learning process rather than just watching passively.
- Personalized experience: Interactive videos can adjust the flow based on the user’s inputs, creating a more tailored onboarding experience.
- Higher completion rates: With interactive elements, users are encouraged to complete steps and stay focused, leading to better onboarding results.
Key Elements of an Effective Interactive Client Onboarding Video
- Clear prompts: Make sure it’s easy for users to know what to do next. Use prompts like “Click here to continue” or “Try it yourself now.”
- Real-time feedback: When users interact, provide immediate feedback (e.g., “Great job!” or “Here’s how you could improve”) to guide them through the process.
- Simple, actionable steps: Break down tasks into easy-to-follow steps, so users feel confident progressing through the onboarding.
Example: Take a look at Typeform’s interactive onboarding, where users can explore the platform while following step-by-step prompts to create their own form and onboard new users. It’s an excellent example of combining video with action!
Pro Tip: Leverage video messaging software like Potion to easily create personalized AI videos that make your onboarding process both fun and hands-on for your users. Plus there’s no hosting limit, and you can even generate AI videos using their personal AI avatar feature.
## 6. Success Story Videos: Inspire and Build Confidence
Success story videos, sometimes referred to as customer testimonial or case study videos, highlight real-life examples of how existing customers have successfully used your product. These videos feature authentic customer stories, showcasing the value and impact your product can have. While not purely educational, they play a huge role in onboarding by inspiring new customers and showing them what’s possible.
Why It Works
- Inspires action: When customers see others achieving great results, they’re more likely to be motivated to use your product and achieve the same results.
- Builds trust: Hearing from a peer or industry leader builds credibility. It shows that your product works and that other customers have successfully used it.
- Sets goals: Success story videos give new users a clear picture of the potential outcomes they can achieve if they fully engage with your product.
Key Elements of an Effective Success Story Video
- Authenticity: The story should feel real and relatable. It’s not a commercial; it’s a true account of someone’s experience with your product.
- Specific examples: Focus on concrete results — how much time was saved, how high ticket sales increased, or how workflow improved. Numbers help drive the point home.
- Call to action: End the video by encouraging users to take their next step, whether it’s scheduling a demo, contacting customer support, or exploring a specific feature.
Example: Check out HubSpot’s success story videos, showcasing how companies have scaled using their marketing software. These videos highlight the transformation customers have experienced with the help of HubSpot’s tools.
Pro Tip: Include success stories from a variety of industries and company sizes. This helps your customers relate to at least one story and see themselves achieving success with your product.
## 7. Training Webinars: In-Depth Learning Sessions
Training webinars are live or pre-recorded sessions where you walk customers through more advanced features, best practices, and use cases. Think of them as extended onboarding sessions that dive deep into your product’s functionality, helping users master your platform. Unlike shorter videos, webinars allow for a more detailed explanation and typically include a Q&A session for live versions, creating an interactive environment for customers.
Why It Works
- Hands-on learning: Customers can follow along step-by-step, pausing the video if necessary to apply what they’re learning in real-time.
- Builds a community: If it’s a live webinar, users can ask questions and engage with others, fostering a sense of community around your product.
- Covers advanced topics: While the initial customer onboarding videos give users the basics. Webinars allow you to dive into advanced features, helping users become power users.
Key Elements of an Effective Training Webinar
- Clear structure: Break the webinar into sections, each focusing on a specific feature or workflow. This makes it easier for users to follow along.
- Real-world examples: Use real customer scenarios to demonstrate how different features can be applied in everyday use. This helps users visualize how they can benefit from the tool.
- Interactive elements: If live, encourage questions throughout the webinar or leave space at the end for a Q&A session.
Example: Check out Salesforce’s training webinars that provide a deep dive into their CRM platform. They combine detailed walkthroughs with live Q&A to help customers get the most out of the software.
Pro Tip: Make your webinar recordings available on-demand. Not every user can attend live sessions, but they’ll still benefit from the in-depth learning experience of a pre-recorded webinar.
## 8. Milestone Celebration Videos: Mark Achievements Along the Way
Milestone celebration videos recognize and celebrate a user’s progress with your product. Whether they’re completing their first project, reaching a certain number of actions within the app, or even hitting a subscription anniversary, these videos are sent to acknowledge achievements. They’re more than just a “congrats”—they’re a key part of making your customers feel valued and motivating them to keep engaging with your product.
Why It Works
- Boosts user motivation: Celebrating milestones shows customers their progress, encouraging them to continue using the product and reach even greater achievements.
- Builds emotional connection: It personalizes the customer experience and makes users feel appreciated, not just another anonymous account.
- Increases retention: Recognizing milestones at key moments can re-engage customers who might otherwise have drifted away.
Key Elements of an Effective Milestone Celebration Video
- Personalized message: Make the video feel personal, addressing the user by name and acknowledging their specific achievement.
- Encouraging tone: Use language that celebrates the customer’s progress and pushes them toward the next step or milestone.
- Call-to-action: Suggest the next step they should take. For example, if they’ve completed their first task, encourage them to explore more advanced features.
Example: Check out Duolingo’s milestone celebration, where they send personalized videos when a user reaches a streak milestone. Thus, making the customer feel proud of their accomplishment.
Pro Tip: Automate milestone celebration videos using AI video personalization tools like Potion, allowing you to send these at the right time, personalized for each customer’s progress.
## 9. “Next Steps” Videos: Guiding Customers to Their Next Big Win
Next steps videos are designed to show customers what they should do next after completing a key onboarding task. These videos act as a roadmap, highlighting the next milestone they should focus on, guiding them deeper into the product, and showing how they can maximize its potential. Think of it as a gentle push toward continued progress, keeping them engaged without overwhelming them.
Why It Works
- Guides the journey: After users complete a big step — like setting up their account — they might not know what to do next. These videos provide a clear path forward.
- Improves product adoption: By continually guiding customers through the product, you ensure they’re using all the key features, not just the basics.
- Prevents drop-off: When users are unsure of the next step, they might disengage. These videos keep them on track, boosting retention.
Key Elements of an Effective Next Steps Video
- Specific guidance: Highlight exactly what the next action is — whether it’s setting up a secondary feature, exploring an advanced tool, or completing a tutorial.
- Motivational language: Explain the benefits of continuing to engage with the product to encourage users to take the next step.
- Short and actionable: These videos should be brief, giving just enough information to move the customer forward without overwhelming them with too much detail.
Example: See GreytHR’s “Explainer” video series that guides users through the next steps after they’ve completed a single tutorial.
Pro Tip: Add a personalized onboarding experience for customers who have already completed a task. This makes the video feel more relevant and encourages them to continue engagement.
## 10. Personalized Walkthrough Videos: Tailor-Made for Each User
A personalized walkthrough video takes a more individualized approach to onboarding, giving customers a tailor-made tour of your product based on their specific needs, preferences, or business goals. It’s like having a personal guide, but in video form. With the help of AI or manual effort, you can create customized videos for different customer segments or even individual users. Thus, making customer onboarding videos feel truly unique.
Why It Works
- Highly relevant: Users are far more likely to engage with the content when it directly addresses their pain points or goals.
- Builds loyalty: Personalization makes customers feel valued and understood, fostering a deeper connection with your brand.
- Reduces churn: Tailor the client onboarding process to fit specific user needs. This way, you help them see the exact value your product can bring to their situation. Thus reducing the chances of their abandoning it.
Key Elements of an Effective Personalized Walkthrough Video
- User-specific content: Reference the customer’s name, industry, or business goals to create a sense of exclusivity and personalization.
- Focus on relevant features: Highlight the parts of your product most applicable to that user’s needs. Don’t give a general tour — make it specific.
- Actionable tips: Offer tips that’ll directly benefit that customer, showing them how they can make the most of your product right away.
Example: Check out this example from Intercom’s workflow videos. They craft tailored experiences for different segments, ensuring each user feels catered to.
Pro Tip: You can use tools like Potion to deliver AI personalized onboarding videos without spending hours on each one. They allow you to quickly customize videos with customer-specific details or even generate them using a text script. Thus promoting a sense of personal engagement at scale.
## 11. Quick Tip Videos: Short, Snappy, and Solution-Oriented
Quick tip videos are bite-sized videos (usually under a minute or two) that focus on one specific feature, shortcut, or hack within your product. They’re designed to be easy to consume and laser-focused on solving a particular pain point. Think of them as “pro tips” that give users the inside scoop on how to make the most of your product — without taking too much of their time.
Why It Works
- High engagement: Short videos are more likely to get watched all the way through, especially when users are short on time.
- Promotes continuous learning: Regularly introducing new tips keeps users engaged and encourages them to explore your product more.
- Reduces overwhelm: Instead of bombarding users with a huge amount of information all at once, these quick tips give them small, digestible nuggets of knowledge.
Key Elements of an Effective Quick Tip Video
- Focused content: Pick one specific feature or use case and stick to it. The goal is to keep it short and simple.
- Clear and actionable: Walk users through a task or feature they can implement immediately.
- Visual demonstrations: Show, don’t just tell. Use screen recordings or product demos to visually guide users through the process.
Example: See Canva’s “Tip Talk” videos where they regularly share short, actionable tips on creating stunning designs in just a few clicks.
Pro Tip: Consider creating a series of quick tip videos and releasing them at intervals. This will keep your users coming back for more and steadily improve their product proficiency without overwhelming them with too much information at once.
## 12. Troubleshooting Videos: Solve Issues Before They Happen
Troubleshooting videos are designed to help customers resolve common issues or challenges they might face when using your product. These videos take a “how-to-fix-it” approach, walking users through steps to troubleshoot potential problems. Think of them as your emergency help guide, but way more engaging and helpful than an FAQ article.
Why It Works
- Prevents frustration: Instead of leaving customers stuck and frustrated when encountering an issue, troubleshooting videos provide immediate solutions, keeping them happy and engaged.
- Reduces support tickets: These videos reduce the number of support requests your team needs to handle by offering clear, self-service solutions.
- Increases product confidence: When users know there’s a solution to their problems (and it’s easy to find), they’re more likely to stick with your product.
Key Elements of an Effective Troubleshooting Video
- Focus on common issues: Identify the most frequently asked questions or support tickets and create videos that address these problems.
- Step-by-step guidance: Make sure the video takes users through each troubleshooting step clearly and logically.
- Use real examples: Show real-world scenarios or examples of the problem in action so that users can relate and follow along.
Example: Check out this Zoom video, which walks users through common connectivity and audio issues and offers step-by-step fixes.
Pro Tip: Create a troubleshooting video library on your website or within your app that customers can easily access. You can even categorize videos based on the most common issues (e.g., technical glitches, billing questions, etc.).
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: Why should I use customer onboarding videos?
Videos are an incredibly engaging and effective medium for customer onboarding experience because they provide a visual and auditory learning that’s easier to follow than written instructions. They help customers understand your product more quickly, increase engagement, and reduce the likelihood of user frustration. Plus, they allow for a more personalized and memorable experience. Use these customer onboarding metrics to craft a strategic action plan for lasting success.
## Q: How can I personalize customer onboarding videos?
You can personalize customer onboarding videos by:
- Including the customer’s name, company, or specific use case.
- Customizing the content based on the customer’s industry or goals.
- Using AI email marketing tools like Potion to quickly generate personalized walkthroughs or greetings for individual customers or segments. Personalized videos make the onboarding experience feel more relevant and engaging.

## Q: What’s the best way to create client onboarding videos without breaking the bank?
You don’t need to spend a fortune creating customer onboarding videos.
- Start simple: Use screen recordings with voiceover to explain features.
- Leverage free or affordable tools: AI sales tools like Loom and Potion make it easy to record, personalize, and share videos without needing a professional production team.
- Focus on content: A well-structured, clear, and informative video will always be more valuable than a flashy, high-budget one that lacks substance.
Additionally, follow these customer onboarding best practices to boost retention.
## Q: How many client onboarding videos should I include in my customer journey?
There’s no set number, but your client onboarding videos should align with your product’s complexity. Typically, you’ll want to include:
- 1–2 welcome videos
- 1–2 product tour videos
- Multiple feature-specific videos
- FAQ videos for common questions
- Quick tips for bite-sized learning
- Next steps videos for ongoing engagement
If your product is more complex, consider incorporating interactive webinars or advanced training videos for power users. Spread the videos throughout the customer journey to prevent overwhelming new users.
## Q: Can I reuse the same client onboarding videos for different target segments?
Yes, but with some caveats. You can reuse certain videos (like product tours or FAQ videos) across customer segments, but it’s a good idea to create customized videos where applicable.
## Conclusion
Incorporating a variety of video types into your customer onboarding process is a game-changer for improving user engagement, reducing friction, and boosting long-term retention. From welcome videos that set the right tone to product tours that walk users through your platform, each video type plays a crucial role in ensuring customers feel supported and empowered.

text:
What is cold calling in recruitment — does it still work? While some believe that this age-old technique is a relic of the past. In reality, it remains a powerful tool for recruiters to reach top talent directly. But, let’s face it, cold calling isn’t easy. The thought of dialing up candidates who haven’t heard of you or the company can feel daunting. Still, when done right, cold calling can bring impressive results! It can fill your open positions faster and more efficiently than other methods.
This article will walk you through the ins and outs of cold calling in recruitment. Right from understanding its importance to crafting compelling scripts and handling rejections like a pro. We’ll also dive into some common pitfalls recruiters face and provide actionable tips to ensure you maximize every opportunity.
Whether you’re just starting out in recruitment process enhancement or looking to sharpen your skills. This article will give you everything you need to know.
## What Is Cold Calling in Recruitment?
Cold calling in recruitment is the process of reaching out to potential candidates without prior contact, often through a phone call. This is done to gauge their interest in a job opportunity. Unlike warm leads (where candidates have shown some form of interest or engagement with the company), cold calling involves contacting individuals who may not even know your company exists.
For many recruiters, it’s an essential tool because, let’s face it, not every qualified candidate is actively looking for a job. Some of the best talent may be sitting in comfortable positions, unaware that a more exciting opportunity awaits them!
## Why Cold Calling Still Matters
In the digital age, with LinkedIn messages and automated emails dominating recruitment outreach, you might wonder why cold calling is still relevant. The truth is, while digital communication is convenient, it can also be easy to ignore. A phone call, on the other hand, forces real-time engagement. You can immediately establish rapport, address objections, and create a personal connection that written communication just can’t replicate.
Let’s look at why cold calling in recruitment still packs a punch:
- Direct engagement: Nothing beats real-time interaction. Cold calling allows you to immediately gauge a candidate’s interest and tailor your pitch accordingly.
- Personal touch: Candidates can hear the enthusiasm in your voice, making it easier to build trust and excitement.
- Immediate feedback: If a candidate is not interested, you’ll know right away. No need to wait days or weeks for an email response.
- Cuts through the noise: While candidates’ inboxes are flooded with messages, phone calls still stand out as a more personalized approach.
Pro Tip: Want to maximize your cold calls? Research candidates thoroughly before picking up the phone. Understand their career history, current role, and any commonalities you share. This preparation can transform a “cold” call into a much warmer interaction.
## Tips on How to do Cold Calling in Recruitment
Like anything in recruitment, success with cold calling hinges on preparation. The more time you spend understanding your candidate and preparing your pitch, the better your chances of getting them on board.
## 1. Research the Candidate
Before dialing, take a few minutes to learn about the person on the other end of the line. LinkedIn, GitHub, and even social media platforms can offer invaluable insights. What skills do they have? What’s their current role? Are there any mutual connections? Being informed shows that you’re serious and have done your homework.
## 2. Craft a Compelling Script
While it’s important not to sound robotic, having a well-thought-out script ensures you don’t get caught off guard or forget key details. Your cold calling script for recruitment agency should be clear, concise, and personalized. Remember to introduce yourself, state the purpose of your call, and offer a reason why the candidate might be interested in the opportunity.
Here’s a basic framework for your cold-calling script:
- Introduction: “Hi [Name], my name is [Your Name], and I’m a recruiter at [Company]. How’s your day going?”
- Purpose: “I came across your profile and noticed you have extensive experience in [specific area]. I wanted to connect and see if you’d be open to hearing about a new opportunity that aligns with your skills.”
- Value Proposition: “This position offers [mention key benefits — e.g., career growth, flexibility, higher salary].”
- Next Steps: “Would you be interested in learning more or discussing this further?”
## 3. Timing Is Everything
When it comes to cold calling, timing is critical. Avoid calling too early in the morning or too late in the day. Generally, mid-morning or early afternoon is best. Also, be mindful of time zones if you’re recruiting globally.
## 4. Set Clear Goals
Before picking up the phone, know what you want to achieve from the call. Are you looking to schedule a follow-up interview? Gauge the candidate’s interest? Or simply introduce yourself and your company? Having a clear objective will keep the conversation focused and purposeful.
## 5. Practice Makes Perfect
Cold calling can be nerve-wracking, especially if you’re new to it. A little practice can go a long way in boosting your confidence. Try rehearsing your script with a colleague or even in front of a mirror. The more comfortable you are, the more natural you’ll sound when the real call happens.
## 6. Anticipate Questions
Think about the questions a candidate might ask during the call. What’s the company culture like? What are the salary expectations? Why is this role available? Having thoughtful answers ready will help you handle any curveballs without missing a beat.
## 7. Create a Distraction-Free Environment
Cold calls require focus. Eliminate potential distractions before dialing. That means closing unnecessary tabs, silencing your phone (except for the call, of course!), and making sure you’re in a quiet environment. Distractions can easily throw you off your game, so it’s best to minimize them.
## 8. Check Your Mindset
It may sound cliché, but your mindset matters. Approach each call with positivity and confidence. If you go in thinking, “This call probably won’t go anywhere,” it likely won’t. On the other hand, a confident attitude can be contagious — candidates will pick up on your enthusiasm and energy.
## 9. Have a Follow-Up Plan
A successful cold call doesn’t always end with an immediate “yes.” Be prepared to follow up. Whether you schedule a future call, send additional information, or simply touch base later, having a plan for next steps will keep the momentum going and show the candidate you’re serious.
Pro Tip: Always make sure you have a pen and paper handy — or a digital notepad open — during the call. Jotting down notes while the candidate speaks can help you remember key details and demonstrate that you’re actively listening!
## Overcoming Common Objections For Cold Calling in Recruitment
No one said cold calling in recruitment would be easy. You’re bound to face objections. Some candidates may be too busy, uninterested, or skeptical. How you handle these objections can make or break the conversation.
## Objection 1: “I’m not looking for a new job right now.”
Your Response: “I completely understand! Even if now isn’t the right time, would it be okay if we stayed in touch for future opportunities? It’s always good to have a backup plan.”
## Objection 2: “I don’t have time to talk.”
Your Response: “I won’t take up too much of your time — just a quick minute to share this opportunity. If you’re interested, we can schedule a longer chat later.”
## Objection 3: “I’m happy where I am.”
Your Response: “That’s great to hear! However, I believe this role offers a few things your current position might not — like [mention specific benefits]. It’s always good to know what’s out there.”
## Objection 4: “I don’t think I have the right experience.”
Your Response: “I totally get that, but from what I’ve seen in your profile, you’ve got a lot of relevant skills that would translate well into this role. Plus, this company really values diverse experiences, and they’re great at providing support and training where needed.”
## Objection 5: “I’m not interested in a career change right now.”
Your Response: “Completely understandable! Timing is everything. That said, it never hurts to explore options — you never know when the perfect opportunity might come along. Would you be open to just hearing about the role, even if it’s just for future reference?”
## Objection 6: “What’s in it for me?”
Your Response: “Great question! This opportunity offers a chance for significant career growth, whether it’s moving up the ladder or working on cutting-edge projects. Plus, the compensation package is highly competitive — always a nice bonus, right?”
## Objection 7: “I’ve heard about your company, but I’m not sure it’s a fit for me.”
Your Response: “That’s fair! Every company isn’t for everyone. But based on what I know about your experience and goals, I think this could be a strong fit for you. If it’s okay, I’d love to share more about why I think that, and you can decide if it feels right for you.”
## Objection 8: “I’m too busy to consider new roles right now.”
Your Response: “I hear you! Everyone’s juggling a lot these days. If now isn’t the best time, could I send you over a quick summary of the role? You can review it when you have a moment, and we can circle back when you’re ready.”
## Objection 9: “I’ve had bad experiences with recruiters before.”
Your Response: “I’m really sorry to hear that! I can imagine how frustrating that must’ve been. My approach is a little different — I prioritize transparency and long-term relationships. Let me know if you’re open to a quick chat, and hopefully, I can change your mind about working with recruiters.”
Pro Tip: Always have a list of common objections prepared, along with responses that address those concerns in a polite yet assertive manner. Practice makes perfect!
When handling cold calling objections, always show empathy first. Acknowledging their concerns before responding with a solution or alternative helps to build trust and keeps the conversation open.
## Cold Calling Techniques to Boost Success For Recruiters
So, how can you turn those cold calls into meaningful conversations that lead to hires? Here are some tried-and-tested techniques to improve your cold-calling strategy.
## 1. Use Personalized Video Outreach Before the Call
Want to grab their attention even before you make the call? Try sending a personalized video! AI email marketing software like Potion is a game-changer when it comes to this. It enables you to create AI personalized videos at scale. This means you can generate customized videos for dozens or even hundreds of candidates in a fraction of the time. Simply record your message once, and the AI creates thousands of personalized variations for you. All with individual candidates' names, current roles, and even personalized video backgrounds. Thus delivering your message as if it were a one-on-one video.
In the video, you can introduce yourself, explain why you’re reaching out, and hint at the exciting opportunity you have for them. By the time you call, candidates will already have a sense of who you are and why you’re contacting them, creating a warmer lead. This approach increases the chances of a positive conversation and helps you stand out in a crowded recruitment market.
For recruiters juggling multiple candidates, this method is a powerful way to make a personal connection — without sacrificing efficiency!
## 2. Use a Referral Approach
Rather than diving straight into the pitch, start by mentioning a referral or common connection. For example: “I was speaking with [Mutual Contact], and they mentioned you’d be a great fit for a role I’m working on.” This approach instantly warms up the conversation.
## 3. Create a Sense of Urgency
When a candidate senses urgency, they’re more likely to engage. Mention that the position is filling up quickly or that there’s limited availability for interviews. However, be careful not to overdo it, as this can come across as pushy.
## 4. Personalize Every Call
No two candidates are the same, so why should your pitch be? Tailor each call to the individual you’re speaking to. Highlight aspects of the role that align with their experience or career aspirations.
## 5. Active Listening
Cold calling is not just about delivering your pitch — it’s about engaging in a two-way conversation. Practice active listening by acknowledging what the candidate says and asking follow-up questions to show genuine interest.
## 6. Use Data to Back Up Your Pitch
People respond well to facts. Back up your pitch by citing data related to the opportunity you’re presenting. For example, “This company has experienced a 30% growth rate over the past year, and they’re looking for someone with your expertise to help sustain that momentum.” Data-driven pitches add credibility to your call and make the opportunity more enticing.
## 7. Offer Value Even If They’re Not Interested
Not every candidate will be interested in the role you’re offering, and that’s okay! However, don’t end the call there. Instead, offer something valuable, like sharing industry insights, salary benchmarks, or upcoming trends. This leaves the candidate with a positive impression and keeps the door open for future opportunities. Plus, you position yourself as a helpful resource rather than just another recruiter.
## 8. Practice the 3:1 Compliment-to-Request Ratio
Make your cold call feel less like a sales pitch and more like a friendly chat by using the 3:1 ratio: for every request you make (such as asking if they’re interested in hearing more), offer three compliments or positive observations about their skills, experience, or profile. For instance: “I saw you’ve led several successful projects in [specific area]. Your leadership and expertise really stand out, and I think this role would give you a great platform to shine even more.”
Lastly, let’s face it — recruiting through cold calling can sometimes be stressful, especially when you face rejections. But staying calm and collected during the call, regardless of the outcome, is key.
Candidates will sense your professionalism and confidence. This reflects positively on both you and the company you’re representing. If a candidate isn’t interested, gracefully wrap up the conversation and thank them for their time.
## Cold Calling vs. Other Recruitment Methods
Cold calling isn’t the only tool in a recruiter’s arsenal, but it’s certainly one of the most direct. Here’s how it compares to other popular recruitment methods:
## 1. Cold Calling vs. Email Outreach
Both cold calling and email outreach allow recruiters to connect with potential candidates, but the experiences are quite different. Here’s a closer look at how they compare:
- The immediacy of response: Cold calls provide real-time interaction, whereas emails can sit unread for hours, days, or even weeks.
- Personal connection: Hearing a voice on the other end builds rapport faster than an email. Cold calls feel more personal, whereas emails can sometimes come across as impersonal or formulaic.
- Candidate engagement: With cold calls, you can tailor your conversation on the fly based on the candidate’s responses. Emails, however, are static and may not always capture a candidate’s attention in the same way.
- Time investment: Sending out mass emails is faster and requires less effort than making individual phone calls. However, the quality of engagement in cold calls is often higher, even though it takes more time.
- Open rates vs. answer rates: While email open rates can be low (especially for cold outreach), cold calls, when answered, almost always ensure some level of engagement, even if brief.
## 2. Cold Calling vs. LinkedIn InMail
LinkedIn InMail is another popular method for recruiters to connect with potential candidates. However, cold calling brings its own set of benefits that differ from this platform’s messaging feature:
- Response time: InMail can often go unanswered for days, especially if the recipient isn’t active on LinkedIn. Cold calls, on the other hand, prompt an immediate response.
- Personalization: Although LinkedIn InMail can be customized, a voice conversation offers a much higher level of personalization. Candidates can feel the recruiter’s enthusiasm, something text can’t fully convey.
- Engagement level: Cold calling requires the candidate to engage on the spot, while InMail allows them to delay their response or ignore the message altogether.
- Effort involved: InMail allows recruiters to message many candidates quickly, while cold calling requires more effort since each call is personalized and takes time. However, the depth of connection during a cold call can outweigh the convenience of InMail.
- Avoiding spam filters: While InMails can be filtered out or ignored, a cold call bypasses these barriers, ensuring the recruiter has a direct line to the candidate.
## 3. Cold Calling vs. Job Postings
Job postings are the traditional way to advertise open positions, but relying on them alone can limit your candidate pool. Here’s how cold calling compares:
- Proactivity: Cold calling allows recruiters to proactively reach out to candidates rather than waiting for them to apply. Job postings rely on candidates coming to you, which may limit your reach, especially with passive talent.
- Targeted approach: Cold calls enable recruiters to target specific candidates with tailored opportunities, whereas job postings cast a wider net that can attract unqualified applicants.
- Speed of results: While job postings can generate a lot of responses, sifting through irrelevant applications can slow down the recruitment process. Cold calling offers more immediate, qualified conversations with potential hires.
- Engagement quality: Candidates reached via cold calling are often more passive, which means you may be introducing them to opportunities they hadn’t considered. In contrast, job postings attract active job seekers who may or may not be the right fit for the role.
- Cost-effectiveness: Job postings often come with costs, especially on premium job boards. Cold calling, while time-intensive, can be more cost-effective if you already have a candidate database to work from.
Cold calling stands out when direct, personalized, and immediate engagement is the priority. That said, combining cold calling with other recruitment methods can create a well-rounded strategy that taps into both passive and active talent pools.
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: Is cold calling in recruitment outdated?
Nope! While digital methods are on the rise, cold calling remains a highly effective way to reach passive candidates who aren’t actively job-hunting.
## Q: Does cold calling for jobs work?
Absolutely, it does! Cold calling for jobs can be an incredibly effective strategy, though it often flies under the radar. Here’s why it works: most job seekers rely heavily on online applications, but cold calling allows you to take a proactive approach, putting yourself directly in front of decision-makers. You’re not just another resume in the pile — you’re a real person, making a genuine connection.
By reaching out to employers directly, you’re able to express interest, showcase your enthusiasm, and potentially learn about openings that aren’t even advertised yet. Many roles are filled through internal networks or before they’re posted, so cold calling gives you a chance to tap into those hidden opportunities.
That said, success with cold calling requires preparation. You need to research the company, tailor your pitch, and approach the conversation with confidence. Sure, it takes guts to pick up the phone and call a potential employer, but when done right, it can set you apart from the crowd and open doors that might’ve otherwise remained closed.
## Q: What’s the best time to make cold calls in recruitment?
The best time to cold call is typically mid-morning or early afternoon. Avoid calling too early or late in the day when candidates may be busy or unavailable.
## Q3: How long should an individual recruitment cold calling last?
Ideally, cold calls should be short and to the point — no longer than 5–10 minutes. Your goal is to spark interest and schedule a follow-up conversation.
## Q4: What if a candidate isn’t interested?
If a candidate isn’t interested, don’t push. Politely ask if you can stay in touch for future opportunities and thank them for their time.
## Conclusion
Cold calling in recruitment is far from outdated. When done with the right approach, it remains a highly effective way to connect with top talent, build meaningful relationships, and fill roles that might otherwise go unnoticed. From preparing the perfect script for recruiter cold call to overcoming objections and actively listening, mastering cold calling can give you a significant edge in today’s competitive recruitment landscape.
