- AI-Powered Personalization: Add a sprinkle of magic with Potion’s AI. Merge your video with dynamic text overlays and data points specific to each prospect, creating a truly personalized experience.
- Seamless Integration: Potion offers 50+ integrations that allow you to create dynamic videos easily. This ensures you can effortlessly add video magic to your email campaigns.
Ready to transform your email outreach? Create a free account on Potion today and experience the power of video personalization!
Remember, in the age of information overload, a video is truly worth a thousand words.
## Frequently Asked Questions or FAQs
## Q: I hate the phone! Is cold emailing enough on its own?
Cold emailing can be a powerful tool, but it shouldn’t be your only weapon. Consider it the first step in building a relationship. A well-crafted follow-up call after a few email touches can be a game-changer. So don’t be afraid to pick up the phone after you’ve warmed things up with email. Additionally, if you are suffering with low open rates, consider using these tips for cold emailing.
## Q: My emails are getting ignored! What am I doing wrong?
There could be a few culprits. One, your emails might be landing in spam folders. Ensure you’re sending from a reputable email address and avoid spammy language in your subject line. Two, your emails might be generic and forgettable. Personalize your message, showcase the value you offer, and make sure your call to action is crystal clear. Three, you might not be following up enough. Persistence is key! Send a few follow-up emails over a span of a week or two, but avoid being overly aggressive. Still, if things aren’t working, ensure you aren’t committing any of these common cold email mistakes.
## Q: Can I use social media to connect with prospects before cold calling or emailing?
Absolutely! Social media platforms like LinkedIn are goldmines for finding decision-makers and researching their needs. Engage with their content, join relevant groups, and establish yourself as an expert in your industry. This social proof can make your outreach efforts all the more impactful.
## Q: I’m worried about being pushy or salesy in my outreach.
It’s a valid concern! The key is to focus on providing value. Instead of a blunt sales pitch, lead with how your product or service can solve their problems and make their lives easier. Offer helpful content, insights, or free consultations. When you position yourself as a solution provider, the sales part becomes a natural next step.
## Q: Is there a magic formula for outreach success?
There’s no one-size-fits-all answer, but there are some key ingredients. Combine a strategic approach (understanding your audience and aligning your outreach methods), compelling content (emails that grab attention and offer value), and a sprinkle of persistence (don’t give up after one attempt), and you’ll be well on your way to outreach mastery!
## Conclusion
There you have it, folks! The cold emailing vs cold calling showdown has reached its conclusion. Remember, there’s no single “best” method. It’s all about understanding the strengths and weaknesses of each approach and aligning them with your specific goals and audience. But still, here’s a quick summary,
Choose Cold Emailing When:
- You’re targeting a large audience with geographically dispersed contacts.
- You’re offering a complex product or service that requires detailed explanation.
- You want to provide prospects with information they can refer back to later.
- Your target audience is known to be unresponsive to phone calls.
Choose Cold Calling When:
- You’re selling a high-value product that requires a personal touch.
- You need to quickly qualify leads and gauge their interest.
- Your ideal customer has a short attention span and might not read emails thoroughly.
- You’re a natural communicator who thrives on building rapport through voice interaction.
Pro Tip: Don’t be afraid to experiment! A multi-channel approach combining cold emails and cold calls can be highly effective.
So, dust off your AI email marketing tools, polish your sales pitch, and prepare to conquer your outreach goals! By embracing a strategic multi-channel approach, you can quickly gain amazing results. Now go forth and sell!

text:
It’s 2024 and attention spans are shorter than ever. Cutting through the noise and grabbing your audience’s interest is crucial, especially when it comes to creating video sales letters. Here’s where the debate between conversational and scripted video sales letters heats up.
Both approaches have their own strengths and weaknesses. Deciding which one is right for you depends on your brand voice, target audience, and the specific product or service you’re selling. Buckle up, as we compare conversational vs scripted video sales letters in this article. Thus, helping you choose the winning VSL formula for your business.
## Conversational Video Sales Letters: The “Let’s Grab Coffee” Approach
Imagine having a casual conversation with a friend about a product that’s genuinely awesome. That’s the essence of a conversational video sales letter. It’s all about building rapport, addressing pain points in a relatable way, and showcasing the solution in a natural, unscripted flow.
Here’s what makes conversational video sales letters so engaging:
- Feels Authentic: There’s no robotic delivery or rehearsed lines. It feels like a genuine conversation, fostering trust and connection with viewers. That’s one of the many reasons why it is also great for personalized video marketing.
- Relatable and Engaging: Ever felt like a company’s just talking at you, not with you? Conversational VSLs break down that barrier. It feels like a real person addressing real concerns, making it highly relatable.
- Flexibility: You can adapt your message on the fly, addressing specific audience concerns that arise during filming.
- Engaging Personality: Your personality shines through, making the VSL more memorable.
- Building Rapport: Conversation allows for back-and-forth. You can anticipate questions, address common sales objections, boost your video sales strategy and even inject a bit of humor, all of which help build rapport with viewers.
But hold on, conversational doesn’t mean unprepared! Here are some video sales letter tips and best practices on how to nail the conversational approach:
- Develop a Script Outline: While not a rigid VSL script, an outline ensures you cover key points and the call to action (CTA). Additionally, outline key points you want to convey, but leave room for improvisation.
- Practice, Practice, Practice: Rehearse your delivery to sound natural, not overly scripted. Think of it as warming up before a friendly chat.
- Know Your Audience: Research their demographics, pain points, and preferred communication style.
- Embrace Personality: Let your brand voice shine through! Humor, anecdotes, and a touch of vulnerability can go a long way in building a connection.
- Winging It Can Backfire: Going completely off the cuff can lead to rambling or missing key points altogether. A basic structure keeps you on track while allowing for a casual flow.
- Editing Magic Required: If not well recorded, conversational VSLs often require more editing to remove awkward pauses, stumbles, and other “ums” and “ahs.”
However, conversational video sales letters aren’t perfect for everyone. Here are some potential drawbacks:
- Requires Confidence: This approach demands comfort speaking unscripted, which might feel daunting for some.
- Less Control Over Messaging: Sticking to a specific message during an impromptu conversation can be tricky.
- Editing Challenges: Fluffs, stumbles, and awkward pauses require skillful editing to maintain a polished look.
Examples: Imagine a makeup artist showing off her latest product line while sharing personal tips and tricks behind-the-scenes of her studio.
Here’s a VSL for your reference,
## Scripted Video Sales Letters: The Power of a Polished Pitch
Scripted video sales letters are like well-rehearsed presentations. They deliver a clear message, highlight benefits with well-crafted arguments, and often feature high-quality visuals.
Here’s what makes scripted video sales letters effective:
- Professional Polish: Polished scripts can sound incredibly professional and authoritative. It’s like having a seasoned salesperson deliver your pitch — perfect for building trust and establishing your brand’s expertise.
- Targeted Messaging: You have complete control over the message you want to convey, ensuring all key points are covered.
- Crystal Clear Communication: Scripted videos remove the risk of rambling or losing your train of thought. You know exactly what you want to say and how you want to say it. This ensures a focused, well-organized message. Further, every VSL delivers the same polished message, ensuring brand consistency.
- Data-Driven Optimization: You can A/B test different scripts to see what resonates best with your audience.
- Multiple Takes & Editing Magic: Scripted videos allow for multiple takes and meticulous editing, resulting in a polished, error-free final product.
- Repeatability is Key: Scripted VSLs are easy to replicate. You can film it once and use it across various platforms, saving you time and resources in the long run.
However, scripted videos can sometimes feel a tad… stiff. Here are a few tips & best practices on how to breathe life into your script:
- Inject Personality: Don’t let the script make you sound like a monotone robot. Inflection, pacing, and enthusiasm make all the difference.
- Storytelling is Key: Weave a compelling narrative that connects with viewers on an emotional level.
- Visual Appeal: High-quality visuals like product demos, customer testimonials, and explainer animations can dramatically enhance engagement.
- Vary Your Vocal Inflection: Don’t monotonously drone on. Use inflection to emphasize key points.
- Incorporate Humor (If It Suits Your Brand): A well-placed joke can break the ice and make your VSL more engaging.
- Focus on Eye Contact: Make viewers feel like you’re talking directly to them.
While polished, scripted videos might not be ideal for everyone, as they offer:
- Less Flexibility: Once the script is locked in, making changes on the fly can be difficult.
- Stiffness Can Kill: Scripts can feel overly formal, robotic even. This can come across as inauthentic and disconnect you from your audience. Who wants to listen to a monotone lecture?
- Lack of Spontaneity: The beauty of conversation lies in its unpredictable nature. Scripted VSLs often lack that spark of spontaneity, making it harder to build a genuine connection.
- Adaptability Issues: Life throws curveballs, and so do customer needs. Scripted VSLs can be inflexible, making it difficult to address specific pain points or questions viewers might have.
- Can Feel Impersonal: If not delivered with enough warmth and personality, a scripted video can feel robotic and off-putting.
- Higher Production Costs: Professional actors, scripting, and editing can lead to higher production costs compared to conversational videos.
Examples: Think of a high-tech company unveiling a new product with a sleekly produced video that showcases its features and benefits through a compelling narrative.
Here’s a VSL for your reference,
## Conversational vs. Scripted: The Ultimate Showdown
So, which approach reigns supreme? Well, there’s no one-size-fits-all answer. It depends! The best format for you depends on several factors:
- Your Brand Personality: Are you a playful startup or a well-established corporation? A conversational VSL might suit the former, while a scripted approach might better represent the latter.
- Your Target Audience: Consider who you’re trying to reach. Younger demographics might connect with a conversational style, while a more formal approach could resonate with business professionals.
- Your Comfort Level: Do you feel confident speaking unscripted? If not, a well-crafted script can be a lifesaver. However, a conversational approach could be your secret weapon if you’re comfortable “winging it” with some preparation.
Choose Conversational VSLs If:
- You’re comfortable speaking unscripted.
- You’re doing video prospecting and want to leverage good AI video personalization to your benefit.
- Your target audience resonates with a casual tone.
- You want a more flexible approach for addressing audience concerns.
Opt for Scripted VSLs If:
- You have a complex product with a lot of information to convey.
- Brand consistency is crucial, and you want a polished presentation.
- You have the resources for professional editing and sound design.
- You’re trying to craft a personalized shopping experience using video for your e-commerce store.
However, the best approach often lies in a hybrid combining the strengths of both styles.
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: Can I combine conversational and scripted elements?
Absolutely! You can have a scripted framework with conversational elements sprinkled in, or vice versa.
## Q: I’m still stuck between conversational and scripted. How can I decide?
Try both! Experiment with creating a shorter video in each style and see which one resonates better with your audience. Metrics like watch time, engagement, and click-through rates can offer valuable insights.
## Q: What if I mess up during a conversational video? Should I re-record?
It depends! Minor stumbles or pauses can sometimes add to the authenticity of the conversational approach. For major flubs or if you go way off track, consider re-recording that specific segment.
## Q: I’m not a great public speaker. Can I still pull off a conversational VSLs?
Absolutely! Practice beforehand, focus on delivering key points, and remember, a touch of nervousness can even add to the authenticity!
## Q: Should I invest in professional equipment for my video?
While high-quality visuals are great, a well-lit, well-framed phone video with good audio can be just as effective, especially for a conversational approach.
## Q: Can I use teleprompters for a conversational video?
Sure! Teleprompters can be a helpful tool, especially if you’re prone to nerves or want to ensure you hit all the key points. Just remember to practice beforehand to ensure your delivery feels natural and not robotic.
## Q: I don’t have a big budget for video production. Are there any workarounds?
Absolutely! Natural light, a clean background, and good audio can go a long way. Leverage free stock footage or create your own simple graphics using online tools. Remember, the content and your delivery are key, not fancy bells and whistles.
## Conclusion
Conversational videos are perfect for building rapport and a sense of community, while scripted videos excel at delivering a polished, controlled message. Consider the hybrid approach to create a video that feels both genuine and impactful.
Remember, the best approach is the one that feels most comfortable for you and resonates most deeply with your target audience.

text:
Let’s face it, cold emails can feel like tossing messages into a bottomless abyss. You spend ages crafting the perfect pitch, hit send, and…crickets. But fear not, email pros! This guide is packed with effective cold email examples for b2b that will have recipients hitting “reply” faster than you can say “increased sales.”
We’ll unveil winning formulas, explore different approaches, and provide concrete cold email templates for b2b sales to inspire you. So, buckle up, get ready to ditch the dreaded silence, and transform your outreach strategy!
## Understanding the Art of the Cold Email
Let's establish a solid foundation before diving into specific cold email examples. Here are some key ingredients for crafting emails that resonate:
- Personalization is King (and Queen): A generic “Dear Sir or Madam” is a recipe for instant deletion. Take the time to find your recipient’s name and tailor your message to their specific needs.
- Hook ’Em from the Start: The first sentence is your golden opportunity to grab their attention. Use a thought-provoking question, a surprising statistic, or a relatable anecdote.
- Focus on Value, Not Just Features: Don’t just list features of your product or service. Explain how it directly benefits the recipient and solves their pain points.
- Keep it Concise & Compelling: People are busy. Aim for emails that are easy to scan and under 300 words.
- Craft a Clear Call to Action (CTA): Tell the recipient exactly what you want them to do next, whether it’s scheduling a call, visiting your website, or downloading a free resource.
## Top Cold Email Templates 2024: Let’s Get Specific!
Now, let’s get down to business with some inspiringly good cold email templates for B2B sales across various scenarios:
## 1. The “Mutual Connection” Approach
This email leverages a shared connection to build rapport and establish trust.
Subject: Following Up on [Mutual Connection’s Name]’s Recommendation
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], [Mutual Connection’s Name] recently mentioned you and your impressive work at [Company Name]. They raved about your expertise in [Area of Expertise]. At [Your Company], we specialize in [Your Company’s Value Proposition]. I noticed you recently [Mention a relevant action the recipient took, e.g., downloaded a white paper]. Perhaps we could connect to discuss how our solutions might complement your current efforts in [Area of Interest]. Happy to chat for 15 minutes at your convenience. Best regards, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This cold email example for b2b sales taps into the power of social proof and creates a sense of familiarity. The reference to a mutual connection warms the recipient up to your message.
## 2. The “Pain Point Hero” Approach
This email identifies a common challenge faced by the recipient’s industry and offers a solution.
Subject: Are You Struggling with [Industry Pain Point]?
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], I came across your recent article on [Industry Topic]. It seems you, like many others in the [Industry] industry, are facing the challenge of [Common Pain Point]. At [Your Company], we’ve helped numerous companies overcome this very hurdle. Our [Product/Service] enables you to [Benefit 1], ultimately leading to [Benefit 2]. We’d love to share a case study showcasing how we helped a company similar to yours achieve [Quantifiable Result]. Are you open to a quick call next week? Best, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This email demonstrates that you understand the recipient’s challenges and positions yourself as a solution provider.
## 3. The “Compliment & Curiosity” Approach
This email starts with a genuine compliment and piques the recipient’s interest with a thought-provoking question.
Subject: I Was Impressed with [Something You Admired]
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], I recently came across [Company Name]’s work on [Project/Initiative], and I was thoroughly impressed by [Specific Detail]. It got me thinking, what are your biggest challenges when it comes to [Area Related to the Compliment]? At [Your Company], we specialize in [Your Value Proposition], and we’ve helped companies like yours achieve [Benefit]. Perhaps there’s an opportunity to explore how we could collaborate. Would you be open to a brief 10-minute conversation to discuss your current approach and see if there’s any potential synergy? Looking forward to hearing from you! Best regards, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This cold email template starts on a positive note and uses a question to spark the recipient’s curiosity. It subtly positions your company as a potential collaborator without being overly salesy.
## 4. The “Industry News & Insights” Approach
This email leverages a recent industry development to spark a conversation.
Subject: Did You See the News About [Industry News]?
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], I came across the recent news about [Industry News] and it immediately made me think of your work at [Company Name]. This development could potentially impact [Area of Impact for Recipient]. At [Your Company], we’ve been closely following this trend and have some unique insights we’d love to share. Would you be interested in a quick 15-minute call to discuss how this might affect your business and explore any potential solutions? Best, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This cold email example for b2b sales demonstrates your awareness of industry trends and positions you as a thought leader. It offers valuable insights without being a blatant sales pitch.
## 5. The “Social Proof Powerhouse” Approach
This email highlights the success stories of your existing clients to build trust and credibility.
Subject: How [Client Name] Achieved [Impressive Result] with [Your Company]
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], I noticed you’re the head honcho at [Company Name], a company known for its innovative approach to [Industry]. Here at [Your Company], we share that passion for pushing boundaries. We recently helped a company very similar to yours, [Client Name], achieve a phenomenal [Quantifiable Result] with our [Product/Service]. Their story might resonate with you. Would you be interested in a quick case study on how we made it happen? No pressure, but it might just spark some ideas for your own growth strategy. Best regards, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This email leverages social proof by showcasing the success of a similar company. It positions your company as a trusted partner capable of delivering results.
## 6. The “Resourceful & Relevant” Approach
This email offers a free resource aligned with the recipient’s interests and subtly introduces your company’s solutions.
Subject: Free Guide: Mastering [Industry Skill] in 2024
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], I stumbled upon your insightful recent post on [Industry Topic]. It seems you’re constantly striving to master the art of [Industry Skill]. At [Your Company], we share that dedication to excellence. We created a free, downloadable guide packed with actionable tips on how to [Benefit of Guide]. This guide might be a valuable addition to your toolkit, and who knows, maybe it’ll spark a conversation about how our solutions can further empower your team. Grab your free copy here: [Link to Guide] Best, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This email offers practical value upfront and positions your company as a helpful resource. It subtly introduces your solutions without being pushy.
## 7. The “Humorously Human” Approach (Use with Caution!)
Using humor in professional emails to break the ice and stand out from the crowd is a good move. This cold email example uses this technique as a cornerstone.
Subject: Warning: This Email Might Be Slightly Less Boring Than Usual
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], Let’s face it, most cold emails are about as exciting as watching paint dry. But hey, at least I’m honest! The truth is, I came across [Company Name] and was genuinely impressed by [Specific Detail]. It’s refreshing to see a company doing [Something Unique]. At [Your Company], we also like to think we’re a little different. We specialize in [Your Value Proposition], and we’ve helped companies like yours achieve [Benefit]. Intrigued? If so, let’s chat and see if there’s a spark. Coffee’s on me (virtually, of course). Cheers, [Your Name]
Why it Works (Use with Caution): This approach can be effective for certain audiences, particularly in creative industries. It injects humor and personality, but tread carefully to avoid being unprofessional.
Remember, the key is to tailor your email tone to match your target audience and brand identity.
## 8. The “Event Follow-Up” Approach
This email capitalizes on a recent event (conference, webinar) the recipient might have attended.
Subject: Following Up on [Event Name] — Insights & Collaboration?
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], Hope you enjoyed the [Event Name] last week! I particularly found the session on [Specific Session Topic] insightful. Your company’s focus on [Area of Interest] resonated with me, especially considering [Your Company]’s expertise in [Your Value Proposition]. At [Your Company], we’ve helped companies like yours achieve [Quantifiable Result] through [Solution/Service]. Perhaps there’s an opportunity to connect and explore how we could collaborate. Would you be open to a quick call to discuss your current approach and see if there’s a potential fit? Best regards, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This cold email example leverages a shared experience (the event) to establish rapport and demonstrates your knowledge of the recipient’s interests.
## 9. The “Question Provocation” Approach
This email sparks curiosity by posing a thought-provoking question relevant to the recipient’s industry.
Subject: The Million Dollar Question for [Industry] Professionals in 2024
Body:
Hi [Recipient Name], If you could instantly solve one challenge facing the [Industry] industry today, what would it be? At [Your Company], we believe the answer lies in [Area of Expertise]. Our [Product/Service] empowers companies to [Benefit 1], ultimately leading to [Benefit 2]. We’d love to hear your thoughts on this critical industry question and explore how we can potentially help you overcome your biggest hurdles. Are you up for a quick conversation to brainstorm some solutions? Best, [Your Name]
Why it Works: This approach piques the recipient’s interest by presenting a relevant question. It positions your company as a problem-solver without being overly salesy.
## 10. The “Testimonial Showcase” Approach

## Good Cold Email Examples for an Opener: Breaking the Ice
Similar to cold calling opening lines, your cold email opening line sets the tone for your entire email. Here are a few good cold email examples to capture the recipient’s interest:
## 1. The Personalized Touch
People love to feel seen and heard. A personalized customer engagement approach demonstrates you’ve done your research.
Example: “Hi [Name], I came across your recent article on [topic] in [publication] and found your insights on [specific point] particularly interesting. At [Your Company], we help businesses like [Their Company] achieve [benefit].”

Example: “Have you ever wondered how to [achieve a desired outcome] without [common obstacle] getting in the way? At [Your Company], we’ve helped companies like yours overcome this challenge by [solution].”
## 3. The Shared Connection
Did you find a mutual connection on LinkedIn or attend the same industry event? Leverage that shared experience to build rapport from the get-go.
Example: “Hi [Name], I noticed we both connected on LinkedIn after [event/conference]. I was particularly impressed with your presentation on [topic]. At [Your Company], we specialize in [your solution].”
## Bonus Tips: Craft a Subject Line That Sizzles!
Your subject line is the first impression, so make it count. Here are a few tips to help boost impact of the above-mentioned cold email templates:
- Keep it short and sweet. Aim for under 50 characters.
- Intrigue without being misleading. Spark curiosity, but don’t resort to clickbait tactics.
- Personalize it when possible. Weave in the recipient’s name or company for added relevance.
## Beyond the Examples: Pro Tips for Cold Email Success
Remember, these cold email examples are just a springboard. Here are some additional tips to maximize your outreach efforts:
- Segment Your Audience: Tailor your emails to different segments of your target audience based on their needs and pain points.
- A/B Test Different Subject Lines: Experiment with different subject lines to see what grabs the most attention.
- Optimize for Mobile Devices: Ensure your emails are easy to read on smartphones and tablets.
- Follow up (But Don’t Be a Pest): A well-timed follow-up email can significantly increase your response rate. However, avoid bombarding recipients with constant messages. Here are a few cold email follow up examples you can refer to.

## Frequently Asked Questions or FAQs
## Q: How many cold emails should I send per day?
There’s no magic number, but quality over quantity reigns supreme. Focus on crafting personalized emails rather than a mass blast. Aim for a manageable number that allows for personalization and follow-up.
## Q: What if I don’t get a response?
Don’t be discouraged! Persistence pays off. Consider sending a well-crafted follow-up email a few days after your initial message. However, avoid bombarding recipients with constant emails.
## Q: Is it okay to use these cold email templates for B2B sales?
Absolutely! These cold email examples for B2B sales can be a great starting point. Just remember to personalize them for each recipient. Here are some key elements to personalize:

## Q: What are some b2b cold email best practices that work?
Here are some tips to maximize your cold email outreach:

- A/B Test Different Subject Lines: Experiment with different subject lines for cold emails to see what grabs the most attention.
- Optimize for Mobile Devices: Ensure your emails are easy to read on smartphones and tablets.

## Q: When should I avoid using humor in a cold email template?
While humor can be a disarming tactic, use it with caution. Consider your target audience and brand identity. Avoid humor that could be misconstrued as unprofessional or offensive.
## Q: How can I measure the success of my cold email campaign?
Track your open rates, click-through rates, and response rates to gauge the effectiveness of your cold email campaigns. Use this data to refine your approach and improve your results over time.

## Conclusion
Crafting winning campaigns takes practice, but with the right approach and these valuable cold email examples as inspiration, you can transform your outreach efforts. Remember, a good cold email template can be the spark that ignites a long-lasting and fruitful business relationship.
So, ditch the generic templates and one-size-fits-all messages. Infuse your emails with personality, address your recipient’s specific needs, and showcase your value. text:
Prospecting. It’s the lifeblood of any sales team, the never-ending quest to generate sales leads and convert them into happy customers. But let’s face it; traditional cold email templates can feel a bit…well, stale. Sending another email that just gets lost in someone’s inbox can make you feel like you’re not getting anywhere.
Meet video prospecting, the shiny new technique in the B2B prospecting world. This approach leverages the power of visuals to add a personal touch and break through the noise of overflowing inboxes. But is it all hype, or can it truly dethrone the cold email king? Let’s dive into the video prospecting vs cold email showdown to see which approach reigns supreme.
## Video Prospecting vs Cold Email: Which Works Better for B2B Sales
Let’s see how these two work, compare their effectiveness and help you decide which might best fit your sales goals.
## Round 1: Engagement
First things first, engagement. We all know the struggle — getting your prospect to even open that cold email can feel like winning the lottery. Here’s where prospecting with video throws a knockout punch.
Studies show that emails with video content boast click-through rates that are a whopping 2–3 times higher than emails without. Why the magic? Videos are inherently more engaging. A quick glimpse into a friendly face and a passionate voice instantly grabs attention, making your message stand out from the text-heavy crowd.
Cold email, on the other hand, can often feel impersonal and robotic. Cold email subject lines get ignored, and generic greetings make prospects feel like another number. Don’t get us wrong, cold email still has its place, but when it comes to grabbing attention and sparking engagement, video prospecting takes the crown.
## Round 2: Building Rapport
Sales aren’t about pushing products; they’re about building relationships.
Here’s where video prospecting shines again. A well-crafted video allows you to showcase your personality, enthusiasm, and expertise — all qualities that build trust and rapport with your prospect.
Imagine receiving a cold email that reads, “Our software can revolutionize your workflow!” Yawn, right? Now, picture a short video where a friendly face explains the exact pain points your software addresses, using specific examples and genuine empathy. Suddenly, you’re intrigued!
Dangling modifier alert! Building rapport through video allows you to connect with your prospect on a human level. Thus fostering a sense of trust and connection that’s simply not possible with a text-based approach. This emotional connection is crucial for laying the groundwork for a successful sales conversation. Here are a few video prospecting scripts to help you get started. Also, it is the primary reason why people are shifting to video sales letters from traditional alternatives. Here’s an example by Kenny Morgan,
## Round 3: Budget Wars & Cost Justification
Let’s face it, sales is a budget-conscious game. Every dollar spent needs to deliver a return on investment (or ROI). So, how do AI video prospecting and cold email stack up when it comes to keeping your budget in check?
Traditional email platforms can be surprisingly affordable. Basic plans often start at a few bucks a month, offering features like email automation and basic tracking. However, the real cost might be hidden.
Crafting compelling cold emails that actually get opened and generate responses takes time and effort. Although you can follow cold email best practices. Still, that’ll mean hiring a copywriter or investing in expensive AI email marketing tools. Plus, the sheer volume of emails needed to generate leads can quickly eat away at your budget. Here’s where video prospecting throws a surprising counterpunch.
And while creating high-quality video content can be expensive, there’s a new challenger in the ring: AI video prospecting tools like Potion. These innovative platforms allow you to send targeted video messaging for business at a fraction of the cost of traditional video production.
Here’s the breakdown: Hiring a professional videographer to create a single, polished video message can cost you $1,000 or more. Subscription-based AI personalized video email tools like Potion, on the other hand, costs just $99 per month. Thus allowing you to create dozens, even hundreds, of personalized video messages for a fraction of the cost.
Pro Tip: Don’t be afraid! A simple webcam recording with a genuine message can be just as effective as a Hollywood-style production. Leverage AI video personalization tools for dynamic video creation with elements like the prospect’s name, video background, etc, all without breaking the bank.
By embracing this, you can unlock the power of video, without blowing your budget. Remember, it’s all about delivering a personalized message that resonates with your prospect. With a bit of creativity and the right video messaging software, you can do that without sacrificing your bottom line.
## Round 4: Efficiency — Time is Money, Baby!
Let’s face it, time is a precious commodity for sales reps. So, which approach allows you to reach more prospects and close more deals in less time?
Here’s a secret: crafting compelling video messages can actually be more efficient than writing lengthy cold emails. You can script, record, and edit short prospecting videos in a fraction of the time it takes to personalize and send dozens of emails. Plus, with video, you can deliver a clear, concise message that resonates with your audience.
Now, cold email can be efficient for blasting out a high volume of messages, but the response rate often suffers. Prospecting with video, on the other hand, focuses on quality over quantity. Sure, you might send fewer videos, but the ones you do send are more likely to spark genuine interest and lead to productive conversations.
## Round 5: Customization — One Size Doesn’t Fit All
Sales is all about understanding your audience’s needs, and overcoming common sales objections. Here’s where prospecting with video offers another advantage.
Cold email, by its nature, tends to be a one-size-fits-all approach. You blast out the same generic message to a list of prospects, hoping it resonates with a few. But what if you could tailor your message to each individual?
Video prospecting allows for a level of marketing personalization that cold email simply can’t match. Imagine sending a short video to a prospect, mentioning a recent article they wrote or referencing a specific challenge they face in their industry. This level of personalization instantly grabs attention and shows the prospect you’ve done your homework.
Pro Tip: Take advantage of social media platforms like LinkedIn to gather intel on your prospects. Mention a specific post they shared or a skill they highlighted in their profile. This small touch shows you’re genuinely interested in them, not just another number on your contact list.
## Round 6: Breaking Through the Noise
The modern sales landscape is a crowded battlefield. Everyone’s vying for your prospect’s attention. So, how do you make your message stand out from the constant barrage of emails, calls, and social media notifications?
Cold emailing struggles to break through the noise. Inboxes are overflowing, and your message is likely competing with dozens of others. The result? Ignored emails and a deflated prospecting spirit.
Prospecting with video, on the other hand, is inherently attention-grabbing. A personalized video message in someone’s inbox is a novelty. It stands out, sparks curiosity, and gives you a much better chance of getting your foot in the door.
Pro Tip: Get creative with your thumbnails! A captivating image can be the difference between someone clicking play or letting your message decay unseen.
## Round 7: Building Value, Not Just Hype
Sales conversations shouldn’t be a one-sided pitch fest. They’re about building trust and demonstrating value. Here’s where prospecting with video wins once again.
Cold email often focuses on features and benefits. It tells prospects what your product or service does, but it might not always explain why they should care. This can leave them feeling like just another target on your sales list.
Video allows you to tell a story. You can weave in powerful visuals, customer testimonials, and even data-driven results to showcase the real-world impact of your solution. This content-rich approach positions you as a thought leader and builds trust by demonstrating genuine value.
Pro Tip: Don’t just talk about yourself in your messages. Focus on your prospect’s pain points and challenges. Offer practical tips and insights that demonstrate your expertise and establish you as a valuable resource, not just a salesperson.
## Round 8: Feedback Loop
The best salespeople are constantly learning and adapting their approach. So, how do video prospecting and cold email compare when it comes to gathering valuable feedback?
Cold email feedback can be limited. Sure, you might get a few replies here and there, but most prospects simply hit delete without a word. This lack of feedback makes it difficult to understand what’s resonating and what needs improvement.
Video prospecting opens a two-way communication channel. Platforms like Loom often allow viewers to leave comments and feedback directly on your video. This real-time feedback loop is invaluable for refining your message and tailoring future videos for even greater impact.
Pro Tip: Don’t be afraid to ask for feedback in your messages. A simple question like, “What are your biggest challenges with [insert pain point]?” can spark a conversation and provide valuable insights into your prospect’s needs.
## Round 9: Building Lasting Relationships
Sales isn’t just about closing deals; it’s about building long-term relationships. So, how do video prospecting and cold email stack up when it comes to fostering customer connections?
Cold email often feels transactional. It’s a one-time interaction focused on securing a sale. Once the deal is closed, the email chain often goes cold, leaving the customer feeling like just another number on the spreadsheet.
Prospecting with video allows you to connect with your customers on a personal level. With Zapier, you can even automate follow-up videos to offer post-sale support, share valuable resources, or simply check in and see how they’re doing. This ongoing communication strengthens your relationship and opens the door for future sales opportunities.
Pro Tip: Use testimonials in your prospecting messages. Showcase happy customers raving about your product or service. Social proof is a powerful tool for building trust and demonstrating the value you deliver.
## Round 10: Data Tracking & Analytics
In today’s data-driven world, tracking your outreach efforts is crucial. So, how do video prospecting vs cold email compare when measuring success?
Cold email platforms offer robust tracking features. You can see open rates, click-through rates, and even track if someone downloaded an attachment. However, this data often lacks context. Did they open your email because they were interested, or was it just another piece of digital flotsam they skimmed over?
Prospecting with video, on the other hand, provides deeper insights. Many platforms like Potion track video prospecting metrics like watch time, engagement rates, and even where viewers dropped off. This data allows you to see which parts of your message resonate most and tailor your future videos for even better results.
Pro Tip: Use a clear call to action (CTA) in your messages. This could be a simple request to schedule a call, visit your website, or download a resource. Tracking how many people respond to your CTA (via UTM parameters) clearly indicates how effective your message is.
## The Verdict: A Powerful Partnership, Not a Punch Out
Alright, so the final bell rings. Is prospecting with video the clear winner, ready to banish cold email to the prospecting wasteland? Not quite.
The truth is, both video prospecting and cold email have their strengths and weaknesses. The most effective strategy leverages the power of both approaches.
Think of it like this: Use video prospecting to break the ice and capture attention. Then, follow up with a well-crafted cold email that expands on your video message and provides a clear next step. This one-two punch can be a powerful way to build rapport, showcase value, and ultimately close more deals.
So, ditch the outdated cold email scripts and embrace the power of video. But don’t forget your email skills just yet. The future of sales lies in leveraging both of these B2B prospecting tools to create a winning sales strategy.

## Q: What if I’m not a natural on camera?
Don’t sweat it! The beauty of prospecting with video is that it doesn’t require Hollywood-level production value. A simple, well-lit recording with a genuine message can be incredibly effective. Focus on being yourself, and let your passion for your product or service shine through. Here are a few video prospecting examples to help you get some confidence.
## Q: How long should my video messages be?
Keep it short and sweet! Aim for videos under 2 minutes. People are busy, and their attention spans are short. Get your message across quickly, and leave them wanting more.
## Q: Can I use video prospecting with cold emails?
Absolutely! In fact, combining video prospecting and cold emailing can be a powerful one-two punch. Use your email to introduce yourself and the value proposition, then include a link to your video for a more detailed explanation.

text:
Ever feel like your sales copy is falling flat? Do you craft the perfect message and highlight all the features, but do conversions sputter along? In today’s digital world, people are bombarded with information. Text-heavy sales letters can easily get lost in this digital shuffle.
Meet the video sales letter (or VSL) — a dynamic marketing tool shaking up the sales game. It is a short, persuasive video that acts like a digital salesperson, showcasing your product or service and driving viewers toward a purchase.
So, Why use video sales letters for sales? Here’s the breakdown: VSLs are one of the most powerful AI email marketing tools that blend storytelling with persuasive messaging. All wrapped up in a captivating video format. Think of it as your most charismatic salesperson, on-demand, ready to pitch your product or service 24/7. Let’s uncover a few VSL benefits to get the hang of it.
## 10 Benefits of Video Sales Letters (VSL)
Forget static text and one-dimensional pitches. Video sales letters (VSLs) are the secret weapon your sales strategy craves. But what makes them so effective? Let’s explore various reasons why you should use VSLs for sales.
## 1. Captivate Attention in a FOMO-Fueled World
Let’s face it, people are bombarded with text. Emails, social media posts, blog articles — it’s information overload! A VSL cuts through the clutter. People are 8 times more likely to engage with video content than text, and for good reason. Videos are inherently captivating. They tap into our visual cortex, keeping viewers glued to the screen.
Imagine this: a prospect stumbles upon your landing page. They see a wall of text. Meh. But then they spot a play button — a video promising to solve their problems. Intrigued, they click. They’re hooked. That’s the power of VSLs — they grab and hold attention hostage, giving your sales message a fighting chance.
Example: Feeling overwhelmed by the complexities of accounting software? A VSL can showcase a user navigating the software with ease. Thus highlighting its features and benefits clearly, concisely, and engagingly.
## 2. It’s All About That Human Touch
With the ChatGPT era, sales pitches can feel impersonal and robotic. Text on a page can’t convey the warmth of a smile or the sincerity in your voice. VSLs bridge that gap. By putting a face to the name (yours, or a friendly spokesperson), you build trust and rapport with viewers.
You can connect with them emotionally, sharing stories, anecdotes, and resonating experiences.
This emotional connection is crucial for driving sales. People buy from people they like and trust. On this note, VSLs allow you to forge that connection in a way text simply can’t.
Example: A VSL for a productivity app can feature the CEO sharing his own struggles with time management before showcasing how his app transformed his life. This vulnerability creates a connection with viewers, making them more receptive to the app’s benefits.
## 3. Show, Don’t Tell
Ever heard the saying, “a picture is worth a thousand words”? Well, a video is worth a million! VSLs allow you to showcase your product or service in action. This is especially powerful for complex products that require explanation.
With a VSL, you can conduct live demos, provide walkthroughs, and illustrate how your offering solves real-world problems. It’s the ultimate “show, don’t tell” strategy, leaving a far more lasting impression than text descriptions ever could.
Example: Selling fitness equipment? A VSL can showcase different exercises being performed with the equipment. Thus allowing viewers to visualize how it can be used to achieve their fitness goals.
## 4. Leverage Social Proof
Testimonials are a tried-and-true sales tactic, but VSLs take them to the next level. Imagine replacing a static text quote with a video testimonial.
Now, viewers see a real person, sharing their positive experience with genuine enthusiasm. It’s social proof on steroids! These video testimonials add credibility and authenticity to your video messaging for business. Thus making viewers likelier to believe in the value you offer.
Example: A VSL for a CRM software can feature real clients singing its praises. Seeing happy customers using the product successfully is a powerful persuasion tool.
## 5. Video Sparks Action
So, you’ve captivated attention, built trust, showcased your product, and leveraged social proof. Now what? You need to drive action, and VSLs excel at it. With a clear call to action (or CTA) at the end of your video — whether it’s visiting a website, signing up for a free trial, or making a purchase — you nudge viewers towards the next step in the sales funnel.
Unlike traditional sales letters where CTAs can feel like an afterthought. VSLs seamlessly integrate the CTA into the narrative, making it a natural progression from the information presented.
Here’s the magic: VSLs allow you to get creative with your CTAs. You can add a clickable button alongside the video itself. Thereby eliminating the need for viewers to navigate elsewhere. Also, you can offer limited-time discounts exclusive to VSL viewers, creating a sense of urgency and encouraging immediate action.
Example: Imagine a video sales letter funnel for a language learning app. At the end, the instructor could offer a free bonus lesson for viewers who click the “Get Started Today” button within the video itself. This eliminates friction and makes enrolling in the app a quick and easy decision.
## 6. Cater to Different Learning Styles
People absorb information in different ways. Some folks are visual learners, thriving on images and demonstrations. Others prefer auditory learning, responding best to the spoken word. And then there are the kinesthetic learners, who connect best through seeing things done.
The beauty of VSLs? They cater to all these styles! With visuals, audio, and demonstrations, VSLs ensure your message resonates with a wider audience.
Example: A VSL for a productivity course can incorporate screen recordings, animations, and the instructor explaining the concepts. This caters to visual, auditory, and kinesthetic learners, maximizing the message's impact.
## 7. Measurable and Adaptable
Unlike text sales letters, VSLs offer valuable data and insights. Most video sales letter platforms provide analytics like watch time, engagement rates, and CTAs clicked. This goldmine of information allows you to see what’s working and what’s not. Did viewers drop off halfway through? Maybe you need to tighten up the intro. Did a specific product demo generate a surge in clicks? Double down on that section! By analyzing VSL performance, you can continually refine your message and optimize your sales pitch for maximum impact.
Example: Imagine a VSL for a weight loss program. Analytics reveal viewers clicking away right after a section on meal prepping. This might indicate a need to simplify the meal prepping process or showcase alternative strategies.
## 8. Perfect for the Mobile Age
Let’s face it, people are glued to their smartphones. In fact, mobile video consumption is on the rise. VSLs capitalize on this trend perfectly. They’re easily digestible on any device, allowing viewers to consume your sales message wherever they are, whenever they have a spare moment.
This accessibility is a huge advantage. Removing barriers to entry and making your product or service instantly discoverable.
Example: A VSL for a travel agency can showcase stunning vacation destinations through captivating mobile-friendly videos. This allows potential clients to browse travel options on their commute or during breaks, maximizing convenience and sparking wanderlust.
## 9. Breathe Personality into Your Brand
Let’s be honest, traditional sales copy can feel stuffy and corporate. It lacks the warmth and personality that connects with customers on a deeper level.
VSLs, however, are a breath of fresh air! They allow you to showcase the human side of your brand. You can inject your personality, humor, and enthusiasm into the video. Thus making your brand relatable and memorable.
Example: A VSL for a dog walking service can feature the owner walking adorable pups with genuine love and care. This injects personality into the brand and demonstrates the company’s passion for animals.
## 10. Break Down Complex Ideas
Sometimes, explaining your product or service can feel like deciphering rocket science. Features can get bogged down in technical jargon, confusing potential customers. For this, video sales letters offer a powerful solution.
With clear visuals, demonstrations, and easy-to-understand language, VSLs can break down complex ideas into digestible chunks. This makes it easier for viewers to grasp your value and how your product solves their problems.
Example: A VSL for financial planning services can use animations and metaphors to explain complex investment concepts like compound interest. This visual approach simplifies the message and makes financial planning seem less intimidating.
So there you have it—10 rock-solid reasons to use VSLs for sales. They capture attention, build trust, showcase your offering, boost remote selling, and do so much more! In today’s fast-paced digital world, VSLs offer a unique opportunity to connect with your audience, simplify your message, and ultimately skyrocket your sales. So, don’t be a wallflower in the crowded marketplace. Embrace the power of video storytelling in marketing and unleash the sales potential of VSLs!
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: Are VSLs expensive to produce?
Not necessarily! While high-quality productions are impressive, you can create effective VSLs using simple video sales letter software like Potion, and your desktop. The key lies in a compelling script, good lighting, and clear audio.
## Q: I’m not a professional videographer. Can I still create effective VSLs?
Absolutely! While high-quality productions are impressive, you don’t need fancy equipment to create impactful VSLs. Leverage your smartphone and editing software like iMovie or Windows Movie Maker. Focus on a clear message, good lighting, and crisp audio. Authenticity often trumps Hollywood-style productions.
## Q: How often should I update my VSL?
There’s no hard and fast rule, but consider refreshing your VSL every 6 months to a year. This keeps the content fresh and ensures you’re addressing any pain points or trends that might have emerged since its creation.
## Q: Can I use video sales letter for any industry?
Absolutely! VSLs are a versatile tool that can be used to sell anything from software to clothing to consulting services.
## Q: Can I use a script for my VSL?
Absolutely! A well-crafted Video sales letter script ensures your message is clear, concise, and flows smoothly. However, don’t sound robotic. Practice your delivery beforehand to inject a natural conversational tone. Here are few video sales letter examples for some inspiration.
## Q: Where should I host my VSL?
Many options exist! Popular choices include Potion, YouTube, Vimeo, or directly embedding the video on your website landing page.
## Conclusion
There you have it, folks! We’ve discussed why use video sales letters for your next campaign. In a world overflowing with text, VSLs offer a dynamic and engaging way to connect with your audience, showcase your value proposition, and ultimately drive sales.
So, are you ready to ditch the static and embrace the power of video? Don’t wait any longer! Fire up your camera, unleash your creativity, and craft a VSL that will leave your viewers wanting more. But remember, creating a compelling VSL doesn’t have to be a daunting task.

With its intuitive interface, AI personalization, and end-to-end support, Potion empowers anyone to craft professional-looking personalized video marketing campaigns.

text:
You’ve closed the deal and a shiny new customer is eager to jump on board. But hold on to your celebratory hats — the real work of building a successful, long-term relationship begins now, with the client onboarding process.
Think of onboarding as that crucial first impression, the gateway to a thriving client partnership. Here’s the thing: a haphazard onboarding experience can leave your customer feeling confused, frustrated, and ready to jump ship. Yikes! On the other hand, a good client onboarding process is your secret to success — a chance to establish trust, set expectations, and lay the groundwork for a smooth, collaborative journey.
This guide equips you with what is client onboarding, its importance, steps involved, etc. Alongside sharing tips, best practices & examples to land a better understanding of the subject. These strategies will help to conquer onboarding chaos and answer that bugging question of how to improve customer satisfaction.
## What is Client Onboarding Meaning?
Alright, so we’ve all heard how amazing client onboarding process can be, but let’s take a step back for a second. What exactly is client onboarding, anyway?
Imagine you just joined a fancy gym. They don’t just throw you a key card and say, “Good luck navigating the maze of squat racks, dumbells and weight machines!” A good gym will have a new member orientation — that’s essentially client onboarding in action.
Client onboarding is the process of welcoming new clients into your business and ensuring they have everything they need to hit the ground running with your service. It’s like rolling out the red carpet and showing them the VIP ropes. This includes things like:
- Setting expectations: Making sure everyone’s on the same page about goals, timelines, and communication styles.
- Gathering information: Understanding their specific needs and challenges to tailor your approach accordingly.
- Providing training: Equipping them with the knowledge and tools to get the most out of your service.
- Establishing clear communication channels: Building a system for smooth back-and-forth throughout the project.
By investing time and effort into client onboarding, you’re not just setting the stage for a successful project. You’re laying the groundwork for a long-lasting, happy client communication. Think of it as that initial gym orientation — a little upfront effort can lead to a loyal gym member (or customer) for years to come!
## Why Client Onboarding is Important
So, What does client onboarding do? Why should you invest time and effort in crafting a stellar client onboarding process? Here are just a few reasons:
- Reduced churn: A precise and efficient onboarding experience minimizes confusion and frustration. Thus, leaving clients feeling confident and valued. Know this: happy clients stick around longer!
- Boosted efficiency: Streamlined onboarding processes save you and your team precious time. No more scrambling to answer basic questions — everything a client needs is readily available.
- Stronger relationships: Clear communication and well-defined expectations promote a more open and collaborative client relationship from the start.
- Faster project kick-off: With all the necessary information and tools at their fingertips, clients can dive into projects with confidence, accelerating progress.
## 6 Steps to a Winning Client Onboarding Process
So, let’s break down the 6-step client onboarding process step by step.
## Step 1: Setting Expectations & Gathering Intel
First impressions matter. A warm welcome email sets the tone for the entire journey. Don’t just send a generic “thanks for signing on” message. Personalize it! Mention a specific detail from your sales conversation, highlight their company’s goals, and express your enthusiasm to work together.
Video personalization tools like Potion can help you do this. Simply record a single video message, add names of your prospects, and their AI will send a personalized welcome video on each signup. All this, without doing anything extra!
Further, this is also prime time to gather crucial intel. Schedule a kick-off call to delve deeper into their needs and expectations. Here are some pro tips:
- Don’t wing it! Prepare an agenda beforehand and circulate it to the customer.
- Ask open-ended questions to understand their pain points and desired outcomes truly.
- Be an active listener. Pay close attention to their responses and use this information to tailor your approach.
By the end of this call, you should have a clear roadmap for the project, including deadlines, communication preferences, and success metrics. This sets realistic expectations for both sides and avoids future misunderstandings.
## Step 2: Contract Clarity & Onboarding Documents
Contracts aren’t thrilling, but they’re essential for a smooth customer relationship. Don’t get bogged down in legalese, though. Present a concise contract outlining the scope of work, pricing structure, and payment terms. Avoid jargon and ensure it’s easily understandable.
This step also involves sending essential onboarding documents. This could include a project timeline, style guide (if applicable), and access information for project management tools. Having everything organized upfront saves time and keeps everyone on the same page.
Pro Tips:
- Use a client portal: Consider using a client portal to house all these documents in a central, easily accessible location.
- Define key terms: If there are any industry-specific terms or technical jargon you can’t avoid, include a clear definition within the contract itself or a separate glossary.
- Open communication: Encourage your customer to ask questions and seek clarification on any points they find confusing.
- Payment terms: Clearly state the payment schedule, including milestones for payment if applicable, accepted payment methods, and late payment fees (if any).
## Step 3: Teamwork Makes the Dream Work
Now it’s time to introduce the all-star team working on the client’s project. Briefly introduce each team member, highlighting their expertise and role in the project.
This is also the time to establish preferred communication channels. Will it be email, project management software, or a combination? Clearly outline how the customer can reach the team and set expectations for response times.
Collaboration is key. Invest in user-friendly project management tools that allow for seamless communication, file sharing, and task tracking. These tools keep everyone on the same page and ensure a smooth workflow. Here are some best practices you could follow:
- Go beyond names and titles. While names and titles are important, add a sentence or two highlighting each team member’s relevant expertise and how it relates to the client’s project.
- Document communication preferences. Include a summary of the agreed-upon communication channels and response times in the onboarding documents for easy reference.
- Put a face to the name. Include headshots or photos of the team members introducing them. This personalizes the experience and helps the customer build rapport.
- Keep it concise. Aim for a brief introduction for each team member, avoid lengthy biographies that might overwhelm the client.
- Designate a point of contact. While the client may interact with various team members, identify a single point of contact to centralize communication and streamline the process.
## Step 4: Client Education & Training
Don’t assume the client knows everything about your service or deliverable. Invest time in customer education. This could involve creating video tutorials, hosting training sessions, or providing clear documentation.
The goal is to empower the customer to understand the process and feel confident using the final product or service. Here are some ways to make client education engaging:
- Keep it concise and focused. Don’t overwhelm them with information overload.
- Train the client on the tool. Don’t assume the customer is familiar with the chosen software. Offer a brief training session to ensure they understand how to access features like file sharing, task tracking, and communication tools within the platform.
- Tailor the training to their specific needs. Don’t provide generic information that might not be relevant.
- Make it interactive. Encourage questions and open communication to address any concerns.
By effectively educating the client, you not only ensure they get the most out of your service but also build trust and establish yourself as a valuable partner.
## Step 5: Gathering Insights & Course Correction
Communication is a two-way street. Don’t wait until the project is finished to hear from the client. Schedule regular check-in calls or surveys to gather feedback throughout the process.
This feedback is gold! It allows you to identify any roadblocks early on, course-correct if needed, and ensure the project stays aligned with the client’s goals. Here are some client onboarding tips for effective feedback sessions:
- Ask specific questions. Don’t rely on vague responses like “everything is good.”
- Actively listen to their concerns. Acknowledge their feedback and demonstrate your willingness to adapt.
- Be transparent. If there are any unexpected challenges or delays, communicate them openly and proactively.
Pro Tip: Don’t just gather feedback, use it! Implement the client’s suggestions whenever possible This shows them you value their input and builds trust in the process.
## Step 6: Launch & Beyond
The project is complete! Time to celebrate! A quick email or personalized AI video message acknowledging their achievement and expressing your appreciation goes a long way. And there’s no better way to personalize it with Potion.
But the relationship doesn’t end there. The final step in this client onboarding process is about fostering long-term engagement. Here are some client onboarding best practices to keep the momentum going:
- Schedule a post-launch review call. Discuss the project’s success, address any lingering questions, and gather final feedback.
- Offer ongoing support. Let them know you’re available to answer questions or provide assistance even after the project is complete.
- Stay connected. Send periodic newsletters, industry updates, or even birthday wishes to keep the communication flowing and build rapport.
By implementing this 6-step client onboarding process step by step, you can transform new customers from initial excitement to long-term partners. Remember, a well-onboarded client becomes a loyal client, leading to a thriving and sustainable business for you.
## Client Onboarding Types
Not all customers are created equal; the same goes for onboarding approaches! While our 6-step process serves as a solid foundation, the delivery method can vary depending on your client’s needs and your resources. Let’s dive into the three main client onboarding types: virtual, in-person, and the ever-adaptable hybrid approach.
## 1. Virtual Onboarding: Tech-Savvy & Streamlined
Perfect for geographically dispersed clients or those who prefer a self-paced learning experience, virtual onboarding reigns supreme in the digital age. Here’s how to make it a virtual slam dunk:
Pro Tips:
- Master the art of the asynchronous call. Schedule pre-recorded video introductions or explainer sessions customers can access at their convenience. This can be easily achieved with services like Potion, allowing you to record personalized customer interactions and share them with a secure link.
- Embrace online collaboration tools. Utilize project management platforms and screen-sharing software to keep everyone connected and on the same page.
- Don’t underestimate the power of documentation. Create clear, concise online guides, FAQs, and tutorials to empower clients to learn independently.
## 2. In-Person Onboarding: The High-Touch Advantage
For clients who crave a more personal touch, in-person onboarding offers an unbeatable opportunity to build rapport and establish trust. Here are some tips to ensure a face-to-face win:
Pro Tips:
- Plan engaging workshops or interactive sessions. Go beyond dry lectures and incorporate activities to keep clients engaged and actively participating.
- Utilize the power of visual aids. Whiteboards, flip charts, and even creative props can help solidify concepts and cater to different learning styles.
- Don’t forget the post-meeting follow-up. Send a recap email with key takeaways, action items, and resources to keep the momentum going after the in-person session.
## 3. Hybrid Onboarding: The Best of Both Worlds
The ever-evolving business landscape demands flexibility. Hybrid onboarding seamlessly blends virtual and in-person elements, catering to a wider range of client preferences. Here’s how to create a harmonious hybrid experience:
Pro Tips:
- Start with a virtual kick-off call (Step 1). This sets the stage for the project and allows for efficient information exchange regardless of location.
- Schedule strategic in-person meetings. Consider reserving face-to-face time for brainstorming sessions or key decision-making moments that benefit from real-time interaction.
- Leverage technology to bridge the gap. Utilize video conferencing tools to facilitate virtual participation in workshops or training sessions that might have some remote attendees.
Remember, the right client onboarding type depends on your specific circumstances. Consider your budget, the client’s location and preferences, and the complexity of the project. By understanding these options and their strengths, you can choose the onboarding champion that will set your client relationship up for long-term success!
## Client Onboarding Examples: Inspiration in Action!
So, you’ve mastered the step-by-step client onboarding process — high fives all around! But how does it translate into real-world scenarios? Let’s dive into some client onboarding examples to spark your creativity and get those onboarding juices flowing!
## Example 1: The Design Duo & The Dream Website
Imagine Sarah, a phenomenal web designer, lands a new customer, John, who owns a local bakery. John’s current website is, well, let’s just say it’s a bit stale. During the kick-off call (Step 1), Sarah takes the time to understand John’s vision for a website that captures the warmth and mouthwatering appeal of his baked goods.
Step 2: Contract time! Sarah keeps it clear and concise, outlining the website’s design elements, functionalities, and timeline. She also includes a creative brief co-created with John to ensure they’re on the same page about the website’s look and feel.
Step 3: Meet the team! Sarah introduces John to her design partner, Mark, a whiz with user experience (UX) design. They establish email as their primary communication channel and set up a project management tool for John to track progress.
Step 4: Education is key! Knowing John isn’t super tech-savvy, Sarah creates a short video tutorial explaining how to navigate the project management tool and upload content. She also provides a cheat sheet summarizing website maintenance basics.
Step 5: Feedback Fiesta! Sarah schedules regular check-in calls throughout the design process to gather John’s input on design drafts. She actively listens to his suggestions and makes tweaks where needed.
Step 6: Launch & Beyond! John’s new website is a showstopper! Sarah sends a celebratory video messaging using Potion highlighting the bakery’s delicious offerings and encourages John to reach out if he has any questions (Step 6). A few weeks later, Sarah followed up with another quick video email to see how John managed the website and offered ongoing support as needed.
## Example 2: The Marketing Marvel & The Social Media Takeover
Now, let’s meet Emily, a social media marketing guru. She’s just landed a client, David, who runs a fitness apparel company. David wants to ramp up his social media presence and attract a younger demographic.
Step 1: During their kick-off call, Emily gets a feel for David’s brand voice and target audience. She also learns about his content creation capabilities.
Step 2: Contract central! The contract outlines the social media platforms Emily will manage, the frequency of content posting, and the content creation strategy (Emily creating vs. David providing content).
Step 3: Teamwork makes the dream work! Emily introduces David to her social media strategist, Alex, who will be crafting the content calendar. They decide on a mix of email and project management tool communication for seamless collaboration.
Step 4: Knowledge is power! Emily knows David isn’t familiar with social media analytics. She creates a training session explaining key customer onboarding metrics like engagement rates and follower growth, empowering David to understand the impact of their social media strategy.
Step 5 & 6: Feedback Fiesta & Launch & Beyond! Emily incorporates David’s feedback throughout the campaign and keeps him updated on the progress with regular reports. After a successful launch, Emily schedules a post-launch review to discuss the campaign’s performance and brainstorm future content ideas. She also sends David a monthly newsletter with industry trends and social media best practices to keep him informed.
These are just a couple of client onboarding examples, but they showcase the power of this 6-step process. Remember, personalize it to your specific industry and client needs. By following these guidelines and adding your own creative flair. You can successfully springboard for long-term client relationships!
## FAQs or Frequently Asked Questions
## Q: How long should the client onboarding process take?
The duration varies depending on the project complexity. A simple project might take a week, while a larger one could take several weeks. The key is to be efficient without compromising thoroughness.
## Q: What if the client doesn’t respond to my emails or calls?
Be persistent but polite. Follow up with a second email or call after a reasonable timeframe. Sometimes, inboxes get flooded, or schedules get hectic.
## Q: Can this client onboarding process be adapted for different industries?
Absolutely! While the core principles remain the same, you can customize the specific steps to fit the unique needs of your industry and clients.
## Q: What if the expectations seem unrealistic during the kick-off call?
Transparency is key. Explain your project timeline and limitations politely but firmly. Offer alternative solutions or adjustments that might better suit their needs and budget.
## Q: What documents are essential for the onboarding paperwork?
If confidentiality is a concern, consider including a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) in addition to the contract. A creative brief or project scope document can also help solidify the agreed-upon deliverables.
## Q: How can I encourage customer participation in training sessions?
Using AI in customer retention, you can offer recordings of the sessions for later reference. Provide incentives like early access to resources or bonus materials for attending. Tailor the training to address their specific questions and concerns raised during the onboarding process.
## Q: What if we get negative feedback during a check-in?
Don’t get defensive! Thank them for their honesty and express your commitment to resolving the issue. Work collaboratively with them to find a solution that addresses their concerns.
## Q: How often should I reach out to the client after launch?
There’s no one-size-fits-all answer. Strike a balance between staying connected and avoiding being overly intrusive. A monthly email update or quarterly check-in call can be a good starting point.
## Q: What are some additional ways to foster long-term customer engagement?
Offer exclusive discounts or early access to new services. Invite them to industry events or webinars you’re hosting. Showcase their success story in a case study or client testimonial. By going the extra mile, you demonstrate your commitment to their long-term success.
Remember, the goal is to build trust and establish yourself as a valuable asset, not just a one-time service provider. By addressing these FAQs and implementing the 6-step client onboarding process effectively, you can create a foundation for a thriving client relationship.
## Conclusion
The client onboarding process isn’t just a box to tick; it’s the foundation for a thriving client relationship. Implementing a streamlined yet thorough approach can transform new clients from initial sign-up to enthusiastic brand advocates.
Remember, happy clients are loyal clients, and loyal clients are the backbone of any successful business.
So, don’t let creating client onboarding videos become an afterthought. Invest the time and effort to get it right, and reap the rewards of long-term partnerships and a flourishing business.
